Cultivation Level 18 — Grand Exorcism

You invoke the full authority of departure, rightful hosting, burial, and spiritual boundary.

Action  
Area: 60-foot Emanation  
Cost: 10 Resonance

Choose any number of allies, Hosts, Intruders, Restless Dead, fiends, demons, undead spirits, possessions, curse Anchors, and hostile spirit Assets in the area. Each hostile chosen creature makes a Charisma saving throw.

Failed Save

The target takes 10d10 Radiant or Psychic damage and suffers the result appropriate to its nature:

- Possessing Intruder: It is forced out of every Host in the area, cannot repossess those Hosts for the scene, and is either manifested in a legal space or sealed in a visible spiritual outline. If its Source CL is at least 5 lower than yours and it has no independent legal existence on the plane, it is expelled for the scene.
- Extraplanar Spirit, Fiend, or Demon: If unanchored and of lower Source CL, it is expelled to its home plane. If anchored, its sustaining Anchor becomes revealed and it is Incapacitated until the end of its next turn.
- Restless Dead or Native Ghost: Choose to destroy a purely hostile residual imprint, send a willing soul onward, or reduce a coherent unwilling soul to 0 Hit Points without destroying it. A coherent soul with unfinished obligations may instead reveal the required funerary or narrative resolution.
- Undead Body or Corpse-Spirit: It is destroyed if reduced to 50 Hit Points or fewer by this activation. A unique equal- or higher-authority undead uses its own destruction and recovery rules.
- Curse or Spiritual Contamination: End one ordinary effect on each willing Host. Against equal or higher authority, suppress it for the scene and reveal its Source, Anchor, or recovery condition.
- Hostile Spirit Asset or Anchor: It takes double damage from the activation. If destroyed, the underlying full soul is not automatically destroyed unless the Asset’s Source Rule expressly makes them the same.

Successful Save

The target takes half damage, becomes Resonance Marked by you, and suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.

Allied Purification

Each willing ally or Host chosen in the Emanation may immediately:

- End one ordinary Charmed or Frightened condition.
- Repeat one save against possession, curse, dream intrusion, memory alteration, or Spiritual Affliction or Heart Demon influence with Advantage.
- Return a displaced soul to its body if both are in the Emanation and no equal- or higher-authority seal prevents return.
- Suppress one equal- or higher-authority spiritual affliction until the end of the scene, provided you succeed on a Cultivation Check against its save DC.

High-Authority Limits

Grand Exorcism does not automatically destroy a deity, erase a Secret Law, annul a willing Soul Anchor, break a lawful Spirit Companion bond, reverse reincarnation, or release a soul held by higher Source CL without a contest and the relevant recovery procedure. It must still expose useful information or create a temporary opening when it cannot produce complete removal.

Domain Integration

When used inside your Domain Manifestation, Grand Exorcism treats every ordinary possession link, invisible hostile spirit, and lower-Source-CL curse Anchor in the Domain as perceived. You may originate the Emanation from yourself or your Soul Fragment.

You manifest the spiritual law of a bell, chime, clap, drum, sutra, sword-ring, hand seal, or other tradition-appropriate purification sound.

Action  
Area: 30-foot Emanation  
Cost: 5 Resonance

Choose any number of creatures, spiritual Assets, haunted objects, and curse Anchors in the area. A hostile Intruder, Restless Dead, fiend, demon, undead spirit, or possessing entity makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save: It takes 6d8 Radiant or Psychic damage, chosen for each activation, becomes Resonance Marked by you, and is Frightened of you until the end of your next turn.

Successful Save: It takes half damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

A willing Host or ally in the area may instead receive one purification benefit:

- End one ordinary Frightened or Charmed condition caused by a spirit, curse, possession, or Heart Demon.
- Repeat one saving throw against possession, dream intrusion, memory alteration, or spiritual contamination with Advantage.
- Suppress one ordinary curse or spiritual contamination until the start of your next turn.

Resonant Exposure

Bell Against the Anchor

Instead of damaging a creature, you may target one spiritual Anchor or curse Anchor you can perceive in the area. Make a Cultivation Attack against its AC or a Cultivation Check against its save DC. On success, deal 6d8 Force or Radiant damage to the Anchor, or reduce the sustaining effect’s Source CL by 2 until the end of your next turn if it has no Hit Point profile. This cannot reduce Source CL below 1 and does not permanently alter the originating cultivator. Cultivation Level 14 — Seal of Binding

You create an exorcist seal that restrains a designated spiritual threat and exposes its removal procedure.

Action  
Range: 30 feet  
Cost: 6 Resonance  
Duration: The scene  
Concentration: No

Choose one Intruder, Restless Dead, fiend, demon, incorporeal undead, curse Source, hostile spirit Asset, or possessed creature you perceive. The target makes a Charisma saving throw.

Failed Save

Create a Binding Seal Anchor in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target or attach it visibly to the Host, object, corpse, threshold, or ground.

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC.
- Hit Points: 5 × Proficiency Bonus.
- Saving Throws: Uses your Wisdom saving throw bonus.
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL.
- Immunities: Poison, Disease, Psychic damage, and ordinary bodily conditions.

While the Anchor remains:

- The target is Restrained.
- It cannot become invisible, incorporeal, or enter a Host unless the new state is an inherent passive quality that cannot be suppressed.
- It cannot teleport, cross planar boundaries, or move more than 30 feet from the Anchor.
- A possessing Intruder is forced out of its Host and remains adjacent to the Host or Anchor if it lacks a legal body.
- The target repeats the Charisma saving throw at the end of each of its turns. Three total successful repeat saves destroy the Anchor and end the effect. These successes need not be consecutive.

Successful Initial Save

The target is Restrained until the start of your next turn, becomes Resonance Marked by you, and you learn one of the following if it has one:

- Its immediate escape condition.
- Its sustaining Anchor category.
- Its invitation or possession route.
- The true name, title, taboo, burial need, payment, or unfinished obligation most relevant to peaceful resolution.

Breaking or Resolving the Seal

A creature can attack the Anchor if it can perceive and affect spiritual objects. Destroying it ends the binding but does not harm the target.

You, the Host, or an ally can also end the binding by completing one exposed lawful resolution. The resolution must be one of the following: Revoke Invitation by the willing Host or the authority that granted it; Break or Suppress the Sustaining Anchor through its printed profile; Return Remains or Complete Burial when that need was diagnosed; Pay the Recorded Restitution or Offering; Speak the Recorded True Name or Release Formula when a Source Rule grants it that function; Accept Surrender and Provide a Legal Departure Route; or complete Spiritual Exorcism or another printed removal procedure. A resolution cannot be invented after the seal is applied merely to deny the feature.

Soul Splitting Expression — Seal Warden

While Soul Splitting is active and a Binding Seal Anchor exists, use Seal Warden as your Subpath Expression. Move the Soul Fragment to a legal space adjacent to the Anchor. Until the start of your next turn, the Anchor has Resistance to all damage and the sealed target has Disadvantage on its next repeat saving throw.

Cultivation Level 14 — Borrowed Ending

You can detach a consequence from the moment it was supposed to occur.

Reaction  
You can use this when  You or an ally within 30 feet would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, fail a death saving throw, become Charmed or Frightened, become possessed, suffer a curse, lose a memory, have identity altered, suffer a permanent wound, or fail a Cultivation Check with an immediate consequence  
Cost: 6 Resonance and 1 Fate Tension

Create a Borrowed Ending and delay the triggering consequence until the end of the target’s next turn.

During the delay:

- The target remains at a minimum of 1 Hit Point if the trigger was reduction to 0 Hit Points.
- A failed death saving throw is not recorded yet.
- A condition, possession, curse, memory wound, identity wound, or permanent injury has not yet taken hold, though signs of it are visible.
- The target has one meaningful opportunity to alter the branch through healing, escape, exorcism, surrender, counter-technique, bargain, destroying an Anchor, accepting another cost, or another action capable of changing the cause.

At the end of the target’s next turn:

- If the cause was legally removed or the situation genuinely changed, the Borrowed Ending dissolves.
- If nothing changed, the original consequence occurs.
- If the source is equal or higher authority, a successful Cultivation Check is required for complete dissolution. On failure, reduce the consequence’s severity by one step where logically possible or delay it until the end of the scene.

Ending Token

The Borrowed Ending appears as a visible spiritual token attached to the target: a black thread, unfinished sentence, inverted hourglass, unfallen drop of blood, severed shadow, or another omen.

It is a Cultivation Asset with:

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 6 × Proficiency Bonus
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
- Immunities: Poison, Psychic, and ordinary bodily conditions

Destroying the token by hostile action causes the original consequence to occur immediately unless the destructive effect expressly consumes or rewrites fate. A willing equal- or higher-authority healer, exorcist, fate cultivator, or source-specific countermeasure may instead target the token to dissolve it.

No Repeated Borrowing

A creature cannot carry more than one Borrowed Ending from you at a time. You cannot use Borrowed Ending on the same underlying consequence twice unless a distinct Source Rule recreated it after genuine resolution.

Cultivation Level 10 — Nudge Consequence

You can apply force to a probability already in motion.

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature you can see within 60 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, saving throw, death saving throw, or Cultivation Check  
Cost: 4 Resonance

Before the final outcome is declared, add or subtract 1d8 from the triggering roll. If the target is unwilling and you worsen its result, it makes a Charisma saving throw.

- Failed Save: Apply the full modifier.
- Successful Save: Apply only 1d4, and the target suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.

After the result resolves, gain 1 Fate Tension if the modifier changed success to failure or failure to success.

Consequence Echo

When Nudge Consequence changes an outcome involving a major enemy, a death saving throw, a Secret Law, divine agent, artifact, tribulation, fate-protected creature, breakthrough, permanent injury, or identity-scale effect, choose one:

- gain 1 additional Fate Tension;
- accept one Named Echo from the fixed Named Echo table and state it immediately.

A Named Echo is a coherent future complication connected to the intervention, such as:

- the spared enemy recognizes your fate signature;
- a broken weapon fails at a later dramatic moment;
- the healing that succeeded creates a visible omen;
- a diverted curse seeks a new route;
- an authority notices the altered probability;
- the beneficiary owes a spiritual favor.

A Named Echo cannot negate the changed outcome retroactively. Resolving or willingly accepting it removes 1 Fate Tension.

Refuse Certainty

Once per scene, when a creature within 60 feet would automatically succeed or fail because of an ordinary lower-Source-CL feature, spend 2 additional Resonance. Require that creature to roll normally instead. Equal or higher authority uses a Cultivation Check contest.

Cultivation Level 3 — Omen Glimpse

You can read one outcome before it becomes attached to an action.

Prepare an Omen

After at least 1 minute observing meaningful signs—cards, bones, stars, smoke, dreams, spirit behavior, battlefield movement, blood patterns, falling leaves, or another legal omen medium defined in the Normalized Execution Notes—spend 1 Resonance and roll one d20. Record the result as your Omen die.

- You can hold only one Omen die.
- Preparing a new one replaces the old one.
- An Omen die lasts until used, until the current scene ends, or until circumstances change so completely that the divination’s subject no longer exists.
- If a scene begins without preparation because you were genuinely surprised, you may prepare an Omen as a Bonus Action by spending 2 Resonance and gaining 1 Fate Tension.

Invoke the Omen

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature you can see within 60 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, saving throw, death saving throw, or Cultivation Check  
Cost: 1 Resonance

Before the final outcome is declared, replace the d20 with your Omen die. The Omen die is then expended.

If the target is unwilling and the replacement would make its result worse, it may make a Charisma saving throw.

- Failed Save: The replacement applies.
- Successful Save: The original roll stands, but the creature becomes Resonance Marked by you and you retain the Omen die until the end of your next turn.

Omen Limits

An Omen cannot replace a roll that has no d20, retroactively change a fully resolved event, or automatically override a higher-authority fixed result. A Secret Law, divine decree, artifact prophecy, tribulation law, or equal- or higher-Source-CL certainty can require a Cultivation Check.

Cultivation Level 6 — Read the Thread

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 3 Resonance  
Target: One creature, object, location, active plan, or imminent event you can meaningfully observe

Choose one Thread Question from the Normalized Execution Notes:

- What is this subject most likely to do next?
- What is it trying hardest to protect?
- What immediate danger is connected to it?
- What choice would most alter its next likely outcome?
- Is fate around it ordinary, Restricted, Forbidden, Secret, divine, artifact-level, tribulation-bound, or otherwise distorted?
- What visible sign will precede the next major consequence tied to it?

The answer is symbolic but operationally useful. It must identify a real pressure, likely action, danger, leverage point, omen, or distortion rather than empty atmosphere.

Thread Clarity

- Against ordinary and lower-Source-CL concealment, the answer is direct enough to guide immediate action.
- Equal or higher authority can require a Cultivation Check.
- On a failed check, you learn which category is obscured and one visible sign of the concealment rather than receiving false information.
- Protected fate can reveal a branch rather than a certainty: “If no one intervenes,” “if the oath remains intact,” or “if the artifact is used.”

Mark the Branch

After receiving the answer, choose one creature involved in the predicted branch. If it knowingly takes the predicted action before the end of your next turn, it becomes Resonance Marked by you and you may move 10 feet or allow one ally within 30 feet to move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that creature.

Cultivation Level 18 — Sever One Thread

You can cut one resolved possibility away from the world and force another nearby possibility to occupy its place.

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature within 90 feet succeeds or fails on an attack roll, ability check, saving throw, death saving throw, or Cultivation Check, or an immediately resolved event creates a single discrete outcome  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Requirement: You are not Fate-Tangled, and the event has not yet produced further dependent rolls or completed a later action

Name the thread you are severing in a brief statement: “the blade lands,” “the seal holds,” “the soul escapes,” “the gate opens,” or another precise outcome.

Choose one procedure.

Reroute the Roll

Force the creature to reroll the d20 and choose which result applies. If the creature is unwilling, it makes a Charisma saving throw first.

- Failed Save: You choose which result applies.
- Successful Save: The reroll occurs, but the target chooses which result applies and suffers two different ordinary Spiritual Pressure effects as one exceptional package.

Restore the Omen

If you used an Omen die on the triggering roll or on a directly connected roll this scene, replace the final d20 with the expended Omen result instead. An unwilling target makes the same Charisma saving throw described above.

Cut the Immediate Event

For a discrete non-roll event—an ordinary teleport completing, an ordinary possession taking hold, an ordinary gate opening, an ordinary execution trigger firing, or an ordinary Anchor collapsing—make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s Source Rule.

- Success: The named event does not occur. Costs already paid remain paid unless the source says otherwise.
- Failure: Delay the event until the end of the current turn and reveal one legal condition that could stop or alter it.

Severed-Thread Consequence

After Sever One Thread resolves:

- Set your Fate Tension to its maximum.
- You become Fate-Tangled.
- Choose and record one Severed Thread Consequence from the fixed list before play continues. It must arise from the altered event.
- You cannot use Sever One Thread again until that consequence is resolved through its recorded completion condition. Restoring Resonance or completing an ordinary rest does not restore access.

Examples include:

- an authority notices the impossible divergence;
- the spared death returns as a future tribulation;
- a sealed enemy gains a prophetic connection to you;
- the abandoned possibility becomes a hostile omen-spirit;
- a different branch claims the cost that was refused;
- your name disappears from one relationship, record, or prophecy until repaired.

Secret-Law Authority

An equal- or higher-Source-CL Secret Law, divine decree, artifact destiny, tribulation law, fixed reincarnation event, voluntary self-sacrifice, or campaign-defining outcome can resist Sever One Thread. Resolve the contest by Source CL and then Cultivation Check. Even on failure, you learn whether the outcome was fixed, protected, willingly accepted, or anchored elsewhere.

Fate Reader changes possibility. It does not erase Karma already earned, invalidate a lawful Soul Contract, or remove the moral and spiritual consequences of the action that created the roll.

Action  
Range: Touch  
Cost: 3 Resonance

Touch a willing creature suffering Frightened, Charmed, a Nightmare Scar, ordinary despair, grief paralysis, emotional corruption, or an ordinary memory-emotion wound.

Choose one:

Consume

End one ordinary effect. Gain 1 Sorrow Burden if you are below your maximum. You take 1d8 Psychic damage per authority tier, normally one die for ordinary, two for Restricted, three for Rare or Forbidden, and four for Secret or comparable effects. This damage cannot be reduced, redirected, transferred, converted into healing, or used to generate another Sorrow Burden.

Suppress

Suppress a stronger effect until the end of your next turn. You take 2d8 Psychic damage that cannot be reduced. The target gains Advantage on the next save or Cultivation Check it makes against that effect during the suppression.

Diagnose

Do not remove the effect. Learn its Source CL relationship to yours, whether it is self-generated or externally imposed, one trigger that strengthens it, one condition that weakens it, and one lawful recovery route.

Equal- or higher-Source-CL effects can require a Cultivation Check. Failure never worsens the target’s condition; instead, you become Resonance Marked by the hostile source until the end of your next turn.

Reaction  
You can use this when  A meaningful creature within 60 feet becomes Bloodied, Frightened, Charmed, possessed, reduced to 0 Hit Points, dies, or experiences a major emotional break

Gain 1 Sorrow Burden and choose the triggering creature. If it is willing or fails a Wisdom saving throw, it becomes Resonance Marked by you until the end of your next turn.

You learn the dominant emotional category around it: fear, grief, rage, guilt, love, emptiness, despair, relief, using the fixed Emotion Categories in the Normalized Execution Notes.

This does not reveal the cause, hidden facts, exact memories, guilt’s truth, or whether the emotion is morally justified.

Carry the First Tear

Once per round when an ally within 30 feet would suffer an ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect, you may spend 1 Sorrow Burden to take that effect instead. You may choose a different ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect that meaningfully represents the burden. This does not use your Reaction.

Cultivation Level 18 — Vessel of Ten Thousand Sorrows

You open your soul as a communal vessel without allowing the stored grief to erase your identity.

Bonus Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance and any number of Sorrow Burdens  
Duration: The scene

Create a 30-foot-radius Mourning Field centered on you. It moves with you and has your Source CL.

While active:

- Allies of your choice in the field have Resistance to Psychic damage.
- They have Advantage on saves against Charmed, Frightened, possession, nightmare, despair, grief, ordinary emotional corruption, and forced memory-emotion effects.
- When an ally in the field fails one of those saves, you may take one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect to let it reroll. You can do this once per round without spending your Reaction.
- When you use Eat the Bitter Memory, Shared Burden, Spiritual Exorcism, or another legal feature to remove, suppress, absorb, or delay a meaningful hostile effect in the field, choose one ally in the field. It gains Temporary Hit Points equal to Wisdom modifier + Proficiency Bonus.
- A creature cannot generate Sorrow Burdens from consequences you already absorbed during this activation.

For each Sorrow Burden spent when the field manifests, choose one Mourning Office:

Office of the Wake

Allies reduced to 0 Hit Points in the field remain conscious until the end of their current turn, though they are still at 0 Hit Points and make death saving throws normally afterward.

Office of the Empty Chair

Hostile creatures in the field cannot benefit from ordinary invisibility or emotional concealment against creatures they meaningfully harmed during the scene.

Office of the Funeral Bell

Office of Returning Names

tianxia.talent.smoke.the_last_breath_hid.player_text:
The Last Breath Hides the Empire

“The palace burned for three days. No one agreed where the emperor went. The smoke remembered, but it did not testify.”
To learn this, you need  CL 17+, Court of Hidden Witnesses, hidden smoke scripture
Use a reaction.
You can use this when  One creature you can see or hear within 120 feet declares an attack, harmful effect, Domain, Realm Evolution, Secret Inheritance, escape technique, or public accusation
Cost: 10 cultivation points (your Path resource)
Use Limit: Once per week
A sovereign smoke court answers the declaration before the world finishes witnessing it.
Choose up to three 20-foot cubes within 120 feet. They become Dense Smoke Veils for 1 minute. These veils do not require Concentration.
The triggering creature gains a Smoke Trace that lasts for the full duration.
Then choose one inheritance 
Hide the Witness
Choose up to five willing creatures inside the smoke.
Each becomes Invisible until it leaves the smoke, attacks, deals damage, or the inheritance ends.
This invisibility is smoke-concealment, not an illusion.
Carry the Evidence
One object, corpse, written message, Formation key, or unattended item inside the smoke is carried to another smoke cube you created with this inheritance.
The object must fit inside a 5-foot cube and cannot be worn or carried by an unwilling creature.
Smother the Declaration
The triggering creature makes a Constitution saving throw.
Failed Save: The triggering action resolves with Disadvantage on all attack rolls it makes, and targets have Advantage on saving throws against it. If it required speech, breath, command, roar, song, or verbal scripture, it also cannot be repeated until the end of the creature’s next turn.
Successful Save: Targets have Advantage on saving throws against the triggering action, or the triggering attack rolls have Disadvantage if it uses attack rolls.
Reveal the Ashen Path
Every creature of your choice inside the smoke learns the direction to the triggering creature, even if it teleports or becomes Invisible before the end of its next turn.
The Last Breath Hides the Empire does not erase memory. It controls what can still be seen, carried, followed, or cleanly spoken while the smoke court exists.

tianxia.talent.sniper.the_arrow_that_arr.player_text:
The Arrow That Arrived Before the Bowstring

Secret Sniper Inheritance Prerequisites: Heaven-Hunting Eye, Phasic Shot, CL 17+, a hidden scripture of impossible trajectory
Use an action.
Range: 1 mile, or farther by story/project/formation at GM discretion
Target: One creature, object, formation anchor, vehicle weak point, siege engine, exposed spirit channel, or battlefield command focus whose exact location you know
Cost: Expend Martial Focus and spend 3 cultivation points (your Path resource)
Use Limit: Once per week
You lower your breath until the world forgets you are about to act.
Then the shot arrives.
Make one ranged weapon attack or single-target ranged spell attack. This attack has the following properties:
it ignores normal and long range;
it has Advantage;
Deadly Aim applies;
it ignores Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover;
it ignores Total Cover unless the target is inside a sealed Barrier, sealed vault, demiplane, divine refuge, artifact enclosure, or equivalent absolute protection;
it can pass through one non-absolute obstruction as though using Phasic Shot;
it can apply up to three Snipe talents you know;
it counts as magical, cultivation-enhanced, and spiritually significant.
On a hit, the attack deals normal damage plus 10d10 damage. Then choose three different Decisive Line effects:
Line Through the Heart: The target makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it drops to 0 Hit Points if its remaining Hit Points are equal to or less than half its maximum Hit Points.
Line Through the Hand: The target drops one held item, command implement, weapon, talisman, seal, or focus. If the item is protected, win an opposed Cultivation Check.
Line Through the Foot: The target’s Speed becomes 0 and it cannot teleport until the end of its next turn.
Line Through the Breath: The target cannot speak, chant, roar, provide verbal components, or use breath-keyed techniques until the end of its next turn.
Line Through the Eye: The target is Blinded until the end of its next turn, and invisibility or ordinary concealment does not protect it from you for 1 minute.
Line Through the Formation: Suppress one exposed formation anchor, ward node, barrier segment, domain focus, siege engine component, or command device until the end of your next turn.
Line Through the Technique: End one non-Secret ongoing effect on the target if its Pattern Rank or equivalent is not higher than your Proficiency Bonus; otherwise make an opposed Cultivation Check.
Line Through the Command: One order, command aura, battlefield signal, prepared reaction, or commanded servant sequence from the target fails or is delayed until the end of its next turn.
Line Through the Escape: If the target would move, teleport, or be carried away before the end of its next turn, you may use your Reaction to force it to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the movement fails.
On a miss, the shot still finds a lesser line. Choose one Decisive Line effect other than Line Through the Heart, and apply it if the target fails the relevant saving throw or opposed check.
Limits: This inheritance cannot automatically kill a major villain, destroy an artifact, invalidate a whole fortress, erase a divine refuge, or ignore a superior Secret Inheritance. Against such targets, success may instead create the one opening needed for the party, project, sect, army, or next scene to exploit.

tianxia.talent.sound.the_first_sound_bef.player_text:
The First Sound Before Heaven

“Before Heaven named itself, something rang. The cultivator who hears it does not speak loudly. They remind the world what it once answered to.”
To learn this, you need  CL 17+, Sound-Sovereign Incarnation, World-Ringing Note, hidden primordial-tone scripture
Use an action.
Range: 300 feet, or one connected resonant structure within sight
Area: 60-foot-radius sphere, 300-foot line, or one named resonant target
Cost: 15 cultivation points (your Path resource)
Use Limit: Once per week
Release a primordial tone, absolute silence, or impossible vibration.
Choose one mode.
Heaven-Ringing Mode:
Creatures in the area make Constitution saving throws.
Failed Save: Take 16d10 Thunder or Psychic damage, become Deafened for 1 minute, and become Stunned until the end of your next turn.
Successful Save: Take half damage and become Deafened until the end of your next turn.
Structure-Shattering Mode:
Choose one object, barrier, structure, Formation Anchor, gate, instrument array, or terrain feature.
Make a Sound Cultivation Attack or Cultivation Check against a GM-set DC.
Success: Deal 20d10 Thunder damage to the target, ignoring ordinary Resistance and hardness. If the target survives, choose one ordinary function to suppress until the end of your next turn.
Silence-Before-Sound Mode:
Create a 60-foot-radius field until the end of your next turn.
Inside the field:
hostile verbal components fail;
hostile Voice talents fail;
ordinary sound cannot exist;
Thunder damage from hostile sources becomes 0;
creatures of your choice can still hear your command, bell, or soul-tone.
The First Sound Before Heaven does not automatically destroy artifacts, Domains, immortal formations, permanent karmic bonds, or Realm-defining structures. It may crack, suppress, reveal, or contest them according to GM adjudication.

tianxia.talent.poison.serious_ingrained_.player_text:
Serious Ingrained Toxin Stages

A Serious Ingrained Toxin has stages. At the end of each long rest, the target makes a Constitution saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC.
Success: The poison stage decreases by 1. If it would decrease below Stage 1, the poison ends.
Failure: The poison stage increases by 1, to a maximum of Stage 4.
A creature cannot suffer more than one Serious Ingrained Toxin at a time.
Stage 1 - Bitter Channels. The target has Disadvantage on the first Cultivation Check it makes each day, and cannot reduce cultivation points (your Path resource) costs below their printed values.
Stage 2 - Numb Meridian Flow. The target’s maximum cultivation points (your Path resource) is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus, and it has Disadvantage on concentration saving throws. This maximum cultivation points (your Path resource) reduction ends when the poison ends.
Stage 3 - Foundation Corrosion. The target’s Hit Point maximum is reduced by your Cultivation Level, and the target regains only half as much cultivation points (your Path resource) from short-rest or scene-based recovery. This maximum Hit Point reduction ends when the poison ends.
Stage 4 - Life-Gate Closing. The target cannot regain cultivation points (your Path resource) above half its maximum cultivation points (your Path resource), cannot gain Temporary HP, and has Disadvantage on death saving throws. If the target fails three daily saves while at Stage 4, it dies unless the GM decides the poison instead triggers a major cultivation injury, coma, sealed meridians, or story crisis.

Secret Formation Inheritance

Prerequisites: Sovereign of the World-Diagram, Heavenly Grand Formation, CL 17+ (Cultivation Level), lost scripture, celestial revelation, sect-defining inheritance, or world-array transmission
Timing: Action, or 1 minute if used as a prepared ritual

You unfold the World-Array Scripture. For a short time, the surrounding world is treated as if it had always been built from your Nodes, Gates, and Flow Lines.

Choose five World Laws from the list below. The area becomes a World Array with those laws.

Law of the Eye: You always know the location of creatures inside the area unless hidden by a Secret technique or stronger effect. You do not learn their thoughts, statistics, or secrets.

Law of the Gate: Keyed allies may teleport up to 60 feet inside the area as a Bonus Action. Hostile creatures attempting to teleport inside, out of, or through the area must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or the teleport fails.

Law of the Locked Road: Hostile creatures treat the entire area as Difficult Terrain. Once per round when a hostile creature moves more than 10 feet, you may force it to make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, its movement ends.

Law of the Hidden Road: Keyed allies have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and may Hide while Lightly Obscured inside the area. Hostile creatures have Disadvantage on checks made to find your Nodes, Eyes, hidden Gates, or concealed keyed allies.

Law of the Killing Line: Once during each of your turns, choose a line up to 120 feet long inside the area. Hostile creatures on that line make Dexterity saving throws. A creature takes 8d8 Force damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

Law of the Returning Breath: Once per round when a keyed ally inside the area is reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, it instead drops to 1 Hit Point and is moved up to 30 feet to a legal space inside the area. A creature can benefit from this law only once per use of the inheritance.

Law of the Suppressed Current: The first time each round a hostile creature spends cultivation points (your Path resource) inside the area, it must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the cultivation points (your Path resource) is spent and the effect fails. On a success, the effect works, but the creature cannot benefit from this law again until the start of its next turn.

Law of the Shattered Formation: Choose one non-Secret Formation, Barrier, Domain, or prepared magical battlefield effect inside the area. Make a Formation Check against its creator’s save DC. On a success, suppress it while this inheritance lasts. On a failure, suppress one of its minor benefits until the end of your next turn.

Law of the Nine Palaces: Divide the area into up to nine visible or invisible palaces. Once per turn, when a hostile creature crosses from one palace into another, it must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, choose whether it becomes lost, slowed, or exposed until the start of your next turn. A lost creature cannot willingly move closer to a chosen objective. A slowed creature’s Speed is halved. An exposed creature cannot benefit from Invisible or Half Cover.

Law of the World Anchor: Create nine Anchors. Each Anchor has AC 19, Hit Points equal to 15 × your Proficiency Bonus, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. The World Array does not require Concentration while at least five Anchors remain. If fewer than five remain, you must Concentrate to maintain it. If fewer than three remain, it collapses.

While this inheritance lasts, you may Pulse one Pattern Layer or World Law once during each of your turns without using an action.

Limits: This inheritance does not permanently create territory, erase a kingdom, make you omnipotent, automatically kill creatures, rewrite the past, or suppress a stronger Secret Inheritance without a contested scene. - Reverse: the original source receives it.
- Transfer: one willing creature within 60 feet receives it.

Healing cannot exceed maximum Hit Points.

Movement Pattern

Record up to 30 feet of movement or teleportation.

- Echo: move the original creature the same distance and direction when legal.
- Reverse: return it toward its starting point by the recorded distance.
- Transfer: move one willing creature by the recorded path or teleport distance.

An unwilling creature makes a Strength or Charisma saving throw, chosen according to whether the original was movement or teleportation.

Cultivation-Point Pattern

Record up to twice your Proficiency Bonus Cultivation Points spent.

- Echo: the original creature must pay the recorded amount again to maintain the result it created until the start of its next turn. If it cannot, one active effect from that expenditure is suppressed.
- Reverse: you regain Qi equal to half the recorded amount, rounded up.
- Transfer: one willing creature regains Cultivation Points equal to half the recorded amount, limited by its maximum.

A single expenditure cannot be used to refund itself recursively.

Condition Pattern

Record one condition with a duration no longer than 1 minute.

- Echo: the original recipient repeats the original saving throw. On failure, the condition returns until the end of its next turn.
- Reverse: the original source makes a Charisma saving throw. On failure, it suffers the condition until the end of its next turn.
- Transfer: another legal target makes a Charisma saving throw. On failure, it suffers the condition until the end of its next turn.

This cannot echo or transfer death, permanent transformation, complete cultivation erasure, or a Secret condition without a successful Cultivation Check against the original effect’s save DC.

Powered-Technique Pattern

Record one non-Secret, non-Immortal technique with:

- An activation time of Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.
- An instantaneous effect or duration no longer than 1 minute.
- No permanent material or lifespan cost.

At the start of your next turn, spend the technique’s complete Cultivation Point cost and choose:

- Echo: resolve the technique again from its original source and targets when still legal.
- Reverse: resolve a bounded inverse chosen from damage to healing, push to pull, restriction to movement, concealment to revelation, or another explicit inverse approved by the technique’s tags.
- Transfer: originate the technique from yourself or your Domain Armament using legal new targets.

The repeated technique:

- Uses your Cultivation Attack Modifier and save DC.
- Cannot repeat itself or create another Return Pattern.
- Cannot duplicate an item, permanent summon, artifact property, Secret Law, or permanent effect.

Reaction

Binding an Unwilling Target

An unwilling creature can be bound only when it is Completely Subdued, has formally surrendered, accepted release under stated terms, inherited a valid Contract through an explicit Source Rule, or is subject to recognized conquered or legal authority.

CL18 — Sovereign Soul Contract

Create Sovereign Contract

Ritual Time: 1 hour  
Range: All parties and required Anchors present  
Cost: 10 Qi  
Duration: Indefinite until fulfilled, released, broken, or destroyed

A Sovereign Contract may govern sect succession, dynastic marriage, national tribute, immortal service, possession of a Saint-class treasure, prison of a great cultivator, transfer of a bloodline, protection of a world gate, or another major obligation.

It requires a physical or cultivated Sovereign Contract Anchor such as a tablet, throne seal, ancestral book, blood altar, spirit brand, weapon, city Formation, or world-gate inscription.

Sovereign Contract Anchor

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC + 2
- Hit Points: 12 × your CL
- Resistance: All damage from lower-Source-CL attacks
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic damage
- Source CL: Your CL
- Repair: Equal/higher Contract, Soul, Oath, Formation, or artifact procedure

Sovereign Terms

A Sovereign Contract may pledge:

- An entire Cultivation Point resource.
- One Path, Subpath, Method, Foundation active system, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, Domain Armament network, or Sphere family.
- A soul fragment or reincarnation right.
- Up to ten years of lifespan.
- A bloodline transmission.
- A Saint-class or lower real item.
- A city, sect, office, Formation, route, or treasury recognized by the setting.
- A named future service that remains possible.

A Secret Law, Immortal authority, artifact soul, entire true identity, or world principle can be pledged only when its own Source Rule permits it or the Contract’s authority is equal or higher.

Sovereign Breach

A Sovereign breach creates Claims equal to your Proficiency Bonus and activates one printed Sovereign Penalty:

- Suppress pledged cultivation collateral.
- Seal the breacher’s movement to a named territory.
- Transfer a pledged office, item, resource, or authority.
- Inflict Tier III or Tier IV cultivation harm matching the collateral.
- Call the breacher before the Contract Anchor.
- Place the soul fragment or reincarnation right in escrow within the Anchor.

Contract Court

Action  
Area: 40-foot-radius field centered on the Sovereign Anchor  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

Inside the Court:

- Contract terms, Claims, pledged collateral, breach status, and authorized assignees become visible.
- A party cannot conceal a breach through a lower-Source-CL effect.
- Foreclosure costs one fewer Claim, minimum 1.
- Call the Contracted Party and Foreclose Cultivation may target any party in the field without range limits.
- A Contract challenge can be heard and resolved.

Final Foreclosure

Once during the Court, choose one party in Sovereign breach with at least four Claims. It makes a Charisma saving throw.

Failed Save

Choose one pledged result:

- Collect All Qi: Remove all current points from one pledged resource and prevent recovery for 1 hour.
- Close the Cultivation Collateral: Suppress all explicitly pledged cultivation systems; if every active system was pledged, impose Complete Cultivation Suppression.
- Seize Soul Escrow: Remove the pledged soul fragment, reincarnation right, or spirit collateral into the Anchor.
- Collect the Named Price: Transfer the exact pledged item, office, lifespan, memory, bloodline, service, or authority.
- Compel Performance: Move the party by a legal route to the named site and prevent voluntary departure for 1 hour when the Contract lawfully pledged that service.

Successful Save

One pledged system is suppressed until the end of the target’s next turn, it loses current Cultivation Points equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus, and one Claim remains unspent.

Breaking a Sovereign Contract

A Sovereign Contract can be broken through:

- Fulfillment or mutual release.
- Destruction or lawful alteration of the Sovereign Anchor.
- Equal/higher Contract, Oath, Karma, Fate, Soul, Void, Name, Samsara, or Conceptual authority.
- A successful challenge proving that a required party, term, collateral, or acceptance state was supernaturally falsified.
- A campaign-scale revolution, succession, conquest, artifact intervention, or heavenly judgment recognized by the setting.

Breaking the Contract ends future foreclosure. It does not automatically restore collateral already consumed, transferred, aged, severed, or destroyed; that requires the shared reconstruction procedure.

Contract Is Not Karma

The Contract Court asks whether a valid term was breached and whether named collateral may be foreclosed. It does not decide whether the Contract was just, whether the breacher deserved punishment, or whether unrelated deeds created Karmic Merit or Burden.

End lower- or equal-Source-CL Charmed or Frightened. Against higher authority, suppress the condition until the end of the target’s next turn and allow an immediate repeat save.

Redirect the Breath

Reduce the triggering damage by 2d8 + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier after resistance but before Hit Point loss.

Recenter the Step

Reduce forced movement by up to 15 feet, or allow the target to stand and move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Clear the Senses

Suppress Blinded, Deafened, or one Illusion affecting the target until the end of its next turn when the Source CL is no higher than yours. Against higher authority, grant Advantage on the next relevant save or check.

Open the Constricted Meridian

The target may spend up to your Proficiency Bonus Cultivation Points despite one lower- or equal-Source-CL effect that would prevent voluntary expenditure. This does not end the suppressing effect.

A creature can receive one Corrective Pour per turn. Corrective Pour does not require the target to physically swallow tea; steam, scent, a thrown droplet, or a remote pour through your Domain Armament carries the correction.

tianxia.subpath.qi.tea_sage_cultivator.f.player_text:
CL14 — Grandmaster Infusion

You learn all Tea Formulas.

Tea Changes with the Guest

When a creature consumes one of your prepared Infusion Cups, you may choose any Formula you know at that moment rather than the Formula selected during preparation.

After using Read the Cup and Pulse on the drinker during the current scene, you may place two different Formulas in the same cup. Resolve both, but a creature still cannot maintain two noninstantaneous Tea Formula effects simultaneously; it chooses which one continues.

Reverse the Decoction

Action  
Range: Touch, or 30 feet through your Tea Domain Armament  
Cost: 5 Qi  
Target: One willing, Restrained, Unconscious, or Completely Subdued creature

Choose one poison, disease, charm, fear, Dream infestation, possession, altered-memory effect, meridian blockage, or non-Secret hostile condition you identified through Read the Cup and Pulse.

- Lower Source CL: Extract and end it.
- Equal Source CL or within 2: The target makes the effect’s normal recovery save with Advantage. On success, extract and end it. On failure, suppress it for 1 minute.
- Higher Source CL: Make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s save DC. On success, suppress it for 1 minute and create an extract suitable for later specialist analysis. On failure, suppress it until the end of the target’s next turn.

An extracted effect condenses as bitter sediment, discolored steam, a leaf knot, or another temporary Tea Residue Anchor.

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 3 × your CL
- Source CL: The lesser of your CL or the extracted effect’s Source CL
- Duration: Until the end of the scene

Destroying the Residue does not restore an effect already ended. A specialist may study it during the scene to identify the source, prepare an antidote, or support reconstruction. A Secret Law, permanent cultivation injury, destroyed organ, or erased concept requires its own recovery procedure; Reverse the Decoction can stabilize it but cannot bypass that authority.

Nine-Temperature Service

Action  
Area: Up to your Proficiency Bonus willing creatures within 30 feet  
Cost: 5 Qi

For each target, choose a different one of the following:

- Restore 3d8 + your key ability modifier Hit Points.
- Grant Temporary Hit Points equal to 3 × Proficiency Bonus.
- End lower- or equal-Source-CL Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned.
- Allow an immediate save with Advantage against possession, Dream, altered memory, disease, or a meridian suppression effect.
- Move up to 15 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Gain Advantage on the next attack, check, or saving throw before the end of its next turn.

A creature can receive Nine-Temperature Service once per scene.

---

tianxia.subpath.qi.tea_sage_cultivator.f.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 — One Cup Beneath Heaven

Bonus Action  
Area: 30-foot-radius aura centered on you or your Tea Domain Armament  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

Choose up to your Proficiency Bonus creatures inside as Honored Guests. A hostile creature can be chosen only if it willingly accepts the cup.

For the duration:

- You may use Read the Cup and Pulse on an Honored Guest without using an action once per turn.
- Corrective Pour costs 0 Qi once per round and does not require a prepared cup.
- Honored Guests have Advantage against Charmed, Frightened, possession, Dream effects, altered memory, poison, disease, and supernatural emotional manipulation.
- You always know which Honored Guest is in immediate danger of losing consciousness, suffering complete cultivation suppression, or undergoing possession or identity alteration.

The Correct Cup

At the start of each of your turns, serve one Honored Guest. It gains one benefit:

- Restore 4d8 + your key ability modifier Hit Points.
- Regain Cultivation Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
- End one non-Secret hostile condition whose Source CL is no higher than yours.
- Repeat a save against a higher-Source-CL hostile condition with Advantage.
- Move up to 20 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Gain +2 AC until the start of your next turn.
- Become immune to forced possession and unwilling Dream entry until the start of your next turn.

A creature can receive each benefit once during the activation.

Heaven Receives the Guest

An Honored Guest that willingly refrains from hostile actions until the start of its next turn gains one of the following at that time:

- Regain 2d8 Hit Points.
- Regain 2 Cultivation Points.
- End one level of Exhaustion caused by fear, exposure, poison, hunger, thirst, or overexertion.
- Receive a new saving throw against one ongoing non-Secret hostile condition.

This is a cultivated reward for accepted restraint, not magical compulsion.

Last Cup Before Departure

Once during the activation, when an Honored Guest would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, completely suppressed, possessed, or rendered Unconscious by a hostile effect, you may use Corrective Pour without expending your Reaction.

After it resolves, the guest remains at a minimum of 1 Hit Point if damage was the cause, or the hostile state is suppressed until the end of its next turn if the effect’s Source CL is no higher than yours. Higher, Secret, artifact, or conceptual authority instead grants the guest an immediate resistance attempt with Advantage.

One Cup Beneath Heaven does not create food for an army, replace a rest, or grant long-duration expedition provisions. Those are Culinary authorities.

tianxia.subpath.qi.tea_sage_cultivator.f.player_text:
Cultivation Level 3 — Precision Infusions

Learn three Tea Formulas from the list below. Learn one additional Formula at Cultivation Level 6 and all Formulas at Cultivation Level 14.

Prepare Infusion Cups

Ritual Time: 10 minutes  
Cost: 1 Qi  
Implements: Tea implements and ordinary potable water  
Yield: A number of Infusion Cups equal to your Proficiency Bonus  
Duration: 8 hours

For each cup, choose one Formula you know. A cup may be physical tea, condensed steam, a sealed leaf packet, or another culturally appropriate serving. It is a temporary cultivated preparation, not a potion or permanent item.

A willing creature may consume a cup as a Bonus Action. An Unconscious creature is willing when an adjacent creature uses an Action to administer it. A creature can benefit from only one noninstantaneous Tea Formula at a time; receiving another ends the previous one.

Unused cups lose cultivation potency when the duration ends. They cannot be sold as permanent magic items, multiplied through ordinary copying, or harvested to generate Qi.

Cleansing Bitterleaf

The drinker immediately repeats one saving throw against Poisoned, disease, inhaled smoke, gas, dust, contaminated air, or another bodily contaminant.

- If the effect’s Source CL is no higher than yours, the repeat save has Advantage.
- If the effect has no save, suppress its symptoms until the end of the drinker’s next turn.
- If the drinker is not currently affected, it gains Advantage on the next saving throw against one of those hazards before the end of the scene.

This Formula does not remove a permanent poison, curse, infestation, or cultivation injury unless the effect’s own recovery procedure permits a successful save to do so.

Still-Mind Jasmine

Choose one:

- End Charmed or Frightened when the effect’s Source CL is no higher than yours.
- Immediately repeat a save against a higher-Source-CL Charmed, Frightened, possession, Dream, or supernatural emotional effect with Advantage.
- If no such effect is present, gain Advantage on the next Wisdom or Charisma saving throw before the end of the scene.

Spearpoint Red Tea

For 1 minute, the first time during each of the drinker’s turns that it makes an attack roll or forces a creature to make a saving throw through a cultivated technique, it gains one benefit:

- Add +1 to the attack roll; or
- Add 1d4 to one damage roll against one target after the target fails its save.

Choose after the roll but before the result is declared. This Formula cannot apply to every projectile or target of a Barrage.

Cloud-Step Green Tea

The drinker may immediately move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. For 1 minute:

- Speed increases by 10 feet.
- Standing from Prone costs 5 feet of movement.
- The first 10 feet of forced movement suffered during each round is ignored.

Clear-Eye Oolong

For 10 minutes, the drinker gains Advantage on checks to detect:

- Poisoned food or drink.
- Ordinary disguises and concealed weapons.
- Illusions whose Source CL is no higher than yours.
- Deliberately concealed emotional distress.
- A dream, possession, charm, or altered-memory effect already suspected through other evidence.

This Formula does not automatically reveal a creature’s thoughts, secrets, alignment, or guilt.

Bone-Warming Black Tea

The drinker gains Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 × your Proficiency Bonus and, for 1 hour, has Advantage against environmental cold, heat shock, altitude sickness, and Exhaustion caused by exposure.

Cultivation Level 18 — Ten Thousand Swords Return to Origin

Action  
Range: 90 feet  
Area: 30-foot-radius, 30-foot-high cylinder  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

The field fills with sword projections, reflections, trajectories, and ancestral blade images. These manifestations are not independent weapons, cannot be collected or copy item properties, and make attacks only through this feature.

Center it on a visible point, your Sword Domain Armament, or an active Sword Array Field. If centered on the Array, the fields merge, use the larger area and this duration, and require only one Concentration effect.

Returning Swordstorm

When the field appears, choose any number of creatures inside. Each makes a Dexterity saving throw.

- Failed Save: 10d8 Slashing or Force damage and no Reactions until the end of its next turn.
- Successful Save: Half damage and no Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Perfected Sword Array

For the duration:

- Sword Array entry/start damage functions throughout.
- Both Sword Armaments may move to any legal point once per turn.
- Projected swords teleport along sword paths; real swords travel through legal open paths.
- Twin-Sword Command’s second attack adds your key ability modifier.
- Sword Intent costs 0 Qi once per turn.
- A successful save against Sword Intent still suffers the successful-save result.
- Array Pursuit does not expend your Reaction once per round, though it remains once per round.

Return to the Hand

Once during each turn, call one real bound sword in the field directly to a legal free hand without using an action. An artifact restraint, sealed Formation, spatial lock, or higher-authority control can prevent the call. The sword is never duplicated.

tianxia.subpath.qi.tribulation_vessel.fe.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 — Calamity Furnace

Your maximum Calamity Charges increases by 3.

Furnace Response

Reaction  
You can use this when  You fail a saving throw, take damage, become Grappled, Prone, or Restrained, or would be forcibly moved.  
Cost: 2 Calamity Charges  
Limit: Once per round

Choose the appropriate response:

Reverse the Save

Add your Proficiency Bonus to the failed saving throw, potentially turning it into a success.

This is not saving-throw proficiency.

Consume the Damage

Reduce the triggering damage by:

4d8 + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier

Root Against Heaven

Reduce forced movement to 0 and prevent being knocked Prone by the triggering effect.

Burn the Binding

Immediately repeat a saving throw or escape check against Grappled or Restrained with Advantage.

If no escape roll normally exists, make a Strength, Dexterity, or Cultivation Check, your choice, against the effect’s save DC.

On success, the condition ends.

Scar of Authority

When Furnace Response successfully turns a failed save into a success, reduces damage to 0, prevents forced movement, or ends a condition, gain one Tribulation Scar.

You may maintain one Tribulation Scar.

It records the triggering effect’s Calamity Type and Source CL.

Before your next long rest, consume the Scar to choose one:

- Treat one Calamity Charge as the recorded type.
- Add the recorded Source CL difference, maximum +5, to one Cultivation Check made to resist or overcome a similar effect.
- Allow Tribulation Release to ignore ordinary Resistance to the recorded damage type.
- Recognize the same named technique automatically when you perceive it again.

A formal breakthrough tribulation may create a persistent named Scar through the breakthrough rules rather than this temporary one.

---

Cultivation Level 3 — Gather Calamity

After a Qualifying Calamity resolves, gain one Calamity Charge of the appropriate type.

Spend Calamity

Once per turn, when you activate a Qi-powered feature or make a Cultivation Attack, spend one Charge to choose one benefit:

- Add 1d8 damage of a type associated with the Charge to one damage roll.
- Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus.
- Move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Increase one push, pull, lift, or forced movement by 10 feet.
- Move your Domain Armament 20 feet.
- Add your Proficiency Bonus to one Cultivation Check made as part of the activation.

The Charge is spent even if the attack misses or the target succeeds unless the feature never legally activates.

Calamity Sense

When you perceive an active hazard, hostile field, tribulation residue, damaged Formation, unstable artifact, or environmental catastrophe within 60 feet, you learn:

- Its broad Calamity Type.
- Whether it is stable, growing, collapsing, or about to discharge.
- Its Source CL.
- Whether surviving it could create a Calamity Charge.

Calamity Sense does not reveal exact damage or hidden triggers unless another feature permits it.

Cultivation Level 6 — Flowing Pair

Returning Edge

Reaction

You can use this when  A creature you can perceive hits you or an ally within 5 feet of your Falling Saber with an attack roll.  
Cost: 2 Qi  
Limit: Once per round

Make a saber attack roll using the Falling Saber and compare it to the triggering attack roll.

- If your result equals or exceeds the triggering roll, reduce the triggering damage by 2d8 + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier.
- If your result exceeds it by 5 or more, reduce the damage to 0 unless the attack’s Source CL is higher than yours.
- Against a higher Source CL, reducing the damage to 0 also requires a Cultivation Check against the effect’s save DC.

After the reduction resolves, you may reverse Rising and Falling roles.

Tide Follows Tide

Once per turn after the Rising Saber hits, spend 1 Qi to make one attack with the Falling Saber against the same target or a different creature within its reach.

This additional attack:

- Does not add your ability modifier to damage unless another rule normally permits it.
- Cannot generate another additional attack.
- Can generate Tide Flow if it satisfies the alternating requirement.
- Does not repeat a weapon-delivered technique.

Crossed Current

When both sabers are within 5 feet of the same creature, that creature has Disadvantage on checks and saving throws made to Disarm either saber or forcibly move one away from it.

tianxia.subpath.qi.twin_tide_paired_sabe.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 — Two Seas Become One

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- Both sabers simultaneously count as Rising and Falling.
- Gain the first-hit benefits of Rising Saber from each saber once per turn.
- Receiving Mode grants +2 AC against melee attacks instead of +1.
- Begin each turn with at least 2 Tide Flow. If you have less, increase it to 2.
- Tide Follows Tide costs 0 Qi once per turn.
- Returning Edge costs 0 Qi once per round.
- You may move each floating saber up to 30 feet once during each of your turns without using an action.
- A hostile effect whose Source CL is lower than yours cannot Disarm, seize, or suppress only one of the paired sabers; it must affect both or neither.

Tidal Procession

Once during each of your turns, move up to your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks and make up to four saber attacks distributed among creatures whose spaces you pass within reach.

Requirements:

- Attacks must alternate sabers.
- No creature may be attacked more than twice by this procession.
- Resolve each attack at the relevant point of movement.
- This replaces your Action.

Tidal Procession is one activation. Qi Technique Potency applies once.

Four-Wave Delivery

When you use Tidal Procession, you may deliver one eligible weapon-delivered cultivation technique through multiple hits.

- First qualifying hit: normal technique cost.
- Second qualifying hit: pay 2 additional Qi.
- Third qualifying hit: pay 3 additional Qi.
- Fourth qualifying hit: pay 4 additional Qi.

Declare the maximum number of intended deliveries before the first attack and pay the complete additional cost then.

A missed attack consumes its assigned delivery and does not transfer it to another attack.

The technique cannot be a permanent, resurrection, Secret, strategic-scale, or self-replicating effect. Persistent areas and summoned assets can be created only once.

Sea Without Opening

Once per round after you spend Tide Flow, choose one creature hit by both sabers during the current turn.

It makes a Dexterity or Wisdom saving throw, its choice.

Failed Save: Choose one:

- Restrained between the paired saber currents until the start of your next turn.
- Cannot take Reactions and its Speed becomes 0 until the start of your next turn.
- Suppress one active weapon stance, Guard Mode, or Domain Armament mode until the start of your next turn.
- Increase its next Cultivation Point cost before the end of its next turn by 3.

Successful Save: It cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Against a target 6 or more CL lower than you, the failed-save result lasts until the end of your next turn.

tianxia.subpath.qi.venomous_poison_culti.player_text:
Cultivation Level 3 — Living Venom Dantian

Gain Immunity to Poison damage and Poisoned from effects whose Source CL is lower than yours.

Against equal or higher Source CL, gain Resistance to Poison damage and Advantage on saving throws against Poisoned.

Seed Venom

You can use this when  One of your Qi-powered features deals damage to a creature.  
Cost: 1 Qi  
Limit: Once per turn  
Saving Throw: Constitution

Choose one known Venom Strain.

On a failed save:

- The target gains one Venom Stage.
- It takes 1d8 damage of the Strain’s permitted type.

On a successful save:

- It takes half the additional damage.
- It gains no Stage.

At three Venom Stages, the target becomes Deeply Envenomed.

Strain Symptoms

While a creature has at least one Stage, apply the selected Strain’s symptom:

- Furnace Venom: The first time each turn it spends Cultivation Points, it takes damage equal to the number spent.
- Frost Venom: Speed is reduced by 5 feet per Stage, maximum 15 feet.
- Blood Venom: Healing received is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus per Stage.
- Mind Venom: Subtract 1 from Concentration saves per Stage.
- Spirit Venom: It cannot benefit from Invisible or Incorporeal concealment against you; at two or more Stages, possession and spirit projection costs increase by 1.
- Bone Venom: AC is reduced by 1 at two Stages and by 2 at three Stages. This does not reduce AC below 10 through this feature alone.
- Dream Venom: Subtract 1 from saves against Dream, Illusion, Charmed, Frightened, and sleep effects per Stage.

A target may bear Stages from multiple Strains, but the total cannot exceed three.

Refine the Antidote

Ritual Time: 10 minutes  
Cost: 1 Qi

Create one antidote dose for one Venom Strain you know.

A creature consuming it gains:

- Advantage on its next saving throw against that Strain within 8 hours.
- The ability to repeat one save against one Stage of that Strain immediately.

The dose loses potency after 8 hours.

---

tianxia.subpath.qi.venomous_poison_culti.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 — Myriad-Venom Sovereign

You learn all Venom Strains.

Your Poison damage:

- Ignores ordinary Resistance.
- Treats ordinary Immunity as Resistance.
- Does not override artifact, Secret, conceptual, or explicitly absolute Immunity without another Source Rule.

Sovereign Infection

A creature with three Venom Stages becomes Sovereign-Infected.

While infected:

- It suffers the symptoms of every Strain represented among its Stages.
- It cannot remove more than one Stage per turn.
- Ordinary resting does not remove the Stages.
- Completing a long rest removes one Stage only after successful cultivated treatment.
- If it dies, its corpse remains poisonous and retains one Stage until purified.

Ten-Thousand-Poison Kingdom

Action  
Range: 120 feet  
Area: 40-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required  
Cost: 10 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

Choose three Venom Strains.

For the duration:

- Plague of One Hundred Meridians functions throughout the Kingdom without a separate activation.
- You may change its active Strain at the start of each turn.
- Seed Venom may apply two different Strains on a failed save, but still grants at most one total Stage unless you spend 2 additional Qi.
- Deeply Envenomed creatures cannot regain Cultivation Points.
- Sovereign-Infected creatures cannot activate a feature costing more Cultivation Points than your Proficiency Bonus.
- Venom Possession costs 1 Qi and lasts until the end of your next turn.

Poison the Core

Once during the Kingdom, choose one Sovereign-Infected creature inside.

It makes a Constitution saving throw with Advantage if its Source CL is higher than yours and Disadvantage if at least 6 CL lower.

On failure, choose one structure to poison for 1 minute:

- One Sphere.
- One Subpath.
- One Method.
- One Golden Core Form.
- One Nascent Soul engine.
- Domain Armament.
- Foundation active features.
- All Cultivation Point recovery.

The poisoned structure is suppressed.

The target repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the suppression on a success.

If it fails three saves before succeeding:

- The poison becomes indefinite.
- It remains until removed by cultivated treatment whose Source CL equals or exceeds yours, a breakthrough, a suitable Foundation or Method repair, or a higher-authority purification effect.

On a successful initial save:

- The selected structure is suppressed until the start of its next turn.

Poison the Core cannot permanently erase the structure. It can disable it until treated.

tianxia.subpath.qi.venomous_poison_culti.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 — Plague of One Hundred Meridians

Action  
Origin: You or your Domain Armament  
Range: 90 feet  
Area: 20-foot-radius sphere  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required  
Cost: 6 Qi

Choose one known Venom Strain.

The cloud, pollen, liquid mist, ash, blood vapor, spirit worms, or invisible meridian pressure fills the area.

A creature makes a Constitution saving throw when it:

- Enters the area for the first time during a turn.
- Starts its turn inside.

A creature is affected once per turn.

Failed Save

- 5d6 damage of the Strain’s type.
- Gain one Venom Stage of that Strain.
- If already Deeply Envenomed, apply the Strain’s Plague Effect instead.

Successful Save

- Half damage.
- No new Stage.

Plague Effects

- Furnace: The target cannot spend more Cultivation Points during one turn than your Proficiency Bonus until the start of its next turn.
- Frost: Speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn.
- Blood: It cannot regain Hit Points until the start of its next turn.
- Mind: It cannot maintain Concentration until the start of its next turn. Active Concentration ends.
- Spirit: It cannot become Incorporeal, possess another creature, project its soul, or teleport until the start of its next turn.
- Bone: It loses Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage until the start of its next turn.
- Dream: It is Dazed until the start of its next turn: it may take an Action or Bonus Action, not both, and cannot take Reactions.

Contagious Technique

Once per round, when a Deeply Envenomed creature inside the Plague damages another creature within 5 feet, the second creature makes a Constitution saving throw.

On failure, it gains one Stage of the active Strain.

This cannot spread back to the source creature or recursively spread again during the same turn.

tianxia.subpath.qi.venomous_poison_culti.player_text:
Cultivation Level 6 — Poisoned Meridian Scripture

When a creature reaches two or more Venom Stages, choose one Meridian Affliction. The Affliction persists while it has at least two Stages.

You may change the Affliction once during each of your turns when you damage the target with a Qi-powered feature.

Closed Meridian

The target cannot regain Cultivation Points.

Labored Circulation

The first Qi-powered feature it activates each turn costs 1 additional Cultivation Point.

If it cannot pay the complete cost, the activation fails without spending other costs.

Crooked Meridian

The first time each turn it uses a movement technique, teleportation, flight activation, or Domain Armament movement, reduce that movement by 15 feet.

If the movement is 15 feet or less, it is suppressed.

Bleeding Meridian

The first time each turn it deals damage with a Qi-powered feature, it takes 1d8 Necrotic or Poison damage.

Muddled Meridian

It has Disadvantage on the first Cultivation Check it makes each turn.

Stolen Breath

It cannot take Reactions after spending Cultivation Points until the start of its next turn.

Forced Purge

A creature with a Meridian Affliction may use its Action and spend Cultivation Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus to make a Constitution saving throw.

On success:

- Remove one Venom Stage.
- End the current Meridian Affliction if fewer than two Stages remain.

On failure:

- The Cultivation Points remain spent.
- It takes 2d8 damage of the active Strain’s type.

tianxia.subpath.qi.venomous_poison_culti.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 — Venomous Incarnation

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 7 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

Your body becomes a sovereign venom system.

For the duration:

- Gain Resistance to all damage except Force, Radiant, and Void.
- Move through openings at least 1 inch wide.
- Move through creature spaces as Difficult Terrain.
- You cannot be Grappled or Restrained by a physical effect whose Source CL is lower than yours.

- A creature that damages you with a melee attack gains one Venom Stage of a Strain you know unless it succeeds on a Constitution saving throw.
- You may originate Poison-, Disease-, Blood-, Mist-, or Spirit-tagged techniques from any point in your space or your active Plague.

Venom Possession

Bonus Action  
Range: 30 feet  
Cost: 3 Qi  
Target: One Deeply Envenomed creature  
Saving Throw: Constitution

On a failed save:

- Enter the target’s body as living venom until the start of your next turn.
- Your body disappears.
- You move with the target.
- You cannot be targeted separately except by an effect that targets poison, disease, internal invaders, souls, or creatures inside another creature.

- At the start of its turn, choose one: it loses its Action, loses its Bonus Action and Reactions, or its Speed becomes 0.

- You do not enter.

At the start of your next turn, emerge into a legal space within 5 feet.

Cultivation Level 6 — Empty Palm

Action  
Range: Touch  
Cost: 3 Qi  
Attack: Melee Cultivation Attack

On a hit, deal:

4d8 + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier

Force or Void damage.

The target gains 1 Void Mark.

Then choose one Empty Palm operation.

Unravel Manifestation

Choose one active effect on the target or one active effect whose Anchor, manifestation, or origin you are touching.

Eligible effects include:

- A Path or Subpath transformation.
- A Sphere talent.
- A Recorded Art.
- A Forged Technique.
- A Domain Armament manifestation.
- A Qi field.
- A summoned or projected Cultivation Asset.
- A temporary barrier.
- A talisman, seal, ward, or Formation function.
- A temporary item property.
- A possession tether.
- A curse or condition with an active supernatural structure.

Resolve as follows:

- Source CL lower than yours and not Secret, Immortal, artifact, or explicitly absolute: suppress the chosen effect until the start of your next turn.
- Source CL equal to yours: make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s save DC. On success, suppress it until the start of your next turn.
- Source CL higher than yours: the target or effect first makes its normal resistance if one exists, then you must succeed on a Cultivation Check against its save DC. On success, suppress it until the end of the current turn.

Suppression:

- Does not refund costs.
- Does not end the effect’s duration.
- Disables only the selected active effect unless it is the sole Anchor sustaining a larger effect.
- Does not permanently destroy an artifact, Foundation, Method, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, or complete Path at Cultivation Level 6.

Empty the Meridian

The target makes a Constitution saving throw.

Failed Save:

- Lose Qi or another current Cultivation Point resource equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
- It cannot regain Cultivation Points until the start of its next turn.

Successful Save:

- Lose 1 Cultivation Point, if it has any.

A creature with no Cultivation Points instead takes additional Force damage equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus.

Hollow the Weapon

Choose one weapon, shield, implement, or Domain Armament the target is wielding, carrying, or actively controlling.

The target makes a Charisma saving throw.

Failed Save:

- The item’s cultivated properties are suppressed until the start of your next turn.
- A floating Domain Armament immediately falls or becomes inert in its current space.

Successful Save:

- One named active property is suppressed until the end of the current turn.

The physical item remains present and is not duplicated or destroyed.

tianxia.subpath.qi.void_touched_cultivat.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 — Erase

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 6 Qi

Choose Erase Manifestation, Erase Substance, or Erase Cultivation.

Erase Manifestation

Choose one visible active manifestation, including:

- A field.
- A wall.
- A barrier.
- A summoned asset.
- A projected weapon.
- A Formation function.
- A talisman effect.
- A transformation.
- A possession tether.
- A temporary technique construct.
- A persistent area.

Resolve authority:

- Non-Secret Source CL lower than yours: erase it immediately.
- Equal Source CL: make a Cultivation Check against its save DC. On success, erase it.
- Higher Source CL or Secret authority: make a Cultivation Check against its save DC. On success, suppress it for 1 minute. If you exceed its Source CL, erase it instead.

Erasing a manifestation:

- Ends the selected manifestation and its dependent functions.
- Does not refund costs.
- Does not erase the creator, underlying learned technique, permanent item, or cultivation system unless the manifestation itself is that system’s only physical vessel.
- Cannot permanently erase an artifact unless the artifact explicitly can be destroyed by Void authority.

Erase Substance

Choose one unattended object, structure section, Construct, Cultivation Asset, corpse without an active spirit, or nonliving material within range.

The target takes:

10d10 Void damage.

This damage:

- Ignores ordinary Resistance and Damage Threshold.
- Treats ordinary Immunity as Resistance.
- Deals double damage to temporary barriers, summoned objects, Formation Anchors, vehicles, and structures.

A nonartifact unattended object or material section no larger than a 15-foot cube whose Source CL is lower than yours is erased completely if reduced to 0 Hit Points.

A living creature, active-soul corpse, unwilling sentient item, artifact, or Secret Anchor cannot be targeted by Erase Substance.

Erase Cultivation

Choose one creature bearing at least 2 Void Marks.

It makes a Charisma saving throw.

Failed Save:

- Take 8d8 Void damage.
- Lose current Cultivation Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus.
- Choose one cultivation system: Sphere, Subpath, Method, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, Domain Armament, Foundation active system, Path recovery engine, or one named Secret/Immortal feature.
- The chosen system is erased from active use for 1 minute.

Successful Save:

- Take half damage.
- Lose Cultivation Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
- The chosen system is suppressed until the start of its next turn.

Deep Erasure

Spend 3 Void Marks instead of 2 when activating Erase Cultivation.

On a failed save:

- A target whose Source CL is 3–5 lower remains unable to use the chosen system until it completes a successful recovery procedure.
- A target whose Source CL is at least 6 lower may have the chosen system erased indefinitely.
- A target within 2 CL suffers the normal 1-minute duration and repeats the save at the end of each turn after the first, ending the erasure on a success.
- A target 3 or more CL higher suffers suppression until the end of its next turn unless you also succeed on a Cultivation Check against its save DC.

Recovery from Deep Erasure

Deep Erasure can be reversed by:

- An equal- or higher-CL Void, Samsara, Conceptual Severance, Karma, restoration, or cultivation-reconstruction authority.
- A successful breakthrough explicitly rebuilding the erased system.
- A major Cultivation Session using the original complete inheritance or manual and a specialist whose Source CL equals or exceeds yours.
- An artifact, ancestor, Immortal, or equivalent authority capable of restoring erased cultivation.
- A release condition established by the story source of the Secret Law.

Ordinary rest, healing, Qi recovery, or retraining does not restore an erased system.

---
