tianxia.subpath.qi.heaven_splitting_conc.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 — Sever Attribute

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 5 Qi

Choose one creature, object, Cultivation Asset, or active manifestation bearing at least 1 Severance Mark.

Choose one attribute currently possessed by the target.

An unwilling creature makes a Charisma saving throw.

On failure, sever the attribute for the duration.

On success, sever it until the start of its next turn.

Eligible attributes include:

- One movement mode, such as flight, swimming, burrowing, teleportation, or Earth Glide.
- One Resistance.
- One Immunity, which becomes Resistance rather than being completely removed unless your Source CL exceeds the target by at least 3.
- Regeneration or automatic healing.
- Incorporeal movement.
- Invisible.
- One elemental tag or damage conversion.
- One sense, such as Truesight, Tremorsense, or Qi Sensing.
- One weapon property or item property.
- One aura or field-following property.
- One size increase, transformation trait, or manifested limb.
- One Sphere.
- One Method benefit.
- One Golden Core Form.
- One Nascent Soul feature.
- One Domain Armament mode.
- One Foundation active benefit.

Attribute Remains, Relation Ends

Sever Attribute does not erase the underlying source.

Examples:

- A wing remains visible but no longer connects to flight.
- Fire remains present but no longer connects to heat or Fire damage.
- A sword remains magical but no longer connects to one property.
- A cultivator still knows a Sphere but cannot connect it to active use.
- A Golden Core remains intact but cannot express one Form.

Major-System Severance

To sever a complete Sphere, Method, Golden Core, Nascent Soul feature set, Domain Armament system, Subpath, or Foundation active system:

- The target must bear at least 2 Severance Marks.
- Spend 2 marks when activating.
- A target within 2 CL repeats the Charisma saving throw at the end of each turn, ending the major severance on a success.
- A target 3–5 CL lower receives no automatic repeat for the duration.
- A target at least 6 CL lower may suffer an indefinite severance when you spend 2 additional Qi.
- A target 3 or more CL higher requires a successful Cultivation Check against its save DC after it fails the save.

Restoring an Attribute

An indefinite severance requires:

- Reconnection through an equal/higher Conceptual Severance or restoration authority.
- Reconstruction through the original inheritance, item, body, or cultivation source.
- A breakthrough explicitly reconnecting the system.
- Samsara return to a state before severance.
- Karma or Fate authority proving and restoring the relation.
- An artifact, Immortal, ancestor, or equivalent source.

Ordinary rest does not reconnect an indefinite severance.

- A summoned servant’s bond.
- An oath witness.

You learn all six Foundational Formulas.

Establish Incense Pavilion

- Source CL: Your CL

Cultivation Level 10 — Chain of Cause and Effect

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required  
Cost: 5 Qi

Choose two creatures, or one creature and one Cultivation Asset, object, location, wound, condition, stolen property, or active effect with a genuine causal connection.

Each unwilling creature makes a Charisma saving throw.

- If both succeed, the Chain fails and 2 Qi is refunded.
- If at least one fails, establish the Chain.
- A willing target may accept without a save.

Choose one Chain form.

Chain of Shared Wounds

Once per turn when one chained creature takes damage, the other takes damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus of one type from the triggering packet.

Spend 1 Burden from the damage source to increase the returned damage to:

2d8 + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier

The second damage cannot trigger this Chain again.

Chain of Shared Restoration

Once per turn when one chained creature regains Hit Points or Cultivation Points, the other receives:

- Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus; or
- 1 Cultivation Point when the triggering restoration included Cultivation Points.

Spend 1 Merit from the source to increase healing to 2d8 + your modifier or Cultivation Point restoration to 2.

Chain of Pursuit

When one chained creature moves or teleports, move the other up to 10 feet toward it.

An unwilling creature makes a Strength or Charisma saving throw each time.

On success, it is not moved.

Chain of Condition

When one chained creature gains Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned, Restrained, Stunned, or another condition approved by the Source Rule, the other makes a Charisma saving throw.

On failure, it gains the same condition until the end of its next turn.

A Secret, permanent, identity, death, or complete-cultivation condition requires a successful Cultivation Check against the original effect’s save DC.

Chain of Consequence

Connect one creature to one actual victim, damaged object, stolen property, transferred condition, or active consequence you can perceive.

While chained:

- When the creature repeats the same category of harmful cause, it gains 2 Burden Marks.
- When it genuinely repairs, returns, restores, releases, or accepts the consequence, it gains 2 Merit Marks.
- It cannot conceal that it is the cause, substitute another victim, or redirect the consequence through a lower-Source-CL effect.
- Once per turn, you may use Return the Deed on an event involving the linked consequence without spending Qi, though the matching mark is still spent.

The Chain does not create an oath, contract, property right, moral rule, or legal duty. It follows a causal relationship that already exists.

Severing the Chain

A chained creature may use an Action to make a Cultivation Check against your save DC.

On success, end the Chain for itself.

A creature at least 3 CL lower cannot attempt this check unless:

- It possesses Karma, Fate, Oath, Void, Name, or conceptual authority.
- The other chained target is destroyed, released, or voluntarily breaks the connection.
- An ally uses an appropriate counter-technique.

Cultivation Level 18 — Heavenly Ripening of Karma

Action  
Area: 40-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder centered on you or your Domain Armament  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

A visible network of red, gold, black, white, or otherwise culturally expressed causal threads fills the field.

For the duration:

- Every creature in the field bears a Karmic Imprint whether or not it consents, promised anything, or entered a contract.
- You perceive all Burden and Merit events occurring inside.
- Gain 1 additional Burden or Merit when a qualifying event occurs, once per creature per round.
- Return the Deed costs 0 Qi once per round.
- Chain of Cause and Effect can connect up to three targets.
- Matured Fruits require no Concentration and can coexist.
- A creature cannot conceal a causal source, transferred consequence, substituted victim, or false attribution from you through a non-Secret effect whose Source CL is lower than yours.

Ripen Merit

At the start of each of your turns, choose one creature with at least 2 Merit.

Spend any number of its Merit and grant one benefit per mark spent:

- Restore 2d8 Hit Points.
- Restore 1 Cultivation Point.
- Grant Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus.
- End one non-Secret Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned, Restrained, or possession effect whose Source CL is no higher than yours.
- Move it 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Grant Advantage on its next attack, check, or saving throw.

A creature can receive each benefit once per turn.

Ripen Burden

At the start of each of your turns, choose one creature with at least 2 Burden.

Spend any number of its Burden and impose one consequence per mark spent:

- Deal 2d8 Force, Psychic, Radiant, or Necrotic damage.
- Remove 1 current Cultivation Point.
- Reduce Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
- Prevent Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Suppress one active technique until the start of its next turn.
- Move it 10 feet toward a recorded victim, damaged object, stolen property, or consequence.

A creature can suffer each consequence once per turn.

Fruit Cannot Escape the Seed

Once during the activation, choose one creature in the field with at least 4 Burden, 4 Merit, or a combined total of 6 marks.

An unwilling target makes a Charisma saving throw.

Failed Save — Burden Judgment

Choose one:

Return All Harm

The target takes damage equal to the total damage it directly dealt to other creatures during the current scene, to a maximum of:

15d10

Choose damage types represented among those events.

Return the Stolen Fruit

Every item, active technique, Cultivation Point, memory, emotion, lifespan portion, cultivation feature, or other property the target stole or seized during the current scene returns to its original owner or lawful state when your Source CL equals or exceeds the theft authority.

Higher-authority theft is suppressed for 1 minute instead.

Close the Harmful Engine

Suppress all Path, Subpath, Sphere, Method, Foundation active, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, Domain Armament, Recorded Art, Forged Technique, Immortal Art, and cultivated-item activations.

Duration:

- Within 2 CL: until the end of its next turn, then repeated Charisma saves at the end of each turn.
- 3–5 CL lower: 1 minute with no automatic repeat.
- At least 6 CL lower: until the end of the scene, the recorded harm is genuinely repaired, or equal/higher authority releases it.
- 3+ CL higher: until the start of its next turn unless you also succeed on a Cultivation Check against its save DC.

Transfer the Consequence

Choose one recorded victim, bearer of a transferred consequence, or rightful owner of stolen property.

Transfer one wound, condition, maximum-Hit-Point reduction, Cultivation Point loss, stolen property, curse, oath consequence, or other karmically linked burden from that creature to the judged target.

A Secret or permanent burden requires a Cultivation Check against its Source DC.

Failed Save — Merit Judgment

Choose one:

Restore the Benefactor

The target regains all Hit Points and Cultivation Points, ends non-Secret hostile conditions whose Source CL is no higher than yours, and gains Temporary Hit Points equal to 5 × your Proficiency Bonus.

Return the Sacrifice

Restore one item, memory, emotion, lifespan portion, cultivation feature, or other genuine sacrifice the target paid for another creature, provided it still exists within Karma and was not erased by higher authority.

Heavenly Protection

For 1 minute, the target gains:

- Resistance to all damage except Force, Psychic, and Void.
- Advantage on all saving throws.
- Immunity to forced possession and unwilling cultivation theft from a Source CL lower than yours.

Carry Merit Forward

Move any number of the target’s Merit Marks to another willing creature and immediately Ripen them without using an action.

Successful Save

- Burden target loses Cultivation Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Merit target regains 4d8 + your modifier Hit Points and gains Advantage on its next saving throw.

Breaking a Heavenly Judgment

A persistent Burden Judgment can be broken by:

- Genuinely repairing, returning, releasing, or accepting the recorded consequence.
- Equal/higher Karma, Fate, Samsara, Void, Name, Oath, or Conceptual Severance authority.
- A major heavenly tribulation or breakthrough explicitly settling the causal thread.
- Proving through real supernatural authority that the recorded cause was false, transferred, or erased.
- Accepting an equivalent consequence approved by the Judgment’s causal structure.

A promise, contract, political pardon, legal acquittal, or disagreement does not automatically alter cultivated Karma. Only the actual cause, consequence, transferred burden, or a superior causal authority changes the thread.

Range: 60 feet  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 6 Qi

Choose one creature bearing at least 2 Burden Marks or 2 Merit Marks whose relevant causal events you perceived or established through reliable supernatural evidence.

The target makes a Charisma saving throw if unwilling.

On a failed save, establish one Matured Fruit tied to an actual recorded cause.

On a successful save, the Fruit lasts until the start of your next turn and uses only its lesser result.

Fruit of Violence

Cause: The target damages another creature.

Consequence:

- Spend 1 Burden.
- It takes 3d8 Force, Psychic, or Radiant damage.
- It cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Lesser Result: Damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

Fruit of Theft

Cause: The target takes, controls, stores, binds, or uses an item, resource, technique, or Cultivation Asset belonging to another creature without valid consent or authority.

Consequence:

- Spend 1 Burden.
- The stolen target immediately returns to its rightful holder, previous location, or nearest legal space when your Source CL equals or exceeds the theft effect.
- Otherwise, the stealing function is suppressed until the start of the target’s next turn.

Lesser Result: The target cannot activate the stolen property until the start of its next turn.

Fruit of Betrayal

Cause: The target directly harms a creature whose aid, healing, protection, or sacrifice materially enabled the target during the current scene.

Consequence:

- Spend 2 Burden.
- One Sphere, Subpath, Method, Domain Armament, or active cultivation system used in the betrayal is suppressed until the end of its next turn.

Lesser Result: The triggering technique costs additional Cultivation Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If it cannot pay, the activation fails without cost.

Fruit of Restitution

Cause: The target restores, repays, releases, protects, or accepts a consequence for another creature.

Consequence:

- Spend 1 Merit.
- It regains 3d8 + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier Hit Points.
- It regains 2 Cultivation Points.
- It may move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Lesser Result: It gains Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus.

Fruit of Accepted Burden

Cause: The target willingly takes damage, a condition, a cost, a contract consequence, or a tribulation meant for another creature.

Consequence:

- Spend 2 Merit.
- Reduce the accepted consequence by half.
- End one non-Secret hostile condition on the target when its Source CL is no higher than yours.
- It gains Advantage on its next saving throw before the end of its next turn.

Lesser Result: Reduce the triggering damage by twice your Proficiency Bonus.

Fruit of Cultivation Abuse

Cause: The target uses a named cultivation system to repeat or preserve a recorded harm while bearing at least 3 Burden.

Consequence:

- Spend 3 Burden.
- Choose the system used by the triggering cause: Sphere, Subpath, Method, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, Domain Armament, Foundation active system, Recorded Art family, cultivated item, or Path resource engine.
- Suppress that system for 1 minute.
- A target 3–5 CL lower receives no automatic repeated save.
- A target at least 6 CL lower remains suppressed until the end of the scene or until it genuinely repairs, releases, returns, or accepts the recorded consequence.
- A target 3 or more CL higher is suppressed only until the start of its next turn unless you also succeed on a Cultivation Check against its save DC.

You do not invent a contractual restitution term. The release must causally address the recorded harm or be imposed by equal/higher Karma, Fate, Samsara, Void, Name, or Conceptual authority.

Lesser Result: The system is suppressed until the start of the target’s next turn.

Persistent Fruit

Against a target 3–5 CL lower, a failed-save Fruit can last beyond 1 minute until its consequence occurs once or the recorded causal harm is genuinely resolved.

Against a target at least 6 CL lower, a Fruit expressly marked as persistent can remain until the recorded consequence is genuinely resolved or equal/higher authority breaks the thread.

Against a target 3 or more CL higher, you must also succeed on a Cultivation Check against its save DC for any Fruit to last beyond the start of your next turn.

CL18 — Banquet of Ten Thousand Tables

Ritual Time: 1 hour  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Ingredients: At least ten complete Meal Portions and any rare ingredients required by chosen Courses  
Targets: Up to 100 × your CL willing creatures that attend and consume a portion  
Duration: 24 hours  
Limit: Once per Cultivation Session

You establish a strategic-scale cultivated banquet, war commissary, sect feast, relief kitchen, shipboard provision rite, or ancestral table.

Each target gains:

- Two Meal Courses of its choice.
- One Body-Forging Course of its choice.
- Immunity to ordinary hunger, thirst, food spoilage, and environmental sickness for the duration.
- Advantage against Exhaustion from travel, forced marching, carrying loads, exposure, and physical overexertion.
- One Heavenly Ration carried within the body as cultivated nourishment.

Heavenly Ration

A creature may consume its Heavenly Ration without using an action when one of the following occurs:

- It is reduced to 0 Hit Points without being killed outright.
- It fails a Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, or death saving throw.
- It gains a level of Exhaustion from physical exertion, exposure, hunger, thirst, poison, or disease.
- It begins its turn with fewer than half its Hit Points.

Choose one result:

- Become Stable, regain 4d8 + your key ability modifier Hit Points, and stand if physically able.
- Turn the failed saving throw into a success when the opposing Source CL is no higher than yours; against higher authority, reroll with Advantage.
- Prevent the triggering level of Exhaustion.
- Regain 4d8 + your key ability modifier Hit Points and Temporary Hit Points equal to 3 × Proficiency Bonus.

A Heavenly Ration disappears when used or when the Banquet duration ends. It is not a separate item and cannot be stolen or transferred after the feast.

No Army Starves

For 30 days after the Banquet, its Camp Kitchen Anchor can produce enough ordinary preserved food and clean water for 100 × your CL creatures each day, provided at least one Supply Unit, seed stock, hunted game, harvested crop, or other genuine food source is supplied each day.

This multiplies and preserves logistics; it does not create unlimited matter from nothing.

Feast Before Battle

Once before the 24-hour duration ends, a target may use a Bonus Action to awaken the Banquet’s martial nourishment for 1 minute:

- Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 5 × Proficiency Bonus.
- Ignore Difficult Terrain caused by rubble, mud, snow, vegetation, or bodies.
- Gain Advantage on Strength and Constitution checks and saving throws.
- The first time each turn it hits with a weapon attack or bodily cultivation technique, add 1d8 damage.

A creature can awaken Feast Before Battle once per Banquet.

Banquet of Ten Thousand Tables does not diagnose hidden conditions, reveal lies, conduct precision purification, or provide reaction-based correction. Those are Tea-Sage authorities.

CL18 — Heaven-Sealing Edict

Action  
Range: 90 feet  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene  
Saving Throw: Charisma

Choose one visible creature. Three immense Seal Pillars appear in legal unoccupied spaces within 30 feet of it. Each Pillar is an Anchor and bears one named binding:

1. Outer Heaven Pillar — movement, teleportation, flight, phasing, possession, and remote origins.
2. Meridian Pillar — Cultivation Point expenditure and recovery, Sphere techniques, weapon-delivered cultivation, and Domain Armament functions.
3. Core Pillar — Path, Subpath, Method, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, Foundation active systems, cultivated-item activations, Recorded Arts, Forged Techniques, and Immortal Arts.

Seal Pillar Profile

- Size: Medium object
- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 6 × your CL each
- Resistance: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from noncultivated attacks
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic damage
- Source CL: Your CL
- Movement: None

A Pillar must be placed on a legal surface or in a legal Formation position. If no legal space exists for all three, the activation fails before Qi is spent.

Initial Resistance

The target makes one Charisma saving throw.

Successful Save

Only the Outer Heaven Pillar binds the target until the start of your next turn. The other two Pillars still appear but do not bind unless the target fails a later Edict save.

Failed Save

The target is bound by a number of Pillars based on authority and preparation:

- Within 2 CL or higher: Outer Heaven and Meridian Pillars.
- 3–5 CL lower: All three Pillars.
- At least 6 CL lower, Completely Subdued, or already bearing your Core Seal: All three Pillars, and Core Pillar imposes Complete Cultivation Suppression.

At the end of each of its turns, a target within 2 CL of you or higher repeats the Charisma save. On success, suppress one active Pillar of its choice until the end of its next turn.

A target 3–5 CL lower repeats the save at the end of every second turn. A target at least 6 CL lower receives no automatic repeat save.

Binding Effects

For each active Pillar:

- Outer Heaven: Speed is 0; the target cannot willingly teleport, fly, phase, become Incorporeal, possess, or use a remote technique origin outside its space.
- Meridian: The target cannot spend or regain Cultivation Points, use Sphere techniques, weapon-delivered techniques, or Domain Armament functions.
- Core: The target cannot activate Path, Subpath, Method, Foundation active, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, cultivated-item, Recorded Art, Forged Technique, Immortal Art, or transformation features.

When all three are active, the target suffers Complete Cultivation Suppression under the shared rule.

Break a Pillar

A Pillar ends when reduced to 0 Hit Points, lawfully displaced outside 60 feet of the target, or overcome by an equal- or higher-authority seal-breaking effect.

A creature adjacent to a Pillar may use an Action to attempt a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC. On success, deal Force damage to the Pillar equal to 5 × that creature’s Proficiency Bonus, ignoring resistance.

The bound target may use Break the Seal against one active Pillar. On success, suppress that Pillar until the end of its next turn. A second consecutive success destroys the binding between that Pillar and the target, though the physical Pillar remains until the Edict ends.

Direct Binding, Not a Puzzle

Knowing the Pillars’ names, observing their order, or guessing their inscription does not remove them. There is no Master Key or cognitive solution. The Edict ends through destroyed Anchors, failed Concentration, seal-breaking authority, a printed release clause, or superior Source CL.

Sealed Passage

A creature or effect cannot teleport, phase, summon, or project through the triangle defined by the three Pillars when its Source CL is lower than yours. Equal or higher authority requires a Cultivation Check against your save DC.

- Hit Points: 4 × your Qi Cultivation CL

Successful Save:

- The target takes half damage.

Ritual Time: 10 minutes  
Range: Touch  
Cost: 2 Qi  
Target: One sleeping, dreaming, Unconscious, Incapacitated, Restrained, Completely Subdued, or willing creature with genuine consciousness

Cultivation Level 14 - Avalanche Meridian Circuit

Your maximum Momentum becomes Proficiency Bonus + 3.

When the normal Momentum rules would grant 1 Momentum, gain 2 instead. A feature directly stating "gain 1 Momentum," such as Store the Collision, still grants exactly 1 unless stated otherwise.

When using Gather and Return, spend between 1 and 3 Momentum. For each Momentum spent, choose one benefit:

- Add one Gather and Return damage die.
- Increase the attack's push by 5 feet.

Normalized Procedure — Avalanche Meridian Circuit

- Replace maximum Momentum with Proficiency Bonus + 3.
- The once-per-round normal Momentum grant becomes 2. A feature directly saying “gain 1 Momentum” remains 1 and is not doubled.
- At this level, Gather and Return's cost and option procedure is replaced: spend 1, 2, or 3 Momentum and make one selection for each point spent from the three printed benefits.
- Each damage selection adds one die of Gather and Return's current size (2d8 at Cultivation Level 14 and 3d8 only when the base feature reaches Cultivation Level 17). Multiple selections add multiple dice.
- The first push selection creates a 5-foot push; each additional push selection adds 5 feet. The push remains directly away unless another rule permits a different direction.
- Each movement selection grants 5 feet of voluntary movement without Opportunity Attacks after the hit. Combine multiple selections into one movement of the total distance or divide them into legal segments during that resolution.
- You may repeat any printed selection. The Cultivation Level 3 +1 AC option is not among Avalanche Meridian Circuit's printed selection list and is unavailable when using this replaced procedure.

Movement: Up to 120 feet in a straight line

Move to an unoccupied space you can see along the line without provoking Opportunity Attacks. You may move through hostile creature spaces, but not through total cover, a sealed Formation, spatial lock, or solid barrier that survives the damage.

Each creature whose space the line crosses or that is within 5 feet of it makes a Dexterity saving throw.

Damage equals 6d10 Force + 1d10 per Momentum spent.

- Failed Save: Full damage, pushed up to 20 feet perpendicular to the line, knocked Prone, and no Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Successful Save: Half damage, pushed 5 feet, and remains standing.

A creature can take this damage only once per use. Unattended objects, temporary barriers, vehicles, structures, terrain sections, and Formation Anchors take double damage.

If a barrier survives, your movement ends before it and you take Force damage equal to twice your CL. Stamina Guard may reduce this recoil, but no Momentum feature can reduce it or generate Momentum from it.

The destination becomes a 10-foot-radius impact zone of Difficult Terrain until cleared or repaired.

---

Normalized Procedure — Heaven-Returning Impact

- Confirm at least 3 Momentum, choose a visible unoccupied legal destination on a straight line within 120 feet, then pay 5 Stamina and all current Momentum. Record the Momentum spent before rolling damage.
- The line has your normal occupied width unless the map requires a 5-foot-wide line. You travel along it without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Hostile creature spaces are passable; total cover, a surviving solid barrier, sealed Formation, or spatial lock is not.
- Resolve every creature's save once. A creature whose space intersects the line and is also within 5 feet of it still takes damage only once.
- Damage is one 6d10 + 1d10 per Momentum spent Force packet. On failure, you choose one of the two perpendicular directions and push up to 20 feet along a legal route; on success, push 5 feet in the chosen perpendicular direction.
- Resolve eligible objects, structures, terrain sections, vehicles, barriers, and Formation Anchors as the line reaches them. Apply double damage once. If a solid barrier is destroyed by the activation, movement can continue; if it survives, movement ends in the nearest legal space before it.
- Recoil from a surviving barrier is one Force packet equal to twice your CL. Stamina Guard can reduce it. No Momentum feature can reduce, prevent, redirect, absorb, or generate Momentum from that recoil.
- The destination impact zone consists of the bounded 10-foot radius of ordinary damaged ground. It remains Difficult Terrain until cleared or repaired under the shared damaged-terrain procedure.

---

tianxia.subpath.body.returning_heaven_mo.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Rebounding Assault

Reaction  
You can use this when  A hostile creature within 60 feet moves you, misses you with a melee attack, or damages you with a melee attack.  
Cost: 2 Momentum  
Limit: Once per round

After the triggering effect resolves, move up to your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. You may move through the triggering creature's space as Difficult Terrain and must end closer to it.

If you end within unarmed reach, make one unarmed strike. On a hit, deal additional Force damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus and either push the target 10 feet or knock it Prone.

The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.

Normalized Procedure — Rebounding Assault

- The trigger occurs after the hostile movement, missed melee attack, or damaging melee attack fully resolves. A single hostile activation can trigger this feature only once.
- Move through the triggering creature's space as Difficult Terrain only if you have enough movement and can legally pass through its space under this feature. You cannot end in its space.
- Every movement segment must end closer to the triggering creature than the immediately preceding position; the final space must also be closer than your starting space. If no legal closer movement exists, the movement ends.
- The unarmed strike occurs after movement if the target remains within reach. It follows the Granted Attack rule.
- On a hit, Proficiency Bonus Force damage is part of the attack packet. Then choose either a 10-foot push directly away or Prone. No collision damage is created unless another rule expressly supplies it.

tianxia.subpath.body.ryujin.feature.drag.player_text:
Cultivation Level 6 - Dragon's Breath

Action  
Area: 15-foot cone  
Cost: 2 Stamina  
Saving Throw: Dexterity

Choose Lightning or Thunder damage.

On a failed save, a creature takes 4d6 damage, increasing to 6d6 at Cultivation Level 11 and 8d6 at Cultivation Level 17. On a successful save, it takes half damage.

Unattended fragile objects automatically fail the save.

Normalized Procedure — Dragon's Breath

- Choose Lightning or Thunder when activating the feature. Every damage roll from that activation uses the chosen type.
- The cone originates from your mouth or another recorded breath organ and requires an unobstructed line of effect. It is a bodily projection exception with the printed 15-foot area and does not create a lingering cloud or Field.
- Each creature in the cone makes one save and takes damage once. A creature occupying more than one space in the cone is still affected only once.
- “Unattended fragile object” means a discrete, unworn, uncarried object that the GM has classified as readily breakable, such as ordinary glass, pottery, paper, thin wood, or comparable material. It automatically fails but retains Immunities and Damage Thresholds. Other objects are affected only when their own rules permit the breath to damage them.
- Cover and line of effect are checked from the breath's point of origin. The breath does not pass through total cover.

tianxia.subpath.body.ryujin.feature.drag.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Dragon's Roar

Action  
Area: 30-foot cone  
Cost: 5 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene  
Saving Throw: Constitution

On a failed save, a creature takes 5d8 Thunder damage and is Stunned until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.

Unattended objects, temporary barriers, and Formation Anchors in the cone take double damage.

Normalized Procedure — Dragon's Roar

- The cone originates from your body and requires line of effect. Each creature in it makes one Constitution save.
- Stunned and Reaction denial begin after damage is resolved and last exactly as printed. A creature that succeeds is not Stunned.
- An eligible unattended object, temporary barrier, or Formation Anchor takes one damage instance and applies the printed doubling once, even if it belongs to more than one listed category.
- Worn, carried, wielded, piloted, or actively controlled objects are not unattended. Artifact objects and world-scale structures retain their own authority and are not automatically destroyed.
- The roar is a Sound- and body-origin effect. Silence or a rule that specifically blocks supernatural sound can contest or prevent it only to the extent printed by that rule; ordinary ambient noise does not.

tianxia.subpath.body.ryujin.feature.drag.player_text:
Cultivation Level 3 - Dragon Scales

While benefiting from Unarmored Defense, gain +1 AC and Resistance to Lightning damage.

Once per turn when you hit with an unarmed strike, deal additional Lightning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

Normalized Procedure — Dragon Scales

- The +1 AC is an AC bonus that applies only while Unarmored Defense is the formula currently determining your AC. It does not apply while armor or a replacement AC formula is used.
- Lightning Resistance is a bodily inheritance and remains active while conscious or Unconscious unless an effect specifically suppresses this feature or your Body Refining cultivation.
- The once-per-turn Lightning damage is part of the triggering unarmed strike's damage packet. It applies after the hit is confirmed, cannot critically multiply separately, and cannot trigger another on-hit rider by itself.
- Scales may be visible or concealable as established by the character's recorded anatomy. Visibility has no additional mechanical consequence unless another rule expressly refers to it.

tianxia.subpath.body.ryujin.feature.stor.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Storm Step

Bonus Action  
Range: 30 feet  
Cost: 3 Stamina

Teleport to an unoccupied space you can see.

Each hostile creature of your choice within 5 feet of the destination makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes 2d6 Lightning or Thunder damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and retains its Reactions.

Storm Step cannot cross a spatial lock, sealed planar boundary, Formation explicitly blocking teleportation, or total planar separation.

Normalized Procedure — Storm Step

- Select the destination and damage type when activating the feature. The destination must be an unoccupied legal space you can see on the same plane and within 30 feet.
- Storm Step is teleportation. It does not trace a movement path, does not provoke Opportunity Attacks, and does not count as crossing intervening spaces.
- If a spatial lock, sealed planar boundary, qualifying Formation, total planar separation, or another explicit prohibition blocks the destination, use Failed Spatial Movement. The arrival burst does not occur when the teleport fails.
- After arriving, choose any number of hostile creatures within 5 feet of the destination. Each chosen creature saves once. A creature cannot be affected more than once by the same Storm Step even if it occupies multiple spaces.
- Reaction denial begins after the save resolves. The feature does not reveal hidden creatures; you can choose only hostile creatures you can identify as valid targets through your current senses or another legal targeting rule.

tianxia.subpath.body.seven_coiled_serpen.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Fifth Coil: Ascending Serpent

While open:

- Climb Speed equal to Speed.
- Jump distances quadrupled.
- Move across liquids and vertical surfaces during your turn.
- Once per turn after moving 15 feet, your next unarmed strike has Advantage.

On a hit with that attack, spend 1 Stamina. The target makes a Strength save. On a failure, throw it 20 feet; on a success, push 5 feet.

A target thrown into another creature causes both to take Bludgeoning damage equal to Proficiency Bonus; the second creature avoids it on a successful Dexterity save.

Normalized Procedure — Ascending Serpent

- Climb Speed equals current walking Speed. Quadruple jump distances after ordinary jump calculations. During your turn you can move across liquids and vertical surfaces while movement remains; if unsupported when movement ends, resolve falling immediately.
- Once per turn, after you have physically moved at least 15 feet during the current turn, record Advantage on your next unarmed strike before the end of that turn. Teleportation does not count unless expressly treated as movement.
- After that advantaged strike hits, you may spend 1 Stamina. The target makes one Strength save. On failure, throw it up to 20 feet in a direction you choose along a legal trajectory. On success, push it 5 feet directly away from you.
- A throw or push stops at the nearest legal space before a solid obstruction. If the failed-save target first enters another creature's space and cannot continue, both creatures take Bludgeoning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus; the second creature makes one Dexterity save and takes no collision damage on success. Resolve one second-creature collision only.
- The thrown target takes its collision damage automatically. Collision damage does not create Prone, an Injury, another throw, or repeated contacts unless another Source Rule says so.

tianxia.subpath.body.seven_coiled_serpen.player_text:
Cultivation Level 3 - First and Second Coils

- Root Serpent: Advantage against Grappled, Shoved, and Prone; standing costs 5 feet.
- Swift Serpent: Speed +10 feet; once per turn after a hit, move 5 feet without provoking.

Normalized Procedure — First and Second Coils

- Root Serpent: Advantage applies to checks and saves made to avoid, resist, or escape Grappled, Shoved, or Prone. Standing from Prone costs 5 feet of movement regardless of current Speed, unless Speed is 0.
- Swift Serpent: Add 10 feet to walking Speed. Once per turn after one attack hits, move up to 5 feet without provoking along a legal route. The movement occurs after the hit resolves and does not require an unarmed strike.
- Each benefit operates only while its Coil remains open. Closing Swift Serpent does not retract movement already completed.

tianxia.subpath.body.seven_coiled_serpen.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Sixth Coil: Crowned Serpent

While open:

- Blindsight 20 feet.
- Advantage against Charmed and Frightened.
- Cannot be Surprised while conscious.
- Unarmed reach +5 feet during your turn.

Once per round when a hostile creature within Blindsight moves or teleports, spend 1 Stamina to move 10 feet without provoking, ending closer to it.

Normalized Procedure — Crowned Serpent

- Blindsight functions within 20 feet through the senses of your cultivated body. It does not see through total cover, identify a creature beyond the sense's range, or automatically reveal a creature protected by stronger supernatural concealment.
- Advantage applies to saves made to avoid or end Charmed and Frightened. You cannot be Surprised while conscious, following the finalized Surprise procedure.
- The +5-foot unarmed reach applies only during your turn and does not enlarge threatened space outside your turn.
- Once per round, after a hostile creature that was within your Blindsight at the start or end of its movement or teleportation finishes that movement, you may spend 1 Stamina to move up to 10 feet without provoking.
- Your movement is physical, follows a legal route, and must end closer to that creature than you began. If no legal destination is closer, you cannot activate the movement. The feature does not follow the creature through a teleport, grant its destination, or bypass total cover.

tianxia.subpath.body.seven_coiled_serpen.player_text:
Cultivation Level 6 - Third and Fourth Coils

- Crushing Serpent: Count as one size larger while Grappling; at start of each turn deal Constitution modifier damage to a Grappled creature; drag at full Speed if no more than one size larger.
- Striking Serpent: Once per turn on a hit, additional 1d8 Bludgeoning or Force, or 2d8 if the target is Grappled by you.

Normalized Procedure — Third and Fourth Coils

- Crushing Serpent: Functional size increases by one category only for initiating, maintaining, escaping, and dragging a Grapple. At the start of each of your turns, choose one creature currently Grappled by you; it takes Bludgeoning damage equal to Constitution modifier, minimum 0. This is not an attack and does not trigger hit riders.
- While dragging no more than one Grappled creature that is no more than one size category larger than your actual or applicable functional size, your Speed is not halved by the ordinary Grapple drag rule. Terrain and other movement penalties still apply.
- Striking Serpent: Once per turn after any hit, add 1d8 Bludgeoning or Force to that hit's packet, or 2d8 if the target is currently Grappled by you when damage is applied. Choose damage type on use. It cannot critically multiply separately.
- The once-per-turn damage remains one total use across all attacks and turns normally reset it.

tianxia.subpath.body.shinobi.feature.ass.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Assassination

You can use this when  You hit a creature when it is Surprised, has not yet acted during the first round, you were Invisible to it, or you were Heavily Obscured from it.  
Limit: Once per turn

Deal additional damage equal to 2d8 + your CL.

Then choose one:

- It cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Apply Pressure-Point Strike without spending Stamina.
- Gain Advantage on your next Stealth check before the end of your next turn.

Normalized Procedure — Assassination
- Check the trigger at the moment the attack hits. Satisfying more than one listed circumstance does not multiply the benefit.
- “Has not yet acted during the first round” means the target has not taken a turn, action, Bonus Action, or Reaction after Initiative was rolled for that scene. A creature that acted before its first turn no longer qualifies under that clause.
- Invisible or Heavily Obscured status is evaluated from the target's perception, not globally. A creature that perceives you normally does not qualify under those clauses.
- The additional 2d8 + CL is one damage packet of the triggering attack's damage type unless that attack has multiple types, in which case choose one type dealt by it.
- The movement occurs after the hit, is granted movement, and does not provoke. The free Pressure-Point Strike spends no Stamina but still requires its save, uses its normal effect, and cannot exceed once per turn.
- Advantage on the next Stealth check is expended on that check and expires at the end of your next turn.

tianxia.subpath.body.shinobi.feature.pre.player_text:
Cultivation Level 6 - Pressure-Point Strike

You can use this when  You hit with an unarmed strike.  
Cost: 1 Stamina  
Limit: Once per turn  
Saving Throw: Constitution

On a failed save, choose one:

- No Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
- Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of its next turn.
- Disadvantage on its next Concentration saving throw before the start of its next turn.
- It cannot speak above a whisper until the start of its next turn.

On a successful save, it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Normalized Procedure — Pressure-Point Strike
- Choose the failed-save effect after the target fails unless the table requires declarations before saves; record the choice and duration. These are temporary physical disruptions, not Injuries or permanent meridian damage.
- The effect can apply to nonhumanoid anatomy through an equivalent vulnerable function unless an explicit immunity blocks that exact impairment.
- A target unable to speak above a whisper can communicate quietly, but cannot produce a command, shout, projected voice, audible activation, or verbal component that explicitly requires clear speech beyond its space. A rule that functions with whispers remains usable.
- Each named effect from you does not stack with itself. Reapplication refreshes the duration or next-roll expenditure.
- On a successful save, only Reaction denial applies. The free use from Assassination still observes Pressure-Point Strike's once-per-turn limit.

tianxia.subpath.body.shinobi.feature.sha.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Shadow Afterimage

Bonus Action  
Range: An unoccupied space within 15 feet  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 4 Stamina

Create one Shadow Afterimage. You may maintain only one at a time.

Afterimage Statistics

- AC: 13 + Proficiency Bonus
- Hit Points: 1
- Speed: 30 feet
- Immunities: Poison and Psychic
- Size: Your size
- Source CL: Your CL

The Afterimage cannot attack, deal damage, activate items, or use cultivation features. It acts immediately after your turn and follows your mental commands. It can Move, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Hide, Help, gesture, produce faint sounds, or manipulate an unattended object weighing no more than 5 pounds.

You may see and hear through it while within 300 feet.

Shadow Exchange

Bonus Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 1 Stamina

Swap spaces with your Afterimage if both spaces are valid and no spatial lock separates them.

The Afterimage is destroyed at 0 Hit Points, when the duration ends, or when you create another.

Normalized Procedure — Shadow Afterimage
- The Afterimage is a projected Body Asset and visual-auditory decoy, not a creature, Complete Soul, Companion, independent person, or duplicate of your body. It occupies its space but has no physical mass except for the printed object manipulation.
- You choose one listed action for it when its turn begins without spending an action. It can move before or after that action. If you issue no command, it takes Dodge and remains where it is. The source prints no command range; no added distance limit applies while you are on the same plane and direct control is not blocked.
- Help follows the normal Help action and requires the Afterimage to be in a legal position to assist. It cannot grant help based on knowledge, strength, tools, or physical force it does not possess.
- Hide uses its own Stealth check with a modifier equal to your Stealth modifier, because no independent abilities are printed. It cannot become more physically real by Hiding.
- Seeing and hearing through it within 300 feet is simultaneous with your own senses unless a Source Rule says otherwise. It does not grant special senses, perfect memory, or line of effect from your body.
- Manipulating an unattended object is limited to 5 pounds, ordinary object interactions, and the Afterimage's space and reach. It cannot attack with, activate, consume, attune, steal a worn object, or use a cultivation item.
- Shadow Exchange is spatial movement. Both spaces must be legal for the arriving body or Afterimage, on the same plane, within 60 feet, and connected by a route not blocked by a spatial lock. Pay cost and action on a failed exchange and use Failed Spatial Movement.
- At 0 Hit Points the Afterimage is destroyed. Damage does not transfer to you. Creating another immediately ends the prior one, and no remains or materials persist.
tianxia.subpath.body.shinobi.feature.sha.why: CLARITY3: owner-approved display-only clarity pass; preserve all mechanics.

tianxia.subpath.body.shinobi.feature.sil.player_text:
Cultivation Level 3 - Silent Step

Gain proficiency in Stealth. If already proficient, gain a +2 bonus to Stealth checks.

While in Dim Light, Darkness, mist, smoke, or an area that is Lightly or Heavily Obscured:

- Ignore nonmagical Difficult Terrain.
- Gain Advantage on checks to Hide.
- Gain a Climb Speed equal to your walking Speed while at least one hand is free.
- A creature cannot make an Opportunity Attack against you while you are Invisible to it or Heavily Obscured from it.

Dim Light alone does not prevent Opportunity Attacks from a creature that can see you normally.

Normalized Procedure — Silent Step
- If you already have Stealth proficiency, the +2 is a fixed miscellaneous bonus. It is gained once from this feature and does not multiply with repeated proficiency grants.
- Determine Dim Light, Darkness, mist, smoke, and obscuration from the current scene. Dim Light grants the listed terrain and Hide benefits but does not by itself block sight or Opportunity Attacks from a creature that sees normally in it.
- The Climb Speed requires at least one functioning free hand for the entire climb. If that hand becomes occupied or disabled, finish the current movement in the nearest legal supported space or begin falling as normal.
- Opportunity Attack protection is evaluated separately for each observing creature at the instant you leave its reach. You are protected only if Invisible to that creature or Heavily Obscured from it.
- Ignoring nonmagical Difficult Terrain does not permit movement through solid objects, occupied hostile spaces, supernatural Fields, or cultivation-created terrain unless those are independently legal.
tianxia.subpath.body.shinobi.feature.sil.why: CLARITY3: owner-approved display-only clarity pass; preserve all mechanics.

tianxia.subpath.body.shinobi.feature.van.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - Vanishing Flesh

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 6 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- You are Invisible.
- Gain Advantage on Stealth checks.
- Gain a Climb Speed equal to your walking Speed.
- Move through hostile creature spaces as Difficult Terrain.
- Create a Shadow Afterimage when the feature activates without paying its cost.
- Shadow Afterimage does not expire while Vanishing Flesh remains active.

When you make an attack or activate a harmful feature, you become visible until the end of the current turn, then become Invisible again if the duration remains.

The first time you hit during each of your turns, deal an additional 3d6 damage of the attack's type.

A creature capable of perceiving Invisible creatures can target you normally.

---

Normalized Procedure — Vanishing Flesh
- This is a temporary Body transformation creating supernatural concealment. Invisibility does not make you hidden automatically; Stealth and detection resolve normally.
- Moving through hostile spaces treats them as Difficult Terrain. You cannot end movement in another creature's space and this permission does not bypass a physical barrier.
- The free Shadow Afterimage appears in a legal unoccupied space within 15 feet when the feature activates. It follows the normal Afterimage rules, can still be destroyed, and ends when Vanishing Flesh ends unless another valid duration would end it sooner.
- Making an attack or activating a harmful feature makes you visible immediately before its first attack roll, save, or harmful resolution and keeps you visible until the end of the current turn. All creatures can perceive that visible state normally. If the duration remains, Invisibility resumes at the end of the turn without an action.
- A harmless movement, defensive feature, Hide action, object interaction, or purely diagnostic effect does not reveal you unless its own rule says otherwise.
- The 3d6 additional damage applies to the first hit during each of your turns, not each attack type or target. Use the triggering attack's chosen damage type.
- A creature with a legal means to perceive Invisible creatures ignores only the Invisibility-based targeting restriction; other cover, concealment, Stealth, and defenses remain.

---

tianxia.subpath.body.sky_treading_tendon.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Pursuit Without Horizon

Reaction  
You can use this when  A hostile creature you can see within 60 feet willingly moves at least 10 feet or teleports using its own feature.  
Cost: 2 Stamina  
Limit: Once per round

Move up to your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. You may use Thousand-Mile Legs and Tread the Empty Sky without paying Tread's normal cost. You must end closer to the triggering creature.

If you end within unarmed reach, make one unarmed strike against it. The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.

Normalized Procedure — Pursuit Without Horizon

- The trigger resolves after the hostile creature completes the qualifying 10 feet of willing movement or its teleport resolves. Movement split into several segments can trigger once when the cumulative willing movement reaches 10 feet.
- A teleport qualifies only when activated by the hostile creature's own feature. Movement imposed by another creature, forced movement, or involuntary teleportation does not.
- After the trigger resolves, move up to your current Speed. Thousand-Mile Legs applies normally. If airborne, you may activate Tread the Empty Sky as part of this Reaction without its Stamina cost; this does not require another action.
- Your final space must be legally closer to the triggering creature by straight-line distance than your starting space. If no such legal space can be reached, move as close as possible; if no movement would end closer, the movement fails but the Reaction and Stamina are spent.
- The unarmed strike occurs after movement and only if the creature remains within reach. It follows the Granted Attack rule and cannot trigger another granted attack.
tianxia.subpath.body.sky_treading_tendon.why: CLARITY3: owner-approved display-only clarity pass; preserve all mechanics.

tianxia.subpath.body.sky_treading_tendon.player_text:
Cultivation Level 3 - Thousand-Mile Legs

Your walking Speed increases by 10 feet. Your long jump and high jump distances are tripled, and you do not require a running start.

When you use Stomping Step, until the end of the turn you may move across liquids and vertical surfaces without falling during the movement, and ordinary nonmagical Difficult Terrain does not cost additional movement. If you end unsupported, you fall normally.

Once during each of your turns, after moving at least 20 feet before hitting with an unarmed strike, deal additional damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus and move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Normalized Procedure — Thousand-Mile Legs

- The 10-foot increase modifies your walking Speed and therefore any feature that explicitly derives a Speed from walking Speed. It does not directly increase a fixed climb, swim, burrow, or teleport range.
- Triple the final long-jump and high-jump distances after ordinary Strength calculations and before a feature that supplies a separate fixed jump distance. No running start is required.
- During Stomping Step, movement across liquid or a vertical surface is ordinary movement using your available Speed. You do not sink or fall during that movement. If unsupported when the turn ends, resolve falling normally.
- Ordinary nonmagical Difficult Terrain costs no extra movement only during that Stomping Step turn. A supernatural Field, Formation, Domain, spatial lock, or explicit movement prohibition retains its authority.
- For the once-per-turn strike rider, count actual distance traveled by voluntary movement during the current turn. Teleportation does not add traveled distance. After a qualifying hit, add Proficiency Bonus damage to the attack packet and take the 5-foot legal movement after the hit resolves.
tianxia.subpath.body.sky_treading_tendon.why: CLARITY3: owner-approved display-only clarity pass; preserve all mechanics.

tianxia.subpath.body.still_water_draw_bo.player_text:
Cultivation Level 3 - Drawn from Stillness

Choose one Draw Blade as your Draw Weapon.

While wielding it:

- Use Constitution instead of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls.
- You may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier.
- It is integrated into Body Refining.
- Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply.
- Draw or sheath it as part of an attack.

First Cut

The first time you hit with your Draw Weapon during each turn, provided you made no earlier attack that turn, deal additional Slashing or Force damage equal to Proficiency Bonus and move 5 feet without provoking.

The weapon need not begin physically sheathed; Draw represents the first committed release.

Normalized Procedure — Draw Weapon and First Cut

- Choose and record one weapon in the Draw Blade group. While wielding that weapon, Constitution replaces Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls, and you may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier. It is integrated into Body Refining and grants no Sphere, extra weapon, or additional attack.
- Drawing or sheathing it as part of an attack changes only its carried state; it does not create a free object interaction usable for another item. The weapon need not begin sheathed for any feature unless that feature expressly says so.
- First Cut qualifies only if the triggering hit is produced by the first attack roll you make during that turn. If that first attack misses, an attack was still made and no later hit that turn qualifies. A save-based technique or nonattack damage made before the attack does not by itself disqualify First Cut unless it includes an attack roll.
- Declare First Cut after the hit. Add Proficiency Bonus as Slashing or Force to the triggering packet, then move up to 5 feet without provoking along a legal route. The movement is optional, occurs after the hit resolves, and cannot pass through occupied spaces without another permission.
- Reactions made during another creature's turn use that turn's separate First Cut eligibility. The feature remains once per turn, not once per round.
tianxia.subpath.body.still_water_draw_bo.why: CLARITY3: owner-approved display-only clarity pass; preserve all mechanics.

tianxia.subpath.body.still_water_draw_bo.player_text:
Cultivation Level 6 - Empty-Scabbard Step

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature makes a melee attack against you.  
Cost: 1 Stamina  
Limit: Once per round

Move 10 feet before the attack roll resolves, without provoking and without crossing solid barriers or occupied spaces.

Resolve the attack from your new position. If outside reach, it misses. If it misses while you remain within reach, make one Draw Weapon attack after it resolves. The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.

Normalized Procedure — Empty-Scabbard Step

- Declare after a creature commits to one melee attack against you but before the triggering attack roll. Spend the Reaction and 1 Stamina, then move up to 10 feet along a continuous legal route without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- The route cannot cross a solid barrier or any occupied space and must end in a space you can occupy. If no movement is legal, you can remain in place; the feature is still spent.
- After movement, recheck the triggering attack's target, reach, line of effect, and any required facing or adjacency. If you are no longer a legal target, that attack misses without a roll. Otherwise make and resolve the triggering attack roll from the new geometry.
- If the triggering attack misses for any reason and you remain within current Draw Weapon reach of the attacker after it resolves, make one Draw Weapon attack against that attacker. The granted attack occurs after every effect of the miss that must resolve first, follows the Granted Attack rule, and cannot grant another attack.
- If the triggering attack is one attack within a Multiattack or Attack action, only that attack is affected. Later attacks can choose legal targets normally.

Cultivation Level 18 - Heaven Divided Before Sound

Action  
Range: An unoccupied space within 120 feet  
Cost: 7 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

Move in a straight line without provoking, across liquids, vertical surfaces, and open air, and through hostile spaces. You cannot pass through total cover, sealed Formations, spatial locks, or a surviving barrier.

Choose up to Proficiency Bonus creatures crossed or within 5 feet of the line. Make one Draw Weapon attack against each. On a hit, deal normal damage plus 6d8 Slashing or Force.

After all attacks, each hit creature makes a Constitution save.

- Failed Save: Speed 0 and no Reactions until the end of its next turn.
- Successful Save: Speed halved until the start of its next turn.

When the line intersects a blocking barrier, make one Draw Weapon attack against it before moving through. On a hit, deal normal damage plus 6d8. If destroyed, continue. If it survives, end in the nearest legal space before it. The barrier counts against maximum targets.

Each creature can be attacked once. Attacks follow the Granted Attack rule.

Normalized Procedure — Heaven Divided Before Sound

- Select an unoccupied legal destination within 120 feet and declare the straight line from your current space to that destination. Spend the Action and 7 Stamina. The route is physical movement, not teleportation, and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- You can cross liquids, vertical surfaces, open air, and hostile occupied spaces as printed, but cannot end in an occupied space. Total cover, a sealed Formation, spatial lock, or surviving solid barrier blocks further travel.
- Before moving, choose up to Proficiency Bonus eligible creatures crossed by or within 5 feet of the line. Resolve chosen creatures and blocking barriers in nearest-to-farthest order. Each creature can be attacked once.
- When the line reaches a blocking barrier, make one Draw Weapon attack against it before entering its space. On a hit deal normal damage plus 6d8 Slashing or Force. It counts against the Proficiency Bonus target maximum. If destroyed, continue; if it survives or the attack misses, end in the nearest legal space before it and ignore selected targets beyond it.
- When you reach each selected creature's position along the line, make one Draw Weapon attack. On a hit deal normal damage plus 6d8 Slashing or Force. These are granted attacks and cannot grant additional attacks.
- After all reachable attacks resolve, each creature hit by this activation makes one Constitution save. On failure its Speed becomes 0 and it cannot take Reactions until the end of its next turn. On success its Speed is halved until the start of its next turn.
- A creature hit several times through an unrelated rule makes one save for this activation. The line does not automatically sever limbs, cut space, destroy an undamaged permanent barrier, or ignore explicit higher-Source-CL movement authority.

Cultivation Level 14 - Moon Reflected Before Motion

At the start of your turn, before moving or taking an action, enter Still-Water Posture until the end of the turn.

- The first Draw Weapon attack has Advantage.
- Speed becomes 0 until that attack resolves.
- On a hit, additional 3d8 Slashing or Force damage and no Reactions until the start of the target's next turn.
- Afterward, Speed is restored and you move up to half your Speed without provoking.

You may enter this posture once per round. Forced movement does not end it; voluntary movement does.

Normalized Procedure — Still-Water Posture

- At the start of your turn, before movement, an Action, Bonus Action, or another voluntary activation, choose whether to enter Still-Water Posture. Entering requires no action and is limited to once per round.
- While in the posture, current Speed is 0 until your first Draw Weapon attack of that turn resolves or the posture ends. Forced movement does not end it. Any willing movement, teleportation, or spatial relocation before that attack ends the posture immediately and grants none of its attack or follow-up movement benefits.
- The first Draw Weapon attack you make during the posture has Advantage. After it resolves, your Speed returns to its normal current value whether the attack hits or misses.
- On a hit, add 3d8 Slashing or Force to the triggering packet and prevent the target from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn. Then move up to half your restored Speed without provoking along a legal route.
- On a miss, no additional damage, Reaction denial, or follow-up movement occurs, but Speed is restored.
- If you never make the attack, Speed remains 0 until the end of the turn and the posture then ends. Actions that do not move you are legal while waiting to make the attack.

Cultivation Level 10 - One Breath, Three Horizons

When you take the Attack action, replace two attacks with a line.

Area: 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line  
Cost: 2 Stamina  
Limit: Once per turn  
Saving Throw: Dexterity

On a failed save, a creature takes two Draw Weapon damage dice + Constitution modifier + 4d8 Slashing or Force damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. On a success, half damage and retains Reactions.

After the line, move to any unoccupied space adjacent to it without provoking, up to half your Speed.

This is not a weapon attack and does not apply attack-hit riders.

Normalized Procedure — One Breath, Three Horizons

- You must have at least two attacks available in the current Attack action. Replace exactly two of those attacks before either is made, spend 2 Stamina, and create one 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line originating from you in a chosen direction.
- Every creature other than you whose space intersects the line makes one Dexterity save and is affected once. Total cover blocks the line; resolve eligible creatures from nearest to farthest until a surviving solid obstruction stops it.
- On failure, roll two copies of the Draw Weapon's printed damage die, add Constitution modifier once, and add 4d8 Slashing or Force as chosen for the activation. The target also cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. On success it takes half total damage and retains Reactions.
- This is one Body technique, not an attack. It cannot critically hit and does not apply attack-hit riders, weapon mastery riders, ammunition, First Cut, or effects requiring a weapon attack.
- After every save and damage packet resolves, move up to half your current Speed without provoking to any legal unoccupied space adjacent to any point of the line. This is physical movement along a legal route, not teleportation. If no route exists, remain in place.
- The replacement remains once per turn across additional Attack actions.

Your unarmed strikes deal double damage to unattended objects, vehicles, structures, temporary barriers, Formation Anchors, and ordinary terrain sections.

You can use this when  You hit with an unarmed strike.

- For a creature collision, the original target must be forced into the second creature's space. On the second creature's successful Dexterity save, place the original target in the nearest legal space before the second creature; only the original target takes the collision damage. Bonus Action

Enter Rooted Stance. It lasts until you become airborne without a supporting surface, willingly teleport, willingly move more than half your Speed during one turn, become Unconscious, or end it without using an action.

While Rooted:

- Gain Advantage on checks and saving throws against Grapples, Shoves, forced movement, and being knocked Prone.
- Gain Advantage on saving throws or Cultivation Checks against unwilling teleportation.
- Count as one size larger for Grappling, Shoving, carrying, lifting, and resisting forced movement.
- Reduce forced movement affecting you by 5 feet.

Normalized Procedure — Rooted Stance

- Rooted Stance is a stance, not a transformation and not Concentration. Entering it does not spend movement.
- “Touching a supporting surface” includes standing, kneeling, sitting, bracing with a limb, or being physically anchored to a substantial surface. A creature carried entirely by another creature is not supported unless a feature says it can root through that carrier.
- Track the voluntary distance you move during each of your turns. The stance ends immediately when that total exceeds half your current Speed. Forced movement, movement of a platform, and movement while you are Incapacitated do not count. Willingly teleporting ends it regardless of distance.
- The “count as larger” permission applies only to the listed operations and does not change your occupied space, reach, weapon damage, or legal mount size.
- Reduce forced movement once per movement event, to a minimum of 0 feet. This does not reduce teleportation; the separate Advantage against unwilling teleportation applies to that procedure.

While Rooted Stance is active:

Cultivation Level 3 - Bow Body

Gain proficiency with Bow weapons.

While wielding a Bow:

- Use Constitution instead of Dexterity for attack and damage rolls.
- It is integrated into Body Refining.
- You may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier.
- Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature does not impose Disadvantage on your Bow attacks.
- Drawing or firing requires only the hands required by the weapon.

At Cultivation Level 5, the attacks count as magical; at Cultivation Level 17, magical and adamantine.

This does not grant the Archery Sphere.

Normalized Procedure — Bow Body

- Record each wielded Bow used with this feature as an integrated weapon. Constitution replaces Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls, and you may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier for attack rolls.
- This feature grants proficiency but does not grant the Archery Sphere, ammunition, a free Bow, an ammunition-creation effect, additional attacks, or permission to ignore loading, reload, draw-weight, or special ammunition rules printed by a specific weapon.
- Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature does not impose Disadvantage on your Bow attacks. Other sources of Disadvantage remain.
- “Drawing or firing requires only the hands required by the weapon” means the weapon uses its own printed hand requirement and no additional free hand is required solely to draw ordinary ammunition. It does not permit firing while a required hand is disabled, occupied, severed, or suppressed.
- The Cultivation Level 5 and Cultivation Level 17 classifications apply to attacks made with an integrated Bow. They do not transform the physical Bow or its ammunition into an adamantine object for harvesting, crafting, or nonattack interaction.
- If another feature replaces the Bow's damage die, use the highest legal replacement unless a rule explicitly adds a separate die.

Action  
Range: The Bow's long range

Make one Bow attack.

On a hit, deal normal damage plus 5d8 Piercing or Force damage. The target makes a Strength saving throw.

Action

Saving Throw: Dexterity

On a failed save, a creature takes one Bow weapon damage die + Constitution modifier + 4d8 Piercing or Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half damage.

The line passes through creatures and stops at an object, barrier, or structure that survives the damage. Unattended ordinary objects, temporary barriers, vehicles, structures, and Formation Anchors take double damage.

Sun-Chasing Line is not an attack and does not apply attack-hit riders.

Normalized Procedure — Sun-Chasing Line

- Replace one attack of the Attack action and choose a point up to 120 feet away, creating a 5-foot-wide line from the Bow to that point. The line requires line of effect and is not a weapon attack.
- Choose Piercing or Force for the activation. Each creature in the line makes one Dexterity save and is affected once. Damage uses one damage die of the integrated Bow, Constitution modifier once, and 4d8 of the chosen type.
- The line does not apply critical hits, attack-hit riders, ammunition riders, weapon mastery riders, or effects requiring a Bow attack to hit.
- Resolve targets and obstructions from nearest to farthest. Creatures do not stop the line. When the line reaches an object, barrier, structure, vehicle, or Formation Anchor, apply its damage once and double the final damage if the target is an eligible unattended or listed target.
- If that obstruction is reduced to 0 Hit Points or otherwise destroyed by this activation, the line continues. If it survives and physically blocks the line, creatures and objects beyond it are not affected.
- Worn, carried, wielded, piloted, or actively controlled objects are not unattended. A target belonging to several doubled categories receives the multiplier once.
- Half and Three-Quarters Cover apply normally unless the line's path physically bypasses that cover. Total cover from a surviving obstruction stops the line.

tianxia.subpath.body.ten_thousand_parasi.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Brood Substitution

Reaction  
You can use this when  You are hit by an attack or fail a Dexterity or Constitution save against a damaging effect.  
Cost: 2 Brood  
Limit: Once per round

Reduce damage by 4d8 + Constitution modifier, move 10 feet without provoking, and leave a swarm-shell in your original space until the start of your next turn.

Swarm-Shell

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 2 x CL
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic
- Vulnerability: Fire and Radiant
- Space: 5 feet; creatures move through as Difficult Terrain

Normalized Procedure — Brood Substitution and Swarm-Shell

- Declare after an attack hits you or after you fail the listed save, before triggering damage is applied. Spend the Reaction and 2 Brood.
- Roll 4d8 + Constitution modifier once and reduce the triggering damage packet at the shared flat-reduction step. The feature does not turn a failed save into a success or remove non-damage consequences.
- After damage resolves, move up to 10 feet without provoking along a legal route. The movement is physical swarm displacement, not teleportation. Leave the Swarm-Shell in your original space only if that space is legal for the Asset.
- The Swarm-Shell is a projected Body Asset with the printed AC, Hit Points, Immunities, Vulnerabilities, and 5-foot space. It is stationary, takes no actions, grants no cover unless normal geometry does so, and lasts until the start of your next turn or until destroyed.
- Creatures can move through its space as Difficult Terrain but cannot end there unless they could normally share its space. Destroying it causes no damage, Brood loss, Injury, or effect on you.
- If movement fails, the damage reduction still applies and the Shell appears in your current space only when legal; otherwise no Shell is created.

tianxia.subpath.body.ten_thousand_parasi.player_text:
Cultivation Level 6 - Gnawing Infestation

When an Infested creature first spends Cultivation Points, takes Dash, willingly moves 15 feet, regains Hit Points, or gains Temporary Hit Points during its turn:

- It takes 3d8 Poison or Necrotic damage.
- It cannot regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points until the start of its next turn.
- The Infestation ends.

If not triggered, it repeats the Constitution save at the end of its turn, ending Infestation on a success.

Normalized Procedure — Gnawing Infestation

- During an Infested creature's turn, monitor the first qualifying event: spending Cultivation Points; taking Dash; accumulating 15 feet of willing movement; regaining Hit Points; or gaining Temporary Hit Points.
- The event commits before Gnawing resolves. Cultivation Points remain spent, Dash remains taken, movement already completed remains, and healing/Temporary Hit Points are first gained, then the feature deals damage and imposes its prohibition.
- Deal 3d8 Poison or Necrotic using the Infestation's recorded type. The creature cannot regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points until the start of its next turn, and that Infestation ends.
- One turn can trigger one Infestation from you once. If no trigger occurs, the creature repeats the recorded Constitution save at the end of its turn and ends the Infestation on success.
- Forced movement, teleportation, involuntary falling, and Cultivation Point loss that is not spending do not satisfy the trigger. A 0-point activation is not spending Cultivation Points.

tianxia.subpath.body.ten_thousand_parasi.player_text:
Cultivation Level 3 - Internal Brood

Gain Resistance to Poison damage and Advantage against disease.

At the start of your turn, spend 1 Brood to regain 1d8 + Constitution modifier Hit Points, increasing to 2d8 at Cultivation Level 11 and 3d8 at Cultivation Level 17. This requires no action, functions once per turn, and cannot heal you at 0 Hit Points.

Infesting Strike

You can use this when  You hit with an unarmed strike.  
Cost: 1 Brood  
Limit: Once per turn  
Saving Throw: Constitution

Deal an additional 1d8 Poison or Necrotic damage. On a failed save, the target becomes Infested until the end of your next turn.

Normalized Procedure — Internal Brood and Infesting Strike

- Poison Resistance and Advantage against disease use ordinary procedures. “Disease” includes effects explicitly tagged or described as diseases, not every Poison or corruption.
- At the start of your turn, spend 1 Brood to restore the printed Hit Points. This uses no action, functions once per turn, and cannot operate at 0 Hit Points before Cultivation Level 18.
- The die scaling replaces the earlier die. Add Constitution modifier once, to a minimum of 0 Hit Points regained.
- Infesting Strike: After an unarmed-strike hit, spend 1 Brood, choose Poison or Necrotic, and add 1d8 to the hit once per turn. The target then makes one Constitution save.
- On failure create one Infested record until the end of your next turn. Record source, Source CL, damage type, trigger status, save DC, and expiration. A new Infestation from you refreshes rather than stacks unless Cultivation Level 14 capacity permits several different creatures.

Cultivation Level 14 - Parasite Sovereignty

Poison and Necrotic damage from this Subpath ignores Resistance. Maintain Infested creatures equal to Proficiency Bonus.

Once per round when an Infested creature takes Gnawing Infestation damage, choose one:

- Regain Hit Points equal to Proficiency Bonus.
- Gain 1 Brood.
- Move 10 feet without provoking.
- Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice Proficiency Bonus.

Brood gained this way can exceed the ordinary gain limit, but this feature remains once per round.

Normalized Procedure — Parasite Sovereignty

- Poison and Necrotic damage from this Subpath ignores ordinary Resistance, not Immunity or a superior defense expressly immune to penetration.
- Maintain Infested creatures up to Proficiency Bonus. When exceeding the limit, choose one existing Infestation to end or decline the new one.
- Once per round after one Infested creature takes Gnawing Infestation damage, choose one printed benefit.
- Healing restores Proficiency Bonus Hit Points and is self-generated Body Refining healing. Brood gain is direct and can bypass the ordinary gain limit but not maximum. Movement is up to 10 feet without provoking along a legal route. Temporary Hit Points equal twice Proficiency Bonus and follow the normal nonstacking rule.
- Several Infestations triggering in the same round grant one benefit total. The benefit occurs after Gnawing damage and its healing prohibition are applied; choosing healing therefore cannot restore Hit Points if that same target's trigger somehow made you subject to an applicable prohibition.
