tianxia.subpath.body.heaven_binding_chai.player_text:
Cultivation Level 6 - Drag the Heavens

Bonus Action  
Target: One creature Tethered to you  
Cost: 1 Stamina  
Saving Throw: Strength

On a failed save, pull it 20 feet, move yourself 20 feet toward it without provoking, pull it 10 feet and knock it Prone, or rotate it to another unoccupied space within 20 feet.

On a success, pull it 5 feet or move yourself 5 feet toward it.

A creature more than two sizes larger has Advantage.

If it collides with a surface or creature, both take Bludgeoning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus; a second creature avoids this damage on a successful Dexterity save.

Normalized Procedure — Drag the Heavens

- Select one creature currently Tethered to you, spend the Bonus Action and 1 Stamina, then resolve one Strength save. A creature at least three size categories larger than you has Advantage; functional size expressly applicable to Grappling or forced movement counts.
- On a failed save, choose exactly one printed result. On a success, choose one of the two printed 5-foot results. Self-movement and target movement are part of this activation and do not create another movement trigger from Drag the Heavens.
- A pull moves the target directly toward you along the shortest legal route. Self-movement moves you directly toward the target, does not provoke Opportunity Attacks, and must end in a legal space. The 10-foot pull-and-Prone result applies Prone after movement ends.
- The rotation result moves the target through a curved or straight legal route no longer than 20 feet to an unoccupied space within 20 feet of you. It cannot pass through total cover or a sealed barrier and cannot end beyond the Meridian Tether boundary.
- Forced movement stops at the nearest legal space before an obstruction. If the moving target first collides with a damageable surface or one creature because no legal continuation exists, resolve one collision only. The moved target takes Bludgeoning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A damageable surface takes the same damage; a second creature makes one Dexterity save, taking the same damage on failure and none on success.
- Collision damage is one packet per affected creature, does not repeat for several occupied squares or chained contacts, and does not create an Injury, Grapple, or additional forced movement unless another Source Rule says so.
- A successful-save 5-foot pull or self-movement uses the same route and legal-space rules. If no legal movement is possible, that movement becomes 0; the Stamina and Bonus Action remain spent.
tianxia.subpath.body.heaven_binding_chai.why: CLARITY3: owner-approved display-only clarity pass; preserve all mechanics.

tianxia.subpath.body.heaven_binding_chai.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Guardian Chain

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature within 30 feet is hit by a ranged attack or would be moved at least 10 feet against its will.  
Cost: 2 Stamina  
Limit: Once per round

Choose one:

- Catch the Attack: Reduce ranged attack damage by 3d10 + Constitution modifier. If reduced to 0, move the protected creature 10 feet toward you without provoking.
- Anchor the Body: Reduce forced movement by 20 feet. If reduced to 0, prevent Prone from the same effect and move it 5 feet toward you.

Guardian Chain cannot prevent teleportation unless the creature is Tethered.

Normalized Procedure — Guardian Chain

- Declare after a creature within 30 feet is hit by one ranged attack but before its damage is applied, or after hostile forced movement of at least 10 feet is declared but before that movement resolves. Spend the Reaction and 2 Stamina; the once-per-round limit is consumed even if the result is later reduced by a stronger rule.
- Catch the Attack: Reduce the triggering attack's total damage packet by 3d10 + Constitution modifier at the shared damage-reduction step. This protects only the chosen hit creature and does not reduce later attacks or separate damage packets from the same activation. If final damage applied becomes 0, move that creature up to 10 feet directly toward you along a legal route without provoking Opportunity Attacks. This is granted movement created by you and does not require willingness.
- Anchor the Body: Reduce the triggering physical forced-movement distance by 20 feet after the source determines distance. If final distance becomes 0, also prevent Prone caused by that same movement effect and move the protected creature up to 5 feet toward you without provoking. Prevented movement creates no collision unless the source expressly creates one without movement.
- Guardian Chain does not reduce ordinary teleport distance. If the protected creature is Tethered and the trigger is willing or hostile spatial movement, you may use Anchor the Body; replace the 20-foot reduction with one Cultivation Check by the spatial effect's activator against your Cultivation Save DC. On failure, use Failed Spatial Movement; on success, the spatial movement resolves normally. Do not roll both this check and the Meridian Tether check for the same spatial activation; Guardian Chain uses this Reaction-based check instead.
- A creature moved toward you by Guardian Chain must end in a legal space. If no legal route or destination exists, move it as far as legally possible. Guardian Chain does not redirect the ranged attack, change its source, or create a counterattack.

tianxia.subpath.body.heaven_binding_chai.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - Heaven-Binding Prison

Action  
Range: A point within 60 feet  
Area: 30-foot-radius, 30-foot-high cylinder  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 7 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

Each chosen hostile creature in the area makes a Strength saving throw.

- Failed Save: Restrained, Tethered to the center, cannot willingly leave, and spatial movement outside requires a Cultivation Check; failure uses Failed Spatial Movement.
- Successful Save: Not Restrained; Speed halved until the start of its next turn.

A Restrained creature repeats the Strength save at the end of each turn, ending Restrained on a success. It remains Tethered until the start of its following turn.

You and chosen allies ignore movement restrictions. Hostile creatures treat the area as Difficult Terrain. Temporary barriers, unattended objects, and Formation Anchors take 4d8 Force damage when it appears.

The central anchor has AC equal to your Cultivation Save DC, Hit Points 5 x CL, Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing, Immunity to Poison and Psychic, and occupies the center. Destroying or suppressing it ends the prison.

Normalized Procedure — Heaven-Binding Prison

- Select a point on a stable surface within 60 feet that can contain the central Anchor's 5-foot space. The prison is a stationary 30-foot-radius, 30-foot-high cylinder centered on that point and lasts 1 minute without Concentration unless ended by its Anchor.
- When the prison appears, designate any number of allies. Each other chosen hostile creature currently in the cylinder makes one Strength save. A creature is affected once by the creation even if it occupies several spaces.
- On failure, the creature is Restrained and gains a Prison Tether to the center. A Prison Tether is separate from Meridian Tethers, does not count against their maximum, prevents willing departure from the cylinder, and requires a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC for spatial movement outside. Failure uses Failed Spatial Movement.
- At the end of each of its turns, a Restrained creature repeats the Strength save. On success, Restrained ends immediately but its Prison Tether remains until the start of its following turn. While only that Tether remains, it is not Restrained but still cannot willingly leave or spatially escape without the check.
- On the initial successful save, the creature is not Restrained or Prison Tethered and its Speed is halved until the start of its next turn. A creature entering after creation receives no initial save or Tether; it treats the area as Difficult Terrain while hostile.
- You and designated allies ignore the prison's Difficult Terrain, Prison Tethers, and movement restrictions. They do not ignore the central Anchor's occupied space or a separate restraint effect.
- On creation, each eligible unattended object, temporary barrier, vehicle, structure, and Formation Anchor in the cylinder takes one 4d8 Force damage packet. Creatures and permanent world terrain are not damaged by this clause.
- The central Anchor is an immobile Body Refining Anchor with Source CL equal to this feature, AC equal to your Cultivation Save DC, Hit Points equal to 5 × effective Body Refining CL, Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing, Immunity to Poison and Psychic, and a 5-foot occupied space. It makes no attacks and grants no cover unless ordinary geometry does so.
- Destroying the Anchor, suppressing it, moving it from the center through an explicit higher-authority rule, your death, or the duration ending immediately ends the prison, every Prison Tether, and every Restrained condition created by it. Damage to the Anchor does not damage you.

---

tianxia.subpath.body.heaven_binding_chai.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Thousand-Link Meridian Network

Chain reach increases by another 5 feet during your turn. Maintain Tethers equal to Proficiency Bonus.

While at least one hostile creature is Tethered:

- Tethered creatures treat spaces within your chain reach as Difficult Terrain.
- You cannot be Disarmed of a Chain Weapon by an ordinary effect.
- Once per turn on a hit against a Tethered creature, deal an additional 2d8 Bludgeoning, Slashing, or Force damage.
- When a Tethered creature willingly moves within your reach, it provokes an Opportunity Attack even if that movement normally would not.

You retain your normal number of Reactions.

Normalized Procedure — Thousand-Link Meridian Network

- Your maintained Meridian Tether maximum becomes your Proficiency Bonus. If that maximum decreases, choose excess Tethers to end immediately. Each Tether retains its own target, duration, distance, Source CL, and removal record.
- The additional Chain reach is turn-only and combines with Chain-Body Integration for +10 feet during your turn. Outside your turn use the Chain Weapon's printed reach plus any other persistent reach expressly granted by another rule.
- While at least one hostile creature is Tethered, every hostile creature Tethered to you treats spaces currently within your Chain Weapon reach as Difficult Terrain. This applies only to its willing movement; forced movement, teleportation, and falling do not pay difficult-terrain cost.
- Reach expansion around a stationary creature does not count as that creature entering or moving within reach. The special Opportunity Attack trigger occurs when a Tethered creature willingly moves at least 5 feet while it is within your current reach, including movement that normally avoids Opportunity Attacks. Teleportation and hostile forced movement do not trigger it.
- The special trigger does not grant an extra Reaction. It uses your normal Opportunity Attack procedure and current out-of-turn reach.
- The 2d8 rider is once per turn total. Declare it after hitting one Tethered creature; choose Bludgeoning, Slashing, or Force. It is part of the triggering hit's damage packet and cannot critically multiply separately.
- Ordinary Disarm immunity prevents mundane or ordinary creature effects from removing the wielded Chain Weapon. Artifact, divine, Secret, Foundation, Method, Immortal, or explicit equal- or higher-Source-CL authority can still contest it.

tianxia.subpath.body.heaven_devouring_ma.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - Devour Heaven and Earth

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 8 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- Maximum Devoured Essence +3.
- Swallow Hostile Power reduces 4d10 + Constitution modifier.
- Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from supernatural attacks become valid stored types.
- Once per round when a hostile creature within 60 feet spends Cultivation Points, gain 1 Essence after its feature resolves. Choose a damage type dealt by it, or Force if none.
- Maw Strike deals 6d8 additional damage.
- Feast upon Protection can treat Immunity as Resistance until the start of your next turn on a failed save.

World-Eating Bite

You can use this when  You hit with an unarmed strike.  
Cost: 5 Devoured Essence  
Limit: Once per turn  
Saving Throw: Constitution

Deal an additional 10d8 of one consumed type.

- Failed Save: End one temporary ward, transformation, aura, stance, or damage-reduction effect. If none, remove Temporary Hit Points and prevent gaining them until the start of your next turn.
- Successful Save: No effect ends, but Temporary Hit Points cannot be gained until the start of your next turn.

Permanent Foundation stages, Methods, Path features, and item properties do not end.

Normalized Procedure — Devour Heaven and Earth

- For the duration, increase maximum Essence by 3. When the transformation ends, any excess records remain until scene end or expenditure; the maximum returning to normal does not itself choose records to discard, but no new Essence can be gained while above maximum.
- Swallow Hostile Power's reduction becomes 4d10 + Constitution modifier; this replaces its earlier roll. Supernatural Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing become valid for every Subpath feature during the duration.

- Track distinct Forms that hit during your current turn. Once per turn immediately after the third different Form hits, or after a later different-Form hit if the Completion was not yet used, choose one Completion Effect.

Once per turn when you take the Attack action, spend 1 Battle Hand to choose one:

- Draw or stow two weapons.
- Move 5 feet without provoking.
- Gain +1 AC until your next turn.

- Once during each of your turns when you take the Attack action, spend 1 Battle Hand and choose one printed operation. The operation can occur at a legal point during that Attack action unless its trigger specifies a hit or miss.
- Drawing or stowing two weapons changes only those two item states and does not grant another object interaction.
- The 5-foot movement follows a legal route and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

- After an attack hits, add Proficiency Bonus as one damage type dealt by that attack to the triggering packet. It cannot critically multiply separately.
- Only one Battle Hand operation can modify the same attack roll. A later operation that does not modify the roll, such as movement or AC, still cannot be selected because Four-Hand Sequence is once per turn.

Cultivation Level 14 - Poisoned Body, Poisoned World

Your Poison damage ignores Resistance.

Once per round, after a hostile creature within reach damages you, Grapples you, or begins its turn Grappling you, spend 1 Stamina without using an action. It makes a Constitution saving throw.

- Failed Save: 3d8 Poison damage and one Sovereign Venom.
- Successful Save: Half damage and no Venom.

This resolves after the triggering damage or Grapple.

Normalized Procedure — Poisoned Body, Poisoned World

- Ignoring Poison Resistance applies to Poison damage from your Body Refining features only. It does not affect another creature's poison, a Sphere technique, an item, or environmental poison unless that effect expressly uses this feature.
- Once per round, after a hostile creature within your current unarmed reach damages you, successfully Grapples you, or starts its turn while maintaining a Grapple on you, you may spend 1 Stamina without an action. You must be able to spend Stamina and perceive or identify the qualifying creature.
- The feature resolves after the triggering damage or Grapple state. If the triggering event moves the creature outside your reach before resolution, it is no longer a legal target.
- The target makes one Constitution save. On failure, it takes 3d8 Poison damage and you choose one Sovereign Venom; on success, it takes half damage and gains no Venom.
- One creature cannot trigger several uses from the same event, and the feature remains once per round even if several creatures damage or Grapple you.
- Damage from this feature cannot trigger another copy of Poisoned Body, Poisoned World or count as a hostile poison source for your own Swallow the Poison.

Cultivation Level 6 - Swallow the Poison

Reaction  
You can use this when  You take Acid or Poison damage, fail a saving throw against poison or disease, or would become Poisoned.  
Cost: 1 Stamina  
Limit: Once per round

Choose the matching response:

- Reduce Acid or Poison damage by 2d10 + Constitution modifier.
- Add your Proficiency Bonus to the failed saving throw, potentially turning it into a success.
- Delay Poisoned until the end of your next turn.

If you take no Poison damage, succeed on the save, or avoid Poisoned, your next Venom Furnace before the end of your next turn deals additional Poison damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

This cannot remove a Hidden Injury, Foundation Burden, permanent disease, Tribulation effect, curse, or poison requiring a special cure.

Normalized Procedure — Swallow the Poison

- Use the Reaction for one triggering damage packet, one failed save, or one impending application of Poisoned. If one event satisfies several triggers, choose one response.
- For Acid or Poison damage, declare after Resistance and Vulnerability are applied but before Hit Points are reduced. Reduce only the matching Acid or Poison portion by 2d10 + Constitution modifier, then continue the ordinary damage procedure.
- For a failed saving throw, declare after the total is known but before consequences are finalized. Add Proficiency Bonus to that roll; if the new total meets the DC, treat the save as successful.
- To delay Poisoned, declare before the condition begins. The condition does not apply until the end of your next turn. If its source would have ended before that time, it never begins; otherwise it begins then for the remaining printed duration. Delay is not removal and does not by itself count as avoiding Poisoned.
- You gain the Venom Furnace bonus only if the chosen response causes you to take 0 matching Poison damage, changes the failed save to a success, or prevents Poisoned from ever beginning. Merely delaying the condition does not qualify unless the source expires during the delay.
- Record one stored adaptation. Your next Venom Furnace before the end of your next turn gains additional Poison damage equal to Proficiency Bonus. A new stored adaptation refreshes this window; it does not stack several bonuses.
- The exclusions for Hidden Injuries, Foundation Burdens, permanent disease, Tribulations, curses, and special-cure poisons apply even when the immediate damage or condition is reduced.

Cultivation Level 10 - Three Sovereign Venoms

When a creature fails its Venom Furnace save, choose one unique state until the end of your next turn:

- Nerve Venom: No Reactions and Disadvantage on its next attack roll.
- Blood Venom: Takes 2d6 Poison damage at the start of its next turn.
- Marrow Venom: Speed reduced by 15 feet and Disadvantage on its next Strength or Dexterity saving throw.

Only one Sovereign Venom from you can affect a creature. Reapplication replaces it.

Normalized Procedure — Three Sovereign Venoms

- Choose a Sovereign Venom only when a target fails the Venom Furnace Constitution save. The chosen state uses Venom Furnace's Source CL and lasts until the end of your next turn unless its own operation resolves earlier.
- Nerve Venom: Reaction denial begins immediately. Disadvantage applies to the target's next attack roll during the duration and is consumed after that roll.
- Blood Venom: At the start of the target's next turn, it takes one 2d6 Poison damage packet, then Blood Venom ends. If the state is removed before that turn, the damage does not occur.
- Marrow Venom: Reduce every Speed by 15 feet, to a minimum of 0. When applied, choose Strength or Dexterity; the target has Disadvantage on its next saving throw of that type during the duration, then consumes the effect.
- A creature can bear only one Sovereign Venom from you before Cultivation Level 18. Applying a new one replaces the previous state after the new save fails. It does not preserve the previous state's unspent rider.
- A Sovereign Venom is a bodily poison effect, not an anatomical Injury, destroyed organ, disease, curse, or independently harvestable dose.

Gain Resistance to Poison damage and Advantage on saving throws against Poisoned and disease. Your unarmed strikes may deal Poison damage.

Cost: 1 Stamina

Normalized Procedure — Venom Furnace

Cultivation Level 14 - Iron Wall

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 5 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

- Gain Resistance to all damage except Force, Psychic, and Void.
- Gain Advantage against being Grappled, Restrained, pushed, pulled, or knocked Prone.

- Your Speed is reduced by 10 feet.

- “Unavoidable self-damage” means damage a Source Rule explicitly states cannot be reduced, prevented, redirected, or resisted, or damage paid as a mandatory cost. Ordinary recoil is reduced normally unless it carries that clause.

Cultivation Level 18 - Asura's Rage

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 7 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- Gain Advantage on unarmed attack rolls.
- Gain Resistance to all damage except Force, Radiant, and Void.
- Gain Immunity to Frightened.
- Your unarmed strikes may deal Bludgeoning, Fire, or Necrotic damage.
- Once per turn when you hit with an unarmed strike, deal an additional 3d6 Fire or Necrotic damage.
- Once per round when a hostile creature damages you, move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Once per round when a hostile creature within your reach damages you, use your Reaction to make one unarmed strike against it.

The reaction attack follows the Granted Attack rule.

When Asura's Rage ends:

- Gain 1 level of Exhaustion.
- Become Hell-Signaled.
- Eat the Flame becomes unavailable until you complete a 10-minute uninterrupted cooling rite after the scene. The rite fails if you take damage, spend Stamina, or perform strenuous activity.

---

Normalized Procedure — Asura's Rage

- Asura's Rage is one temporary bodily state. Its Resistances, Immunity, movement response, damage rider, and Reaction attack all use the feature's Source CL.
- Advantage applies to unarmed attack rolls only. The once-per-turn 3d6 rider is part of one qualifying attack packet and uses the chosen Fire or Necrotic type.
- The once-per-round 10-foot movement resolves after the hostile damage packet. It is voluntary granted movement, does not provoke Opportunity Attacks, and must end legally.
- The Reaction attack is available only when the damaging hostile creature is within your current reach after its damage resolves. It follows the Granted Attack rule and cannot grant another attack.
- The movement response and Reaction attack are separate once-per-round benefits and can both respond to the same qualifying damage if their requirements are met and you have a Reaction.
- When the state ends for any reason, gain 1 Exhaustion, become Hell-Signaled, and disable Eat the Flame as printed. Suppression does not prevent the ending consequences.
- Hell-Signaled functions on the same plane. Qualifying Infernal and Daemonic creatures know your current direction and relative Realm category, but not identity, exact distance, route, equipment, or precise CL.
- The cooling rite can begin only after the scene's immediate conflict has ended. It requires 10 uninterrupted minutes without damage, Stamina spending, strenuous activity, or another cultivation activation. Interruption restarts it. Completing it restores Eat the Flame but does not end Hell-Signaled; only the full 2-hour Cultivation Session ends that state.

- On a hit, the 10d10 is additional attack damage and follows normal critical-hit rules unless another rule changes them. Choose and resolve the Constitution save after all hit damage is determined.
- “Ordinary Resistance to Force” means non-absolute Resistance from a creature statistic, temporary effect, armor, item, or technique. Immunity, a permanent artifact defense, and a rule explicitly immune to physical or Force authority remain.
- When the damage packet is resolved, choose one temporary damage-reduction effect applying to that packet whose Source CL is no higher than yours. It is ignored for this strike. Its action, Reaction, resource, or limited-use cost remains spent unless its rule says otherwise.
- A lower-Source-CL Reaction cannot redirect the strike. It can still perform a different legal function, such as reducing damage, if not otherwise ignored. Equal- or higher-Source-CL redirection resolves normally.
- Double damage to listed unattended targets applies once. A target belonging to several listed categories is not doubled repeatedly.
- The failed-save options are temporary combat impairments, not injuries. The push uses forced-movement rules. The successful-save Reaction denial is the only save result on success.

tianxia.subpath.body.karate.feature.prec.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Precision Strike

You can use this when  You hit with an unarmed strike.  
Cost: 2 Stamina  
Limit: Once per turn  
Saving Throw: Constitution

Choose a target area before the saving throw.

- Arm: On a failed save, Disadvantage on the target's next weapon attack before the start of your next turn.
- Leg: On a failed save, reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
- Breath: On a failed save, it cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.
- Balance: On a failed save, it has Disadvantage on its next Strength or Dexterity saving throw before the start of your next turn.

On a successful save, the target cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn regardless of the selected area.

Normalized Procedure — Precision Strike
- Choose Arm, Leg, Breath, or Balance after the triggering hit but before the save. The labels identify a temporary combat impairment; they do not create an injury, severance, disabled organ, Hidden Injury, or permanent anatomical change.
- A creature does not become ineligible merely because its body plan lacks a human arm, leg, lungs, or ordinary balance organ. Apply the selected printed mechanical effect through the closest equivalent bodily function unless the creature has an explicit Source Rule making it immune to that exact form of physical interference.
- Arm affects only the next weapon attack and is expended whether that attack hits or misses. Leg is a fixed 10-foot Speed reduction and cannot reduce a Speed below 0. Breath prevents Reactions. Balance affects only the next Strength or Dexterity saving throw.
- On a successful save, the Reaction denial replaces the failed-save result; it does not add the selected failed-save result.
- Multiple Precision Strikes from you do not stack the same named effect. Reapplication refreshes its duration or next-roll expenditure.

tianxia.subpath.body.kensei.feature.blad.player_text:
Cultivation Level 3 - Blade Fist

Your unarmed strikes may deal Slashing damage and gain the Finesse property. You may use Dexterity instead of Strength or Constitution for Iron Fist attack and damage rolls.

While wielding a Blade weapon:

- Use Dexterity or Constitution for its attack and damage rolls.
- If using Constitution, use your Cultivation Attack Modifier.
- It is integrated into your Body Refining cultivation.
- Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply to it.

Once per turn when you hit with an unarmed strike or integrated Blade weapon, choose one:

- Deal additional Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
- Reduce the target's Speed by 5 feet until the start of your next turn.
- Prevent it from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Draw or stow one Blade weapon.

Normalized Procedure — Blade Fist
- A Blade is a dagger, sword, saber, cutting-edged axe, or weapon carrying the Blade tag. Record each integrated Blade weapon.
- Granting Finesse to your unarmed strikes permits Strength or Dexterity under the weapon-property rule; this feature additionally permits Constitution through Iron Fist. Choose one ability for each attack and add it once.
- While wielding an integrated Blade, choose Dexterity or Constitution for each attack. Choosing Constitution uses the Cultivation Attack Modifier. The weapon retains its normal item statistics and tags.
- Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply their cultivation-powered and high-authority weapon benefits to the integrated Blade; they do not add a second Iron Fist damage die.
- The once-per-turn rider is chosen after a hit. The additional Proficiency Bonus damage is one packet of Slashing damage. The Speed reduction does not stack with itself. Reaction denial lasts as printed. Drawing or stowing one Blade is part of the hit rider and does not create another object interaction.
- An unarmed strike dealing Slashing damage remains an unarmed strike and natural bodily attack; it does not become a held Blade weapon for a feature requiring one.

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 4 Stamina

For the duration:

tianxia.subpath.body.kensei.feature.seve.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Severing Palm

You can use this when  You hit with an unarmed strike or integrated Blade attack.  
Cost: 4 Stamina  
Limit: Once per turn  
Saving Throw: Constitution

Choose one severing 

- Arm: On a failed save, Disadvantage on all weapon attacks until the end of your next turn.
- Leg: On a failed save, Speed is halved until the end of your next turn.
- Breath: On a failed save, no Reactions until the end of your next turn.
- Flow: On a failed save, Disadvantage on Concentration saving throws and Cultivation Checks made to maintain techniques until the end of your next turn.
- Guard: On a failed save, AC is reduced by 2 until the start of your next turn.

On a successful save, the chosen effect lasts until the start of your next turn. Guard instead reduces AC by 1.

A target cannot suffer multiple instances of the same Severing Palm effect. Reapplication refreshes its duration.

Normalized Procedure — Severing Palm
- The term “severing” describes temporary disruption of bodily combat lines. This feature does not sever anatomy, create an Injury, damage a Foundation, or permanently block a meridian.
- Choose Arm, Leg, Breath, Flow, or Guard after the triggering hit but before the save. Apply the printed result even to a nonhumanoid body through the nearest equivalent function unless an explicit Source Rule grants immunity to that exact impairment.
- Distinct named effects can coexist. The same named effect from you does not stack; reapplication refreshes its duration and uses the new save result.
- Arm affects all weapon attacks for the failed-save duration. Leg halves each applicable Speed after fixed bonuses and before a minimum of 0. Breath prevents Reactions. Flow affects only Concentration saves and Cultivation Checks made to maintain existing techniques. Guard modifies final AC as a penalty and cannot reduce AC below 0.
- On a successful save, the chosen effect still lasts until the start of your next turn, with Guard reduced to -1 AC as printed.
- Ending or repairing an actual bodily Injury does not remove Severing Palm early unless a Source Rule expressly ends temporary technique impairments.

Empty Strike affects Incorporeal creatures, possessing entities, Spirits, and soul-bound Constructs normally.

Normalized Procedure — Empty Strike

- Declare after the unarmed strike hits. Spend Stamina before selecting and resolving the rider.
- The additional Psychic or Force damage is part of the triggering attack's damage packet. Choose its type for each use.
- “Cannot benefit from Invisible” suppresses the mechanical benefits of the Invisible condition for that target during the duration; it does not automatically end the condition, reveal disguises, or make the target visible to creatures that otherwise cannot perceive it.
- A Disadvantage option affects only the next qualifying saving throw in its duration and is then consumed. If no qualifying save occurs, it expires without effect.
- Empty Strike can affect a legally targeted Incorporeal creature, Spirit, possessing entity, or soul-bound Construct without losing damage or riders solely because of that nature. tianxia.subpath.body.kukishin.feature.so.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Soul Severance

You can use this when  You hit with an unarmed strike.  
Cost: 5 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene  
Saving Throw: Charisma

On a failed save, the target is Stunned until the end of your next turn, cannot take Reactions, cannot willingly teleport or become Incorporeal, and has Disadvantage on Concentration saving throws. On a successful save, it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Spiritual Surgery

You may perform Soul Severance as a 10-minute procedure on a willing, Restrained, Incapacitated, or Unconscious target. Choose one:

- Diagnosis: Learn the exact source, Source CL, save DC, duration, and removal procedure of one possession, forced transformation, soul-binding, or spiritual state.
- Exorcism: A possessing entity makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, it is expelled into the nearest legal space.
- Sever Temporary Bond: End one temporary possession, forced transformation, or soul-binding whose Source CL is no higher than yours.
- Suppression: Suppress one higher-CL qualifying effect for 1 minute. This does not remove it.

Normalized Procedure — Soul Severance

- Declare after the unarmed strike hits and spend Stamina before the Charisma save. The save and its riders are part of the same attack activation.
- On failure, all printed restrictions last until the end of your next turn. On success, only Reaction denial applies, with its shorter printed duration.
- The temporary prohibition on willing teleportation or Incorporeality does not cancel an already occupied space or forcibly eject a creature from an existing form. It prevents new willing activations and voluntary use during the duration.
- A target can be affected by only one Soul Severance duration from you at a time; reapplication refreshes rather than stacks.

Normalized Procedure — Spiritual Surgery

- The 10-minute procedure requires uninterrupted physical access to the target and a recorded qualifying spiritual state. The target must remain willing, Restrained, Incapacitated, or Unconscious for the full procedure.
- Diagnosis reveals only the listed mechanical data. A specific equal- or higher-Source-CL concealment can contest one datum through a Cultivation Check; failure tells you that datum is concealed rather than supplying false information.
- Exorcism targets one possessing entity already identified in the target. On a failed Charisma save, use the shared possession-separation procedure and place it in the nearest legal space capable of containing it. This does not destroy, bind, convert, or claim the entity.
- Sever Temporary Bond ends one temporary, unwilling possession, forced transformation, or temporary soul-binding whose Source CL is no higher than yours. It cannot end spirit ancestry, a legal character option, a permanent consensual Bond, a Complete Soul's personhood, or a higher-authority relationship without another rule.
- Suppression selects one qualifying higher-Source-CL effect. It becomes dormant for 1 minute but retains duration and ownership. This option does not remove it, transfer it, or prevent a higher-authority rule from ending the suppression.
- Use the Spirit Awakening Rules Reference or later Universal Cultivation Authority procedures for possession, Complete Souls, spiritual states, and authority collisions.

Cultivation Level 14 - Eye of the Mantis

Bonus Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 3 Stamina

Learn its current and maximum Hit Points, Armor Class, damage Resistances, damage Immunities, whether it is maintaining Concentration, its active physical conditions, and whether Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution is its lowest physical saving throw.

Before rolling the attack's damage, you may choose to deal damage equal only to your ability modifier. If you do, the target has Disadvantage on the Grapple saving throw.

tianxia.subpath.body.nine_star_meridian_.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Falling-Star Descent

Action  
Range: An unoccupied space within 60 feet  
Cost: 2 Stamina and 3 Marks

Move to the selected space without provoking Opportunity Attacks, crossing open air but not solid barriers, total cover, sealed Formations, or spaces too small for you.

Each other chosen creature within 15 feet makes a Dexterity saving throw.

- Failed Save: 6d8 Force or Radiant damage, Prone, pushed 10 feet.
- Successful Save: Half damage, no Prone or push.

The ground becomes Difficult Terrain until repaired. Unattended ordinary objects, temporary barriers, vehicles, structures, and Formation Anchors take double damage.

Normalized Procedure — Falling-Star Descent

- Choose an unoccupied legal space within 60 feet that you can identify. The movement follows one continuous unobstructed route through open air or open space. It is physical celestial movement, not teleportation, and cannot pass through solid barriers, total cover, sealed Formations, or spaces too small for you.
- The movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. If the destination becomes illegal before arrival, stop in the nearest legal space along the route; the impact area is centered on the space where you stop.
- Choose any number of other creatures within 15 feet after arrival. Each makes one Dexterity save and is affected once. Choose Force or Radiant for the activation.
- Resolve damage, Prone, and push after arrival. A push moves directly away from you and stops at the nearest legal space. A successful save prevents Prone and push.
- The impacted ground in the 15-foot area becomes Difficult Terrain. Each 5-foot square can be cleared or repaired under the Body environmental-terrain procedure. This does not automatically create a crater, chasm, or permanent regional damage.
- Eligible unattended objects, temporary barriers, vehicles, structures, and Formation Anchors take double damage once. A surviving obstruction does not prevent the radial impact unless it provides total cover from your arrival space.

tianxia.subpath.body.nine_star_meridian_.player_text:

Reaction

tianxia.subpath.body.oni_blood.feature.b.player_text:
Cultivation Level 6 - Blood Drinker

While Oni Mask or Oni Form is active:

- Once per turn when an unarmed strike damages a Bloodied qualifying hostile creature, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
- When you reduce a qualifying hostile creature to 0 Hit Points with an unarmed strike, regain Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus. This healing can occur once per creature.

Blood Drinker cannot generate healing or Temporary Hit Points from harmless animals, allied creatures, creatures created for resource loops, repeatedly revived or recaptured targets, or creatures that do not qualify under the Qualifying Hostile Creature rule.

Normalized Procedure — Blood Drinker

- Determine whether the target is Bloodied immediately before the qualifying unarmed strike deals damage. A hit that first makes an unbloodied target Bloodied does not satisfy the first bullet for that hit.
- Temporary Hit Points are granted after the damage packet resolves. They follow the normal nonstacking rule.
- The 0-Hit-Point healing resolves after the target is actually reduced to 0 Hit Points and before later corpse, death, or capture procedures. It can occur only once for that creature from you, regardless of revival, transformation, replacement body, or later recapture.
- “Qualifying hostile creature” uses the universal anti-farming rule. A creature created, summoned, revived, healed, captured, or staged primarily to generate this benefit does not qualify.
- Blood Drinker is bodily predation, not soul consumption. It does not capture a soul, steal a Foundation, copy a Sphere, or create harvestable blood authority.

You can use this when  You would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but are not killed outright.  
Cost: 6 Stamina

Action: None

Instead:

- Regain Hit Points equal to half your maximum Hit Points.
- Activate Oni Form without paying its cost, even if it was already used.

“The night did not end. It was simply made too honest to continue.”

To learn this, you need CL 15+, Solar Radiance Form

Cost: 15 cultivation points (your Path resource)

Use Limit: Once per long rest

Transform into an incarnation of sovereign dawn.

gain Fly Speed 60 feet and Hover;

gain Immunity to Radiant damage;

gain Resistance to Necrotic, Fire, and Psychic damage;

shed Bright Light in a 120-foot radius and Dim Light for another 120 feet;

suppress non-Legendary magical Darkness, ordinary illusion concealment, ordinary invisibility, and ordinary fear auras inside your Bright Light;

once per turn when Radiance Strike hits an Unclean target, suppress one visible corruption-derived temporary benefit until the start of your next turn.

Failed Save: Take 4d10 Radiant damage and become Blinded until the start of its next turn.

Successful Save: Take half damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Cultivation Level 5 - Body Tempering

Your body has passed beyond ordinary mortal frailty.

You gain Resistance to nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

This Resistance applies to qualifying damage from mundane weapon attacks, falling, collisions, nonmagical traps, rubble, cave-ins, ordinary machinery, and nonmagical environmental hazards.

An attack or hazard is cultivation-powered rather than mundane when its damage is created or empowered by a Path feature, Subpath feature, Sphere talent, Recorded Art, Forged Technique, Immortal Art, Foundation feature, Method feature, supernatural item power, or another rule explicitly identifying it as magical or cultivation-powered.

Body Tempering does not grant Resistance against cultivation-powered physical damage unless another feature states otherwise.

In addition:

- You have Advantage on saving throws against extreme heat, extreme cold, high altitude, forced marches, starvation, dehydration, and suffocation.
- You can hold your breath for ten times the normal duration.
- Ordinary caltrops, thorns, splinters, and similarly minor environmental hazards cannot damage you unless they are supernatural or part of an active attack or trap.

tianxia.path.body_refining.feature.core_.player_text:
CL10 - Core Tempering Expression

When you enter Core Formation Realm, your accumulated bodily refinement settles into a stable internal expression.

Choose one Core Tempering Expression. Your choice is permanent until you complete a later Realm breakthrough. When you successfully enter Nascent Soul Realm at CL15, you may replace your chosen expression with another before using any CL15 feature.

At CL17, your chosen expression becomes Perfected.

At CL20, choose a second expression. Both expressions function simultaneously, and both use their Perfected benefits.

Golden Bell Circulation

Bonus Action 
Cost: 3 Stamina 
Duration: 1 minute

For the duration:

- Gain +2 AC.
- You have Advantage on checks and saving throws against being pushed, pulled, or knocked Prone.
- Once per round, when Stamina Guard reduces a damage packet to 0, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

The effect ends early if you become Unconscious. Activating Golden Bell Circulation again replaces and refreshes its duration.

Perfected Golden Bell - CL17

While Golden Bell Circulation is active:

- Stamina Guard uses d12s instead of d10s.
- Your Temporary Hit Points from Golden Bell equal twice your Proficiency Bonus.
- You cannot be moved against your will by a creature whose CL is lower than yours unless its feature explicitly ignores bodily anchoring.

A creature of equal or higher CL resolves forced movement normally.

Blood-Furnace Circulation

Once per turn, immediately after you spend one or more Stamina on a feature that successfully resolves, regain Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

If you are at your maximum Hit Points, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus instead.

Blood-Furnace Circulation does not function while you are at 0 Hit Points, cannot be triggered by refunded Stamina or an invalid activation, and functions no more than once per turn.

Perfected Blood Furnace - CL17

The Hit Points or Temporary Hit Points gained become 2 x Proficiency Bonus.

When this feature restores Hit Points, you may also end one ongoing Bleeding state affecting you if that state has a Source CL no higher than your CL.

Mountain-Rending Pulse

Once per turn, immediately after you spend one or more Stamina on a feature that successfully resolves, empower your next Body Refining melee attack before the end of your next turn.

On a hit:

- Deal an additional 1d8 Force damage.
- Choose either to push the target 5 feet or prevent it from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn.

If the empowered attack misses, the empowerment remains until its duration expires.

You cannot hold more than one Mountain-Rending empowerment at a time. Gaining another replaces the previous one.

Perfected Mountain-Rending Pulse - CL17

The additional damage becomes 2d8 Force damage.

On a hit, choose one:

- Push the target 10 feet.
- Knock the target Prone if it fails a Strength saving throw.
- Prevent it from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Deal double damage to an unattended object, temporary barrier, vehicle, structure, or Formation Anchor.

- May deal Force damage instead of their normal damage type.

Your meridians, organs, blood, and nervous system resist contamination and physical collapse.

You gain Advantage on saving throws against the Poisoned condition, disease, Exhaustion caused by physical exertion or environmental exposure, effects that obstruct breathing, and effects that directly disrupt your bodily meridians.

tianxia.path.qi_cultivation.feature.doma.player_text:
CL9 — Domain Armament

A Domain Armament is a movable external Qi focus. It is not a Spirit Awakening Domain.

A Domain Armament may be:

- A projected cultivation construct.
- One specific real weapon bound to your Qi.
- One specific real shield bound to your Qi.

Examples include:

- Sword.
- Spear.
- Needle.
- Bow.
- Bell.
- Brush.
- Fan.
- Seal.
- Mirror.
- Orb.
- Disk.
- Chain.
- Instrument.
- Shield.
- Talisman array.
- Another noncreature weapon or cultivation implement.

Manifest Domain Armament

Bonus Action 
Initial Position: One unoccupied point within 30 feet 
Cost: 1 Qi 
Duration: 1 hour

You may maintain one Domain Armament.

A projected Armament:

- Occupies no space.
- Provides no Cover except through Guard Mode.
- Cannot flank.
- Cannot carry objects.
- Cannot manipulate objects.
- Cannot use unrelated item properties.
- Cannot be targeted unless a rule explicitly affects projected weapons, Qi constructs, or Domain Armaments.
- Ends if you become Unconscious.

Choose Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, or Force damage when it manifests.

Once during each of your turns:

- Move it up to 20 feet without using an action.
- It must remain within 30 feet.

If a projected Armament ends outside range, it moves to the nearest legal point in range.

Binding a Real Weapon or Shield

You may bind one real weapon or shield as your Domain Armament.

Binding Time: 10 uninterrupted minutes while touching the item

The item must satisfy all of the following:

- You own it or have its owner’s permission.
- You are proficient with it or another rule permits its use.
- You meet its attunement and cultivation prerequisites.
- A sentient item consents.
- It is not already bound as another creature’s Domain Armament.

The bond remains until:

- You bind another item.
- You willingly end the bond.
- The item is destroyed.
- A feature explicitly severs the bond.

The actual item alternates between:

- Being wielded.
- Being carried.
- Floating as your Domain Armament.

It is never duplicated.

A Saint-class, Legendary, named, or ancestral item remains the actual item while floating.

Call or Release Bound Item

Move the item between your hand and a floating position:

- As a Bonus Action.
- As part of manifesting Domain Armament.
- At the beginning or end of your Attack action.
- As part of activating an authorized weapon-delivered technique through it.

Calling requires a legal free hand and an unobstructed path.

Releasing requires a legal point within Domain Armament range.

This movement is not teleportation unless another feature says otherwise.

A spatial lock, sealed Formation, total physical restraint, or item-control effect can block it.

Domain Armament Modes

A floating Domain Armament operates in Assault Mode or Guard Mode.

Choose its mode when manifested or released.

Once during each of your turns, change its mode without using an action.

Assault Mode — Domain Armament Attack

Bonus Action

Move the Armament up to 20 feet, then make a Cultivation Attack against one creature within 5 feet.

Projected Armament Hit:

- CL9: 1d8 + key ability modifier
- CL13: 2d8 + key ability modifier
- CL17: 3d8 + key ability modifier

Use the damage type chosen when manifested.

Bound Weapon Attack

Use your Cultivation Attack Modifier and the weapon’s printed enhancement bonus.

On a hit, use the greater of:

- The weapon’s normal damage dice; or
- Your Domain Armament damage dice.

Then add:

- Your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier.
- The weapon’s printed damage bonus.
- Any automatic on-hit property whose trigger is legally satisfied.

The item retains:

- Damage type.
- Enhancement bonus.
- Attunement properties.
- Automatic on-hit properties.
- Material properties.
- Named traits.

A property requiring a separate action, item charge, Attack action, physical grip, stance, or unsatisfied trigger does not activate automatically.

A property saying “while wielding” treats the floating item as wielded unless it explicitly requires physical contact, a free hand, or a stance.

Guard Mode — Projected Shield

A projected shield or defensive form cannot make Domain Armament Attacks.

At the end of your turn, designate one creature within 5 feet as protected until the start of your next turn.

The creature gains:

+2 AC against ranged attack rolls

The protection ends if:

- The creature moves more than 5 feet from the Armament.
- The Armament changes mode.
- The Domain Armament ends.

The bonus:

- Applies to ranged weapon, spell, and cultivation attack rolls.
- Does not apply to melee attacks.
- Does not apply to saving throw effects.
- Does not stack with another shield bonus.
- Stacks with Qi Armor.

Guard Mode — Bound Shield

Use the shield’s printed shield bonus against ranged attacks for the protected creature.

Its enhancement bonus applies.

The floating shield:

- Protects one creature.
- Does not also protect you merely because it is bound.
- Retains appropriate passive properties.
- Can serve as a cultivation focus.

Bound Shield Assault

A bound shield may use Assault Mode.

If it has a printed attack profile, use it.

Otherwise, its Domain Armament Attack deals Bludgeoning or Force damage using normal Domain Armament damage dice.

Bound Item Vulnerability

A bound real item:

- Uses its printed durability.
- Can be targeted by effects explicitly affecting items, weapons, shields, or cultivation implements.
- Can be suppressed, restrained, sealed, trapped, or displaced.

If forced outside Domain Armament range:

- It falls in the nearest legal space.
- Domain Armament benefits are suppressed.
- The bond remains.
- Control returns when it is in range and no blocking effect remains.

---

Cultivation Level 13 — Domain Armament Link

Your Domain Armament improves:

- Control range becomes 60 feet.
- Normal movement becomes 30 feet.
- Domain Armament Attack uses Cultivation Level 13 damage.

Remote Technique Origin

When activating a non-Self Qi Path, Subpath, or Sphere technique, spend 1 additional Qi to originate it from yourself or your Domain Armament.

Measure from the selected origin:

- Range.
- Line of sight.
- Line of effect.
- Cover.
- Cones.
- Lines.
- Areas.
- Touch range when the Armament is within 5 feet.

Remote Technique Origin cannot transmit:

- A consumed physical object.
- A pill or potion that must enter the target’s body.
- A physical talisman unless the Domain Armament carries it legally.
- A weapon attack unless weapon delivery is authorized.
- Direct hand manipulation.
- A Self technique.
- An aura explicitly centered on your body.

It is blocked by:

- Total Cover.
- A sealed Formation.
- A spatial lock.
- A planar boundary.
- An effect explicitly blocking Qi transmission.

A technique uses one origin unless it explicitly permits multiple origins.

Weapon-Delivered Remote Technique

A floating bound weapon may make the required weapon attack when a Source Rule explicitly authorizes weapon delivery.

Determine from the floating weapon:

- Attack range.
- Line of sight.
- Cover.
- Struck point.
- Technique origin.

The item must satisfy every weapon requirement.

A sword cannot deliver a technique requiring a bow. A shield cannot deliver a piercing technique unless it has a legal piercing attack.

CL10 — Golden Core Form

At CL10:

- Qi Armor costs 1 Qi.
- Choose one Golden Core Form.

You may replace the chosen Form after a successful CL15 breakthrough before using your CL15 Nascent Soul feature.

At CL17, your chosen Form becomes Perfected.

At CL20, choose a second Golden Core Form. Both Forms are Perfected.

Stable Golden Core

When Initiative is rolled, if your current Qi is lower than your Proficiency Bonus, regain Qi until it equals your Proficiency Bonus.

At the start of your turn, if your current Qi is lower than your Proficiency Bonus, regain 1 Qi.

Once per round, when a hostile effect would reduce your current Qi, maximum Qi, or restored Qi, reduce that loss by your Proficiency Bonus.

- Start-of-turn recovery becomes 2 Qi.
- Hostile Qi loss reduction becomes 2 × Proficiency Bonus.

Circulating Golden Core

- Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Shift your stance around one creature within your weapon’s reach without provoking an Opportunity Attack from that creature.
- Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
- Move your Domain Armament 10 feet.

- Refunded costs.
- Invalid activations.
- A cost paid solely to activate Circulating Golden Core.

Perfected Circulating Golden Core

Choose two different benefits.

- Temporary Hit Points become 2 × Proficiency Bonus.
- Domain Armament movement becomes 20 feet.

Bonus Action

2 × Proficiency Bonus + key ability modifier

- It requires no Bonus Action.
- It remains once per scene.

Action 
Range: Touch

Choose one poison, disease, or directly caused physical impairment affecting the target.

- Not have the Curse, Tribulation, Foundation Injury, Hidden Injury, Possession, Permanent, or Soul Damage tag.

Effect with Repeat Saves

- End its duration.
- Cure the disease or poison.
- Remove Exhaustion.
- Restore Hit Points.

Qi Cultivation Subpaths

At Cultivation Level 3, choose one Qi Cultivation Subpath for which you have legal access. You gain its features at Cultivation Level 3, Cultivation Level 6, Cultivation Level 10, Cultivation Level 14, and Cultivation Level 18.

| Catalog classification | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Open School | Commonly teachable or institutionally available. Open access does not imply low power. |
| Restricted Scripture | Controlled technical, political, military, medical, inherited, or hazardous instruction. |
| Rare Inheritance | Uncommon structural access, bloodline, vessel, destiny, treasure, or singular transmission. A Rare Variant is a parent-lineage conversion inside this category. |
| Forbidden Variant | A parent-lineage conversion carrying a prohibited, condemned, hazardous, predatory, or politically unacceptable price. Forbidden is not automatically Daemonic. |
| Secret Law | Qualitatively superior law-level authority requiring explicit access and its printed initiation price. |
| Daemonic | A mechanical tag used only when the Source Rule interacts with Corruption, daemonic energy, purification, or anti-daemonic rules. It is orthogonal to social accusations of being “demonic.” |

A character normally has one Subpath progression. Parent and Variant lineages use the executable replacement rules in Shared Qi Subpath Rules R4; they do not provide a second simultaneous Subpath progression.

Record one pending unarmed-strike rider before the end of your next turn; on a hit it adds 4d8 Force to that hit's packet. Reapplication is impossible because the feature is once per scene.

Cultivation Level 18 - Sovereign Reconstruction

You can use this when  You are reduced to 0 Hit Points but are not killed outright.  
Cost: 8 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene  
Action: None

Instead of falling Unconscious normally, your body collapses into a bone cocoon until the start of your next turn.

While inside:

- You are Incapacitated.
- Your Speed is 0.
- You cannot take actions or Reactions.
- Your body cannot be targeted separately from the cocoon.
- You do not make death saving throws.

Bone Cocoon

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 5 x your CL
- Resistance: Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic
- Source CL: Your CL

At the start of your next turn, if the cocoon has at least 1 Hit Point:

- Regain Hit Points equal to half your maximum.
- Stand without spending movement.
- End Prone, Grappled, Restrained, and one Bleeding or temporary physical-injury state on yourself.
- Each hostile creature of your choice within 10 feet makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 6d6 Piercing damage and falling Prone on a failure, or half damage and remaining standing on a success.

If the cocoon reaches 0 Hit Points, reconstruction fails. You remain at 0 Hit Points and begin making death saving throws at the start of your next turn.

Normalized Procedure — Sovereign Reconstruction
- Declare when you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, before Unconsciousness or death saves. This is a 0-Hit-Point replacement and cannot resolve together with Marrow Memory or another replacement of the same event.
- The Bone Cocoon is a Body Asset occupying your current space and matching your size. Your body is contained within it and cannot be targeted separately; an area affecting that space targets the Cocoon normally.
- Damage to the Cocoon does not transfer to you. You retain existing conditions unless the feature ends them on emergence. You make no death saves while the Cocoon has at least 1 Hit Point.
- The Cocoon has no actions, movement, or Reactions. It can be moved, restrained, contained, repaired, or suppressed only when a rule can legally affect a Body Asset. Its printed Resistance and Immunities apply normally.
- At the start of your next turn, check the Cocoon before resolving ordinary start-of-turn effects from your body. If it has at least 1 Hit Point, perform every printed reconstruction step, destroy the Cocoon, and take the turn normally.
- If the Cocoon reaches 0 Hit Points before then, it breaks immediately. You remain at 0 Hit Points in its space, do not receive the reconstruction benefits, and begin normal death-saving-throw timing at the start of your next turn. Excess Cocoon damage does not transfer, but an effect that kills or destroys the contained body explicitly can still do so.
- The emergence burst affects only hostile creatures you choose within 10 feet. Each is affected once. It creates no permanent bone Injury or terrain without another rule.

insight.exorcist-s-calling.player_text:
Exorcist's Calling

Requirements: Spirit Awakening, CL4+ (Cultivation Level), Spiritual Sense
Ability Increase (Level Selection): Increase your Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma score by 1, to the maximum allowed by your current Realm (a stage of cultivation).
Source CL: Your Spirit Awakening CL.

You have learned to diagnose and interrupt invasive spiritual influences before gaining the Path's complete exorcism feature.

Lesser Exorcism

Use an action.
Range: 30 feet
Cost: 2 Resonance
Target: One creature, object, location, manifested spirit, or Spiritual Anchor that you can perceive with Spiritual Sense or Soul Gaze, or one target bearing your Resonance Mark

Choose one Intrusion attached to the target that you can perceive:

- unwilling Possession;
- unwilling or coercive Hosting;
- dream intrusion;
- spiritual contamination;
- imposed emotional corruption;
- memory interference;
- hostile spirit presence; or
- a curse whose Source Rule has a spiritual component.

You cannot target:

- a willing stable Covenant Bond unless both bonded parties consent to separation;
- integrated spirit ancestry or a legal Species, Path, Subpath, Foundation, Method, Origin Insight, or ordinary memory;
- completed death, reincarnation, permanent soul destruction, or divine custody; or
- an artifact, Secret, Immortal, or world-law effect unless its Source Rule permits ordinary exorcism.

Resolution

Make a Spirit Awakening Cultivation Check against the Intrusion's Cultivation Save DC. If it has no printed DC, use the possessing spirit's or creator's Cultivation Save DC. If neither exists, use the Rules Reference fallback Authority DC for the source's Realm.

On a failed check, the Intrusion remains. Learn its broad category, its Source CL band relative to you, and whether it is sustained by a creature, Bond, vessel, location, Domain, or Spiritual Anchor.

On a successful check, compare Source CL:

- 6 or More Lower: End one ordinary temporary Intrusion. For Possession, achieve Grade 2 Separation and place the Intruder in its legal adjacent manifestation, legal vessel, or visible noncontrolling outline. A permanent, Secret, artifact, divine, or explicitly anchored Intrusion is suppressed until the scene ends and reveals one printed release requirement instead.
- 3–5 Lower: Suppress the Intrusion for up to 1 minute while you maintain Concentration. The Host immediately repeats one saving throw the Intrusion allows with Advantage. The Intruder becomes perceptible and cannot conceal its link during suppression.
- Within 2: Suppress the Intrusion until the end of the target's next turn. The Host immediately repeats one allowed saving throw with Advantage. If no repeat save exists, suppression is the complete result.
- 3 or More Higher: Do not suppress it. The Host immediately repeats one allowed saving throw with Advantage. Expose the Intrusion's manifestation and the direction of its sustaining Anchor to your Spiritual Sense until the end of your next turn.

A willing Host may waive resistance made on its behalf. A willing Intruder does not resist separation. If both Host and Intruder oppose separation, use the higher relevant Cultivation Save DC; if only one opposes, use that opponent's DC.

Limits

- A specific Intrusion can be targeted by your Lesser Exorcism only once per round.
- Lesser Exorcism cannot destroy a Complete Soul, transfer spirit ownership, create a Companion Bond, strip integrated ancestry, or remove legal character options.
- It cannot bypass a named rite, material, location, authority, or higher Source CL requirement unless the result expressly satisfies it.

CL13 Improvement

When you gain Spiritual Exorcism from Spirit Awakening:

- Lesser Exorcism costs 1 Resonance;
- its range becomes 60 feet;
- successful suppression against a lower-Source-CL Intrusion does not require Concentration; and
- when you expose an equal- or higher-authority Intrusion, the target has Advantage on its next saving throw against it before the scene ends.

This Insight does not grant the Spirit Companions Sphere and does not replace the Exorcist tradition.
insight.exorcist-s-calling.why: CLARITY3: owner-approved display-only clarity pass; preserve all mechanics.

insight.heart-devil-negotiator.player_text:
Heart-Devil Negotiator

You can bargain with your inner demon when an event would give you Corruption.

Requirements: Daemonic Cultivation and either Spirit Awakening or Wisdom 14+, CL5+ (Cultivation Level)

Ability Increase (Level Selection): Increase your Constitution, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to the maximum allowed by your current Realm (a stage of cultivation).

Bargain with the Inner Demon

No action required.  
Trigger: You would gain one or more Corruption from a single event  
Limit: Once per scene

Make a Wisdom (Insight) check against DC 12 + your current Corruption before applying the triggering Corruption.

Success: Delay the triggering Corruption until the current scene ends. Record its amount and source. When the scene ends, gain all Corruption delayed by this Insight simultaneously. Ending, suppressing, or bargaining with the source does not erase the delayed amount unless that Source Rule expressly removes Corruption already incurred.

Failure: Gain the Corruption immediately and record one Temptation. Choose or roll 1d6:

| d6 | Temptation |
|---:|---|
| 1 | Conceal the Corruption or its source from an ally or authority. |
| 2 | Seize, consume, protect, or study the object or essence that caused it. |
| 3 | Accept a further offer of power, knowledge, or access from the source. |
| 4 | Isolate yourself from anyone likely to interfere. |
| 5 | Spare, obey, imitate, or bargain with the entity behind the Corruption. |
| 6 | Prove your superiority through an unnecessary risk, contest, or display. |

A Temptation is a recorded impulse, not control. It cannot compel an action, impose a condition, or create additional Corruption unless another Source Rule says so. It ends with the scene.

An effect that expressly says its Corruption cannot be delayed overrides this Insight.

TAL_YANG_BASE_SPHERE_ABILITIES.player_text:
BASE SPHERE ABILITIES

The Yang sphere uses Rising Marks. A Rising Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Rising Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Rising Mark represents a motion, wound, breath, oath, technique, or intention that has begun to swell toward completion.
Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Rising Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature, object, or ongoing effect can have only one Rising Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.
A Rising Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked subject is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
Kindled and Overkindled Marks
A Rising Mark has one of two expressions.
Kindled Mark. A Rising Mark on you, a willing creature, an unattended object, or an effect you created is a Kindled Mark. You spend Kindled Marks to help an action complete.
Overkindled Mark. A Rising Mark on an unwilling creature, hostile object, enemy effect, or creature that rejects your assistance is an Overkindled Mark. You spend Overkindled Marks to make hostile exertion overcomplete, exposing or straining the source.
A willing creature may end your Rising Mark on itself at any time, no Action required.
Applying a Rising Mark
You can apply a Rising Mark in three basic ways.
Kindle the Rising. As a Bonus Action, choose yourself or one willing creature, unattended object, or ongoing effect you created within 60 feet that you can perceive. The target gains one Kindled Mark.
Force the Rising. As a Reaction when a creature, object, or effect within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends cultivation points (your Path resource), uses a spell slot, uses a limited feature, teleports, becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Overkindled Mark to the source after the triggering event resolves.
Rising Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Fire, Radiant, or Force damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Overkindled Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Rising Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 (Cultivation Level) | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi becoming too bright, too hot, or too forceful to remain unfinished.
Spending a Rising Mark
Once per round, when a marked subject you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Rising Mark without using an Action. Choose one Completing Response appropriate to the mark.
Kindled Responses
You may use these responses when you spend a Kindled Mark.
Complete Force.
Trigger: the marked subject deals damage. Add 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier to one damage roll. This bonus increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Complete Aim.
Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Add 1d4 to the attack roll, or choose one target making the saving throw and subtract 1d4 from that saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Complete Step.
Trigger: the marked subject begins movement during its turn. Increase one of the subject’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or allow it to stand from Prone without spending movement. At CL 11, the Speed increase becomes 20 feet.
Complete Breath.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points or gains Temporary HP. Increase the amount gained by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier.
Complete Resolve.
Trigger: the marked subject makes a saving throw against an effect that would reduce its Speed, prevent it from taking Reactions, impose Frightened, Paralyzed, Restrained, Stunned, or Unconscious, or suppress its ability to act. Add 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Complete Revelation.
Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll, Wisdom (Perception) check, or Intelligence (Investigation) check against a creature or effect that is Hidden, Invisible, heavily obscured, disguised by illusion, or concealed by a Yin-like technique. The marked subject ignores Disadvantage from not seeing the target for that roll, provided it can still identify the target’s space or general location.
Overkindled Responses
You may use these responses when you spend an Overkindled Mark.
Overheat Force.
Trigger: the marked subject deals damage, makes an attack roll, or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. After the triggering act resolves, the subject takes Fire or Radiant damage equal to 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This damage increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Overexpose.
Trigger: the marked subject becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or benefits from a feature that prevents others from perceiving it. Until the start of your next turn, the subject cannot benefit from being Hidden or Invisible against you, and allies you choose within 60 feet know the subject’s current space if they can perceive the area.
Overcommit Step.
Trigger: the marked subject moves at least 10 feet, teleports, or uses special movement. After the movement resolves, the subject cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If the movement was teleportation and the destination is within 120 feet of you, you know the destination space.
Overgrown Recovery.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores cultivation points (your Path resource), or benefits from regeneration. Until the start of your next turn, the first damage roll against that subject gains a bonus equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Overstrain Technique.
Trigger: the marked subject spends cultivation points (your Path resource), uses a spell slot, activates a limited feature, or uses a named cultivation technique. If the subject uses the same named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability again before the end of its next turn, it gains a Rising Mark immediately after the repeated ability resolves.
Yang Saves
Some Yang features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Cultivation Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC.
Cultivation points are the resource used by your Path: Stamina, Qi, or Resonance.

The Yin sphere uses Waning Marks. A Waning Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Waning Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark represents a motion, technique, wound, breath, or intention that has begun to decline before it finishes expressing itself.

Withdrawing Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Cold or Necrotic damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Waning Mark.

| CL 1-4 (Cultivation Level) | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |

TAL_DAEMONIC_CULTIVATION_BASE_SPHERE_ABI.player_text:
Base Sphere Abilities

When you learn Daemonic Cultivation, you gain Demon Seed, Devour Essence, and Daemonic Augment.
Demon Seed
Use a bonus action.
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: 1 cultivation point (your Path resource) or 1 Stamina
Plant or awaken a Demon Seed in your body, dantian, meridians, or soul. The Seed is a forbidden method-root, not a Demon Core. It does not make you a demon; it opens the second furnace through which the daemonic scripture can breathe.
While Demon Seed is active:
your Daemonic talents may be used;
you gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Daemonic key ability modifier;
once per turn when you hit with a weapon attack, Unarmed Strike, or Cultivation Attack, add 1d4 Necrotic, Psychic, or Force damage;
you have Advantage on saving throws against Frightened;
you have Disadvantage on checks made to appear spiritually pure unless you suppress all visible signs.
At CL 5 (Cultivation Level), the extra damage becomes 1d6.
At CL 11, the extra damage becomes 1d8.
At CL 17, the extra damage becomes 1d10.
When Demon Seed ends, if you used Overdraw during its duration, make a Wisdom saving throw against your Daemonic Save DC. On a failure, gain 1 additional Corruption.
Devour Essence
This ability has multiple modes.
Timing Detail: Bonus Action or Reaction
Range: 30 feet
Cost: None
Use Devour Essence when one of the following happens within range:
a hostile creature is reduced to 0 HP;
a creature fails a saving throw against one of your Daemonic talents;
you score a Critical Hit;
a creature bearing your demonic mark takes damage;
an ongoing summoned, possessed, spirit, fiendish, undead, or demonic effect ends.
You gain 1 Devoured Essence.
You can use Devour Essence once per round.
If the triggering creature is at least your Realm (a stage of cultivation) or has a CR/level equal to at least half your CL, you may instead gain 2 Devoured Essence, but you also gain 1 Corruption.
Daemonic Augment
Use this when its trigger occurs.
Timing Detail: No Action, once per turn
Cost: 1 cultivation point (your Path resource), 1 Stamina, or 1 Devoured Essence
Trigger: You use a sphere talent, weapon attack, Unarmed Strike, or Cultivation Attack that deals damage, imposes a condition, moves a creature, creates a zone, or forces a saving throw.
Twist the technique with daemonic hunger. Choose one:
add Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll;
impose Disadvantage on one Concentration saving throw caused by the triggering effect;
if the triggering effect moves a creature, increase the movement by 5 feet;
if the triggering effect creates Difficult Terrain, one creature that fails a save also cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn;
if the triggering effect deals Necrotic, Psychic, Fire, Poison, Acid, Force, or weapon damage, ignore ordinary Resistance to one of those damage types for that instance;
mark one damaged creature until the start of your next turn. The first time you damage the marked creature before the mark ends, gain 1 Devoured Essence.
Daemonic Augment may modify non-Daemonic sphere talents, but only once per turn. This is one of the main reasons the sphere is forbidden.
Cultivation points are the resource used by your Path: Stamina, Qi, or Resonance.
TAL_DAEMONIC_CULTIVATION_BASE_SPHERE_ABI.why: CLARITY3: owner-approved display-only clarity pass; preserve all mechanics.

SECT_STEWARDSHIP_BASE_STANDING.player_text:
Standing

Standing measures how an institution currently recognizes you.
Standing is not cultivation Realm (a stage of cultivation), social class, noble rank, or universal reputation. It is local and contextual.
There are five ordinary Standing grades.
No Standing. You are a stranger, guest, prisoner, petitioner, or unknown worker.
Servant Standing. You may perform basic labor, receive food or shelter, and be ordered around.
Outer Standing. You are trusted for ordinary duties, simple missions, shared facilities, and basic records.
Inner Standing. You are trusted with restricted duties, better instruction, inner facilities, low-grade resources, and sensitive errands.
Core Standing. You are trusted with disciples, stores, restricted archives, important missions, hall authority, or a named courtyard.
Some institutions may also recognize Elder Standing, Guest Elder Standing, Lineage Heir Standing, Clan Standing, Official Standing, or other campaign-specific statuses. These are story positions and are not automatically gained from this sphere.
When you learn Sect Stewardship, choose one institution where you have Servant or Outer Standing, subject to GM approval. If the campaign begins before you have joined any group, you instead gain the Petitioner status and can use the sphere to earn your first recognized place.

CL20 (Cultivation Level) — Immortal of Qi
You recover Qi each turn, maintain twin Domain Armaments, and gain perfected forms and immortal physiology.
Immortal Circulation

At the start of each of your turns, regain 5 Qi.

This functions in spiritually barren environments unless an effect explicitly suppresses Immortal circulation.

Permanent Nine Heavens Gaze

Nine Heavens Gaze is always active, requires no Action or Qi, and remains suppressible.

Twin Domain Armaments

You may maintain two Domain Armaments.

Manifest or release both through the same Bonus Action for 1 Qi.

Each may have:

- A separate projected form.
- A separate bound real item.
- A separate damage type.
- A separate mode.

Once during each of your turns, move both normally.

Twin Assault

When using your Bonus Action to attack:

- Make one Domain Armament Attack with each Armament in Assault Mode.
- Resolve them separately.
- Once-per-turn additional effects apply once across both attacks unless explicitly stated otherwise.
- A weapon-delivered technique applies to the first qualifying attack unless explicitly extended.
- Neither attack can generate another Domain Armament Attack.

Twin Guard

Two shield Armaments may protect two different creatures.

The same creature cannot add two shield bonuses from Twin Domain Armaments.

Remote Origins

Choose one Domain Armament as the origin of a technique unless it explicitly permits multiple origins.

Complete Cultivated Response

Learn all three Defensive Disciplines.

Second Golden Core Form

Choose a second Golden Core Form.

Both Forms are Perfected.

Immortal Physiology

You do not age or die from old age, and you do not require food, drink, air, or sleep. You still need rests and Cultivation Sessions to recover features whose rules require them.
