tianxia.path.spirit_awakening.feature.as.player_text:
CL7 — Astral Projection

Use an action.
Cost: 4 Resonance 
Duration: Up to 10 minutes 
Concentration: No

Project your spirit from your body.

Body and Range

Your body becomes Unconscious and remains a living creature in its space. It can be moved, damaged, healed, restrained, protected, or killed normally. Your projected spirit can travel up to 300 feet from your body. At CL15, this range becomes 1 mile.

The projection ends if:

- you return to your body;
- you dismiss it without an action;
- the duration expires;
- your body takes damage;
- your projected spirit takes damage;
- your body dies;
- you become unable to maintain a coherent soul connection;
- body and projection are separated by a barrier that explicitly blocks or severs soul connection.

When the projection ends normally, it returns by the shortest legal spiritual route. If no legal route exists because a barrier traps it, the projection remains adjacent to that barrier and you are Incapacitated until the barrier is opened, overcome, or the connection is otherwise resolved.

One Creature, Two Positions

Your body and projection are two positions of the same creature, not two creatures.

- You have one Hit Point total, one condition set, one turn, one action economy, and one Concentration limit.
- An activation cannot affect both positions as though they were separate targets.
- Damage to either position is damage to you and ends Astral Projection after that damage resolves.
- Healing either position heals you once.
- An effect attached to you remains attached unless its own rules require a body or a projected spirit.

Projected Spirit

While projected:

- You retain your senses, Spiritual Sense, Read the Spirit, and Soul Gaze.
- You can communicate telepathically with a willing creature within 30 feet.
- You have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover.
- During a move, you can pass through creatures and up to 5 feet of nonmagical material, but cannot end inside a creature or object.
- Wards, Seals, Formations, consecrated boundaries, spirit prisons, Domains, and Source Rules that block astral travel can stop you.
- You are invisible to ordinary sight but visible to spiritual perception and spirit-revealing effects.
- You cannot manipulate ordinary physical objects.
- You cannot make attacks, activate hostile techniques, manifest a Domain, command a full Companion, use an item, or affect the physical world unless another Source Rule expressly permits it.

An effect that can target spirits can target your projection. Use your normal AC, Hit Points, saving throws, and defenses.

Astral Projection does not create a Soul Fragment, Companion, independent manifestation, second origin for a technique, or separately acting copy of you.

---

tianxia.path.spirit_awakening.feature.im.player_text:
CL20 — Immortal Spirit

Your awakened soul becomes an immortal spiritual structure rather than a mortal consciousness dependent upon one body.

Ageless Soul

You cease aging unless you choose otherwise. Ordinary aging cannot reduce your abilities or kill you.

You do not require food, drink, air, or sleep to keep your soul alive, though your current body may still require them unless a separate feature changes its physiology. You still require rests and Cultivation Sessions to recover features whose rules require them.

Sovereign Identity

An ordinary effect and any effect with lower Source CL cannot, against your will:

- Charm or Frighten you;
- possess or coercively Host within you;
- permanently alter or erase your memory;
- replace your identity;
- consume, destroy, imprison, redirect, or prevent the passage of your Complete Soul;
- permanently sever you from your Soul Anchor.

Equal- or higher-authority effects use their printed procedure. If no procedure is printed, make a Wisdom saving throw against the effect’s save DC; if it has none, use a Cultivation Check contest. Success prevents the attempted permanent result but does not destroy the source.

This protection does not make you immune to persuasion, grief, voluntary bargains, chosen Hosting, chosen memory alteration, lawful consequences, self-created Heart Demons, or the ordinary consequences of your own decisions.

Continue Without the Body

If your body dies while your Complete Soul remains free, you persist as a coherent Unbodied spirit for up to 30 days.

During this state:

- You can perceive and communicate.
- You can use Spiritual Sense, Read the Spirit, and Soul Gaze.
- You cannot make hostile attacks, spend Resonance, manifest a Domain, command a full Companion, manipulate ordinary objects, or activate techniques unless a Source Rule specifically permits bodyless action.
- You can travel as Astral Projection with no distance limit on the same plane, but wards, Domains, spiritual boundaries, and routes still apply.
- You remain one Complete Soul and are not a Companion, Cultivation Asset, or Soul Fragment.

If you are imprisoned, claimed, reincarnated, destroyed, or prevented from reaching an Anchor by an equal- or higher-authority Source Rule, resolve that rule before Return to the Anchor.

Immortal Restoration Capacity

Limit: Once per 28 days

Return to the Anchor and Call Back the Departed use the same capacity. Using either prevents use of the other until 28 days have passed.

Return to the Anchor

While bodyless, spend 7 uninterrupted days at your Soul Anchor, a compatible prepared spirit vessel, or a location explicitly accepted by your Soul Anchor.

If your death and any effect blocking return have lower Source CL, you return automatically in a recreated body with:

- 1 Hit Point;
- 0 Resonance;
- 3 levels of Exhaustion;
- your Path, Subpath, known Spheres, talents, Method, Foundation, Soul Anchor, Insights, and learned techniques intact unless the effect that killed you expressly damaged one of them.

If the death effect or return barrier is within 2 Source CL and has no printed return procedure, make one Cultivation Check against its save DC at the end of the 7 days. If it has no DC, use the Authority DC for its Realm from Spiritual Exorcism.

- Success: You return as above.
- Failure: You do not expend the 28-day capacity. Learn the exact Anchor, authority, or printed condition preventing return. You cannot retry until that condition changes.

If the death effect or return barrier is 3 or more Source CL higher, you cannot return unless its printed recovery condition has already been met. The 7-day attempt reveals that condition but does not expend the 28-day capacity.

A destroyed Complete Soul, completed reincarnation, or voluntary refusal to return cannot be bypassed by this feature.

Call Back the Departed

Time: 8 hours 
Cost: 10 Resonance, paid when the rite begins 
Target: One willing dead creature whose Complete Soul remains reachable

You require at least one:

- the body or meaningful remnant;
- the creature’s true or chosen name;
- its Soul Anchor or equivalent identity Anchor;
- a relic, oath, descendant, bonded spirit, or location with a profound recorded connection to it.

If the soul is free and the death effect has lower Source CL than this feature, restore the creature in a whole body with 1 Hit Point and 3 levels of Exhaustion.

If the death effect or custody is within 2 Source CL, make a Cultivation Check against its save DC. If it has no DC, use the Authority DC for its Realm.

- Success: Restore the creature as above.
- Failure: The rite does not expend the 28-day capacity or its Resonance cost. Learn the exact barrier or printed recovery condition. You cannot retry until it changes.

If the death effect or custody is 3 or more Source CL higher, the rite cannot restore the creature unless its printed recovery condition has already been met. The rite reveals that condition but does not invent a quest, payment, sacrifice, or exception.

Call Back the Departed cannot restore a creature that refuses, has completed reincarnation, whose Complete Soul has been permanently destroyed, or whose Source Rule declares the death final against this authority.

---

CL9 — Soul Vessel

You can create a stable sympathetic vessel for one spiritual relationship.

Create or Replace the Vessel

Time: 10 minutes 
Cost: 2 Resonance 
Target: One Tiny nonliving object you touch

The object becomes your Soul Vessel, a Spirit Cultivation Asset. It may be a doll, name tablet, folded paper figure, mirror shard, prayer strip, bead, thread knot, mask, bell, carved seal, weapon tassel, reliquary, or another object capable of carrying your spiritual imprint.

You can have only one Soul Vessel. Creating another causes the previous vessel to become an ordinary object and ends its Vessel Imprint.

When separate and legally targetable, the vessel has:

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC.
- Hit Points: 4 × Proficiency Bonus.
- Immunities: Psychic and Poison damage; Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned, Prone, and ordinary bodily conditions.
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL.

While worn or carried, use the normal rules for targeting a worn or carried object. Reducing the vessel to 0 Hit Points destroys its cultivated structure, ends its imprint, and leaves an ordinary broken object. This does not damage your soul or the imprinted target.

Create a Vessel Imprint

Use an action.
Range: 60 feet 
Cost: 3 Resonance 
Target: One willing creature, or one creature Resonance Marked by you

An unwilling target makes a Charisma saving throw.

Successful Save: No Vessel Imprint is created. The target knows you attempted the link and suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect until the start of your next turn. 
Failed Save or Willing Target: The Soul Vessel records a sympathetic imprint of the target.

A Vessel Imprint is not a Soul Fragment, copied soul, possession link, ownership claim, memory copy, or Spirit Bond.

Duration

- A willing target’s imprint persists until you dismiss it, replace it, the target withdraws consent as an Action, the vessel is destroyed, or a Source Rule severs it.
- An unwilling target’s imprint lasts until the end of the scene. The target can also use an Action to repeat the Charisma saving throw, ending the imprint on a success.

The vessel can hold only one imprint.

Imprint Benefits

While the imprint persists:

- The target bears your Resonance Mark, and that mark does not expire from its ordinary duration.
- While target and vessel are on the same plane and within 1 mile, you know the direction from the vessel to the target, but not exact distance or a route through spiritual concealment.
- You can use Soul Gaze on the target from the vessel at a range of 1 mile without ordinary line of sight. Total spiritual concealment, a ward that severs sympathetic links, or a higher-authority boundary still blocks it.
- The imprint supplies identity and direction only. It does not let another feature ignore its own range, cover, target, consent, or Source CL requirements.

Vessel Ward

Use a reaction.
You can use this when A willing imprinted target within 60 feet of the vessel fails an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw against a spiritual, mental, emotional, dream, memory, possession, or identity effect. 
Cost: 2 Resonance 
Limit: Once per round

Add your Proficiency Bonus to the saving throw, potentially turning failure into success.

Vessel Ward cannot modify a death saving throw, cannot add Proficiency Bonus twice, and cannot combine with Soulward Response on the same saving throw.

Sympathetic Rite at CL13

After you gain Spiritual Exorcism, a willing imprinted target within 1 mile can be the target of your Deep Exorcism Rite without being touched. Increase the rite’s Resonance cost by 2. A barrier that blocks the Vessel Imprint also blocks the rite.

This remote rite cannot target an unwilling Host or Intruder, cannot establish a new possession target, and cannot exceed the normal authority of Spiritual Exorcism.

---

Cultivation Level 18 - Calamity Briar Incarnation

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 7 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

Gain Demon Spines to maximum.

For the duration:

- Become Large if smaller.
- Unarmed reach +10 feet.
- Resistance to all damage except Fire, Psychic, and Void.
- Unarmed strikes deal 1d12 before modifiers.
- Once per turn on a hit, additional 4d8 Piercing or Slashing.
- Gain 1 Demon Spine at the start of each turn.
- Maximum Spines +3.
- Healing reduction applies only at 6 or more Spines.

Forest of Impalement

Action  
Area: 30-foot-radius sphere centered on you  
Cost: 4 Demon Spines  
Saving Throw: Dexterity

- Failed Save: 8d8 Piercing, Restrained, Bleeding, and lifted up to 10 feet.
- Successful Save: Half damage, pushed 10 feet, not Restrained.

A Restrained creature repeats the Dexterity save at the end of each turn, ending the state and falling safely to the nearest legal space on a success.

The thorn forest remains until the start of your next turn and is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures.

Normalized Procedure — Calamity Briar Incarnation

- On activation, gain Spines to the transformed maximum after increasing that maximum by 3. Become Large if smaller using transformation and legal-space procedures.
- The printed +10-foot reach is the transformation's reach increase and does not stack with Crown of Black Thorns' +5-foot reach unless the source explicitly says both apply; use the higher +10-foot increase.
- Resistance excludes Fire, Psychic, and Void. The 1d12 unarmed die replaces the normal base die; the once-per-turn 4d8 rider is separate.
- Gain 1 Spine at the start of each turn as a direct gain, even if the ordinary once-per-round gain flag is already used. Healing reduction uses the temporary 6-Spine threshold.
- Forest of Impalement: The Action creates a 30-foot-radius projected Body Field centered on you until the start of your next turn. Each affected creature saves once.
- On failure deal 8d8 Piercing, apply Restrained and Bleeding, and lift the target up to 10 feet vertically if a legal space exists. On success deal half, push 10 feet directly away, and do not Restrict.
- A Restrained creature repeats the Dexterity save at the end of each turn. On success it ends this restraint and moves or falls to the nearest legal supporting space without taking falling damage from the feature's own lift.
- The Field is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures and moves with you because it remains centered on you. It creates no permanent terrain, harvestable demon-wood, or automatic Injury.

---

tianxia.subpath.body.bojutsu.feature.hea.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - Heavenly Staff Barrier

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 6 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- Your Staff reach increases by another 5 feet.
- Gain one additional Reaction each round, usable only for a Staff Opportunity Attack, Deflecting Staff, or another Staff feature.
- Hostile creatures provoke Opportunity Attacks when entering your reach.
- A creature hit by your Opportunity Attack has its Speed reduced to 0 for the remainder of the turn.
- You and allies within 10 feet gain Half Cover against ranged weapon attacks and physical projectiles.

Once per turn after hitting with a Staff attack, choose one:

- Push the target 10 feet.
- Move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Prevent the target from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Gain +1 AC until the start of your next turn.

---

Normalized Procedure — Heavenly Staff Barrier
- You must wield a Staff to receive its reach, Opportunity Attack, Deflecting Staff, and cover benefits. If you cease wielding one, those benefits become dormant while the duration continues and resume when you wield one again.
- Reach geometry. During the barrier, your Staff reach is increased by 5 feet outside your turn and by a total of 10 feet during your turn: 5 feet from Staff Form and another 5 feet from this feature. This lets entry into the barrier reach provoke as printed.
- The additional Reaction refreshes at the start of each round and can be spent only on a Staff Opportunity Attack, Deflecting Staff, or a Reaction explicitly identified as a Staff feature. It does not remove any once-per-round limit.
- A hostile creature provokes when it voluntarily enters your current Staff reach. Forced movement, teleportation, appearing in place, and the reach expanding around a creature do not provoke unless another rule says they do.
- On a Staff Opportunity Attack hit, Speed becomes 0 only for the remainder of the current turn. It does not end a teleport already completed or retroactively cancel movement before the hit.
- The 10-foot Half Cover aura moves with you, requires no action, and applies only against ranged weapon attacks and physical projectiles. A creature receives the benefit while within the aura at the instant the attack is resolved.
- The once-per-turn hit rider is chosen after a Staff hit resolves. The 10-foot self-movement requires a legal route and does not provoke. The AC option lasts exactly until the start of your next turn and does not stack with itself.

---

player_evidence.Heavenly Staff Barrier (GM): one additio: While Heavenly Staff Barrier lasts, you gain one additional Reaction each round, usable only for a Staff Opportunity Attack, Deflecting Staff or another Staff feature. Hostile creatures provoke a Staff Opportunity Attack when they enter your reach. You also have Half Cover against non-weapon physical projectiles. Resolve these benefits by hand, including a Staff Opportunity Attack when your usual attack is unarmed. When your Staff Opportunity Attack hits a moving creature, its Speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn. The game does not undo movement already completed, so stop the creature at the space where it was hit.

Cultivation Level 3 - Staff Form

Gain proficiency with Staff weapons.

While wielding a Staff weapon:

- Use Constitution instead of Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls.
- You may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier for its attack rolls.
- It is integrated into your Body Refining cultivation.
- Its reach increases by 5 feet during your turn.
- Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply to it.

This does not grant the Spear or Weapons Sphere.

Normalized Procedure — Staff Form
- Staff record. A Staff is a quarterstaff or a weapon carrying the Staff tag. Record the specific weapon integrated by this feature. Its item properties, enhancement, damage type, handedness, and other tags remain unchanged unless this Subpath expressly changes them.
- Ability and attack choice. For each Staff attack, choose Constitution or another ability the weapon already permits. If you choose Constitution, use the Cultivation Attack Modifier and Constitution for damage. The same attack cannot add two ability modifiers unless another rule expressly permits it.
- Integrated weapon. The wielded Staff is an integrated weapon while you wield it. Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply their cultivation-powered, adamantine, Force-damage, and object-damage permissions; they do not replace the Staff's normal damage die with the Iron Fist die unless another Source Rule explicitly does so.
- Turn-limited reach. The 5-foot increase applies to Staff attacks and Staff features only during your own turn. It does not enlarge your ordinary threatened reach for Opportunity Attacks outside your turn. Heavenly Staff Barrier changes this geometry as stated in its normalized procedure.
- No Sphere grant. Staff Form does not grant a Sphere, Sphere talent, Recorded Art, or proficiency with another Polearm.

tianxia.subpath.body.bojutsu.feature.sta.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Staff of One

While wielding a Staff weapon:

- Gain +1 AC.
- Gain Advantage against being Disarmed.
- Gain Advantage on Opportunity Attacks made with the Staff.

Deflecting Staff

Reaction  
You can use this when  You or an ally within 5 feet takes damage from a ranged weapon attack or physical projectile.  
Cost: 1 Stamina  
Limit: Once per round

Reduce the damage by 2d10 + Constitution modifier.

If this reduces the damage to 0, choose one:

- Catch the projectile if it is small enough to hold.
- Deflect it into an unoccupied space within 15 feet.
- Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Grant the protected ally Half Cover until the start of your next turn.

Deflecting Staff does not block a ray, beam, purely energetic projectile, or save-based area effect.

Normalized Procedure — Staff of One
- The +1 AC requires you to be wielding a Staff. It is an AC bonus, not a base AC calculation, and does not stack with another instance of Staff of One.
- Advantage against being Disarmed applies to checks and saving throws made specifically to retain the Staff. It does not prevent theft while you are helpless or the destruction of the weapon by a legal higher-authority effect.
- The Opportunity Attack Advantage applies only when the attack is made with the Staff.
- Deflecting Staff timing. Declare after the triggering ranged weapon attack or discrete physical projectile has determined damage but before that packet reduces Hit Points. Apply the reduction as an other flat reduction under the shared damage order.
- “Physical projectile” means a discrete material projectile whose path can be intercepted, including ordinary ammunition, thrown weapons, stones, needles, bolts, and comparable manifested matter. It excludes rays, beams, purely energetic bolts, sound, gaze effects, save-based areas, and effects whose rule says they cannot be physically intercepted.
- If a mixed damage packet qualifies because the attack is delivered by a physical projectile, reduce the entire triggering packet. A separate explosion, poison cloud, curse, or area effect created after impact is not canceled unless its Source Rule says interception prevents it.
- If damage becomes 0, choose exactly one printed option. Catching requires a discrete object small enough for one free hand and does not duplicate ammunition or an item. Deflecting into a space ends the triggering attack against its original target; it does not make an attack against another creature. The 5-foot movement must end in a legal space. Half Cover applies only to the protected ally and lasts as printed.
- Deflecting Staff remains once per round even if another feature grants an additional Reaction.

player_evidence.Advantage on checks specifically to reta: You have Advantage on checks specifically to retain the Staff. Apply this Advantage by hand.
player_evidence.Deflecting Staff: non-weapon discrete ph: Deflecting Staff can intercept discrete physical projectiles, including those delivered without a weapon. Resolve those projectiles and attacks combining several separate effects by hand. Rays, beams, purely energetic projectiles and save-based areas cannot be intercepted.
player_evidence.Zero-damage catch/deflect item transfer: If Deflecting Staff reduces damage to 0, catching a projectile small enough for one free hand or deflecting it into an unoccupied space within 15 feet is resolved by hand. The result menu handles legal 5-foot movement without provoking Opportunity Attacks, or the protected ally's Half Cover against ranged attacks until the start of your next turn. Apply that Half Cover to eligible melee attacks and Dexterity saving throws by hand.

tianxia.subpath.body.drunken_fist.featur.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Empty Cup

Reaction  
You can use this when  An attack roll hits you.  
Cost: 2 Stamina  
Limit: Once per round

The attacker rerolls the attack with Disadvantage and uses the new result.

After the reroll resolves, move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. During this movement, you may fall Prone, stand from Prone, move through one hostile creature's space as Difficult Terrain, or end in an unoccupied space on the opposite side of the attacker.

If the rerolled attack can still reach your new space, resolve it normally. Otherwise, it misses.

Normalized Procedure — Empty Cup

- Declare after an attack roll has hit but before damage or hit riders resolve. The reroll replaces the original attack roll even if the new result is higher.
- Determine the rerolled result against your Armor Class before moving, but do not apply damage yet. Then take the granted movement. After movement, recheck the same attack's legal target, reach or range, line of effect, and cover from the attacker's unchanged origin.
- If the reroll misses your Armor Class, the attack misses regardless of movement. If it would hit but can no longer legally reach or target your new space, it misses. Otherwise, resolve the attack and its riders against you normally.
- Passing through one hostile creature's space does not permit you to end there and does not let you pass through an effect that physically blocks passage. The “opposite side” space must be adjacent to the attacker and legal for you.
- This movement occurs during the triggering attack's resolution and cannot itself trigger Empty Cup again.

Cultivation Level 18 - Heavenly Drunk

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 6 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- Gain Advantage on Dexterity saving throws.
- Opportunity Attacks against you have Disadvantage.
- Standing from Prone costs no movement.
- Crawl at your full Speed.
- Move through hostile creature spaces as Difficult Terrain.
- Once per round when an enemy misses you, move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Use Falling Fist once per round without spending your Reaction.
- Once per turn after intentionally falling Prone, gain +2 AC until the start of your next turn.

The reaction-free Falling Fist still follows the Granted Attack rule.

Normalized Procedure — Heavenly Drunk

- “Use Falling Fist without spending your Reaction” removes only the Reaction cost. Falling Fist remains limited to once per round total, whether used normally or through this feature.
- The once-per-round movement when an enemy misses you requires no action and occurs after that attack is fully resolved. A miss created by Empty Cup qualifies, but movement from the same miss occurs only once under this bullet.
- Moving through a hostile space treats each such space as Difficult Terrain and still requires enough movement. You cannot end in an occupied space.
- The +2 AC begins immediately after you intentionally become Prone and lasts until the start of your next turn. Repeated intentional falls refresh but do not stack it. Being knocked Prone unwillingly does not qualify.

---

Cultivation Level 6 - Gilded Bones

When using Stamina Guard, choose one die type for all dice spent against that damage packet:

- Standard Guard: 1d10 per Stamina.
- Gilded Guard: 2d8 per Stamina.

Once per round, if damage remains after using Gilded Guard, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus after the damage resolves.

In addition:

- You take no falling damage from falls of 60 feet or less.
- Gain Advantage against effects that crush, fracture, or break your bones.

Normalized Procedure — Gilded Bones
- When activating Stamina Guard against one damage packet, choose Standard Guard or Gilded Guard before rolling any reduction dice. Every Stamina die spent for that activation uses the chosen expression.
- Gilded Guard replaces 1d10 per Stamina with 2d8 per Stamina; it does not roll both. All other Stamina Guard timing, maximum spend, Reaction cost, and damage ordering remain.
- After the complete triggering damage packet resolves, if at least 1 damage reduced your Hit Points and you have not gained these Temporary Hit Points this round, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to Proficiency Bonus. They do not reduce the triggering packet retroactively and follow ordinary nonstacking rules.
- Falls of 60 feet or less deal no falling damage. A fall longer than 60 feet uses the normal full falling-damage procedure; this feature does not subtract 60 feet from it.
- Bone-protection Advantage applies to checks and saves resisting crushing, fracturing, or bone-breaking. It does not prevent a higher-authority explicit Injury without a save.

Normalized Procedure — Golden Sheen

tianxia.subpath.body.heaven_answering_ad.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - Perfect Counter-Evolution

Reaction  
You can use this when  You take a valid unadapted damage type or fail a save imposing an eligible condition.  
Cost: 2 Stamina  
Limit: Once per round

- Damage Response: Gain the Adaptation before damage is finalized and apply its benefits to the triggering packet.
- Affliction Response: Gain the Affliction Adaptation and reroll the failed save, using the new result.

Return the Lesson deals 4d8 Force instead of 2d8.

You still cannot adapt to Void, untyped damage, maximum-Hit-Point loss, aging, Realm Suppression, CL reduction, permanent identity rewriting, or an effect explicitly barring adaptation.

Normalized Procedure — Perfect Counter-Evolution

- Declare the Damage Response after an unadapted valid damage type in a hostile packet is identified but before damage is finalized. Spend 2 Stamina and choose one valid type in that packet.
- Create the Adaptation immediately, replacing an existing record if capacity requires. Apply its Cultivation Level 14 benefit to the triggering packet: automatic Resistance for listed ordinary types, or twice-Proficiency-Bonus reduction for Force or Psychic.
- Perfect Counter-Evolution itself does not also activate the 1-Stamina Flesh Remembers Pain Reaction; one Reaction cannot pay both features. Force and Psychic therefore receive their printed flat reduction, not packet Resistance, from this response.
- Declare the Affliction Response after failing a save that would impose an eligible condition but before applying that condition. Spend 2 Stamina, create the Adaptation, and reroll the same save against the same DC. Use the new result.
- On success, do not apply conditions or riders imposed only on failure. On failure, resolve the failure and retain the new Affliction Adaptation for later ending saves.
- Return the Lesson's damage becomes 4d8; this replaces 2d8.
- The printed prohibited categories remain absolute. A broad “adapt to anything” interpretation cannot override them or a higher-authority Source Rule that expressly bars adaptation.

---

Cultivation Level 10 - Swallow the Technique

Reaction  
You can use this when  You are affected by a ranged attack, line, cone, burst, other area effect, or hostile technique that forces a save and deals a valid stored type.  
Cost: 3 Stamina  
Limit: Once per round

Resolve the attack or save normally, then reduce all valid stored damage types in the effect by 4d10 + Constitution modifier.

If every valid type is reduced to 0:

- You suffer no non-damage rider that applies only when the effect deals damage.
- Gain 2 Devoured Essence after resolution, divided among valid types present.

Conditions applying regardless of damage still resolve.

Cannot consume a melee attack, effect dealing only physical weapon damage, a persistent zone as a whole, permanent artifact effect, or technique explicitly barring consumption. It may reduce one triggering instance from a persistent zone.

Normalized Procedure — Swallow the Technique

- Declare after the ranged attack, save result, or affected area is known but before valid damage is applied to you. Spend 3 Stamina and the Reaction.
- Resolve the triggering attack or save normally, including whether you are a legal target. Then roll 4d10 + Constitution modifier once and reduce the combined valid stored-type damage portions of that one instance by the result, allocated by you among those valid portions.
- Invalid physical-only, Void, untyped, maximum-Hit-Point-loss, and expressly barred portions remain. This feature does not erase the entire activation, other targets, a persistent zone, or non-damage consequences that apply regardless of damage.
- If every valid damage portion in your instance becomes 0, ignore only riders that explicitly require the effect to deal damage to you. Conditions or movement that apply on a hit, failed save, presence in the area, or regardless of damage still resolve.

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature within your reach targets you with a melee attack.  
Cost: 3 Stamina  
Limit: Once per round  
Saving Throw: Strength

The target makes the saving throw before resolving its attack roll.

On a failed save, choose one:

- Redirect the attack toward another legal creature within the attacker's reach, using the original attack roll.
- Move the attacker up to 10 feet. If you are no longer within its reach, the attack misses.
- Knock the attacker Prone. The triggering attack misses.

On a successful save, resolve the attack normally. If it hits, reduce its damage by 2d8 + Constitution modifier.

Harmonious Body cannot redirect an area effect or environmental hazard.

Normalized Procedure — Harmonious Body

- Declare after you are targeted but before the triggering attack roll. The attacker makes the Strength save immediately.
- If you redirect the attack, choose a legal creature within the attacker's current reach and legal for the original attack. Then the attacker rolls the original attack against the new target using all modifiers and conditions that would have applied. The attack is still the attacker's activation, not yours.
- If you move the attacker, choose a legal destination within 10 feet. Recheck whether you are a legal target and within reach after movement. If not, the attack misses; otherwise, roll it normally.
- If you knock the attacker Prone, the triggering attack misses without an attack roll. Prone then applies normally.
- On a successful save, resolve the original attack. If it hits, reduce its damage by 2d8 + Constitution modifier as an other flat reduction under the Body Refining Shared Procedures damage order. This cannot reduce damage below 0.
- A redirected attack cannot be redirected again by Harmonious Body, Empty Body, or another copy of this same procedure.

Cultivation Level 18 - Sword Saint Incarnation

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 7 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- Gain a Fly Speed of 40 feet and Hover.
- Gain +2 AC.
- Your unarmed strikes and integrated Blade attacks may deal Force or Slashing damage.
- Your critical-hit range becomes 19-20.
- Once per turn when you hit, deal an additional 3d8 Force or Slashing damage.
- Your melee reach increases by 5 feet.
- Move through hostile creature spaces as Difficult Terrain.
- Opportunity Attacks against you have Disadvantage.

The first time during a turn that a hostile creature enters your reach or starts its turn there, it makes a Dexterity saving throw.

- Failed Save: It takes 3d8 Force or Slashing damage and either cannot take Reactions or has its Speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
- Successful Save: It takes half damage and its Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the start of its next turn.

---

Normalized Procedure — Sword Saint Incarnation
- This is a temporary Body transformation. Record activation, current integrated Blade, Source CL, Fly Speed, reach, and selected damage types. It ends if you become Unconscious unless another rule preserves it.
- Hover prevents falling when your Fly Speed becomes 0, but a feature that removes flight or suppresses the transformation uses normal falling and Failed Spatial Movement rules.
- The critical range of 19–20 applies only to attack rolls made by you with unarmed strikes or integrated Blade attacks unless another rule expressly broadens it. It does not stack with another expanded critical range; use the broadest range.
- The 3d8 additional damage applies once per turn to one eligible hit. Choose Force or Slashing when dealt.
- Moving through a hostile creature's space treats each such space as Difficult Terrain. You cannot end movement there and gain no protection from that creature's reactions beyond the printed Disadvantage.
- Each hostile creature can trigger the reach save once per turn: the first time it enters your reach during that turn, or when it starts its turn there if it has not already triggered during that turn. Expanding your reach around a stationary creature does not count as entering.
- The reach effect is not an attack and cannot trigger hit riders. On a failed save choose Reaction denial or the 10-foot Speed reduction. On success apply half damage and the 5-foot reduction. Reapplication refreshes, not stacks, a Speed reduction from this feature.

---

Cultivation Level 18 - Hollow Immortal

You gain the following passive benefits:

- Move through creature spaces as Difficult Terrain.
- Pass through openings as narrow as 1 inch.
- Gain Advantage against Grappled, Restrained, possession, forced transformation, and unwilling teleportation.

Empty-World Incarnation

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 7 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- Gain a Fly Speed of 40 feet and Hover.
- Gain Resistance to all damage except Force, Radiant, and Void.
- Move through ordinary walls, floors, ceilings, barriers, and creatures as Difficult Terrain.
- You cannot be Grappled or Restrained by a physical effect whose Source CL is no higher than yours.
- Use Hollow Step once per turn without paying its Stamina cost.
- After emerging from an object, barrier, or creature's space, gain Advantage on your next attack roll before the end of the turn.
- Empty Strike deals 3d8 additional damage instead of 2d8.

You cannot end a turn inside an occupied space or object.

An artifact barrier, spatial lock, or higher-CL phasing barrier prevents passage unless you win an opposed Cultivation Check.

---

Normalized Procedure — Hollow Immortal

- Passing through a 1-inch opening changes only the minimum opening needed by your body and normally carried equipment. It does not allow you to carry an oversized object, unwilling creature, vehicle, or structure through that opening.
- The listed Advantage applies only to the checks and saves directly resisting or escaping the named effects. It does not create immunity.

Normalized Procedure — Empty-World Incarnation

- Empty-World Incarnation is a temporary bodily state, not a separate projection. It preserves one body, one turn, one Hit Point total, and one set of conditions.
- Hollow Step retains its Bonus Action, duration, targeting, and once-per-turn practical action limit; only its Stamina cost is waived. Activating Empty-World Incarnation does not automatically activate Hollow Step on the same Bonus Action.
- Physical Grapple or Restraint from a Source CL no higher than yours cannot be newly established and becomes ineffective while the state persists. A higher-Source-CL physical effect remains subject to its normal checks and saves.
- Emerging means leaving an object, barrier, or creature space after occupying at least part of it through this feature. Advantage applies to one next attack before the end of the same turn and does not stack from passing through multiple spaces.
- Empty Strike uses 3d8 instead of 2d8; this is a replacement, not 2d8 + 3d8.
- When attempting to enter or cross an artifact barrier, spatial lock, or higher-Source-CL phasing barrier, make one opposed Cultivation Check for that discrete barrier and movement attempt. On failure, movement ends in the nearest legal space before the barrier. On success, pass through for that movement only unless the barrier's rule says otherwise.
- Ending the turn in an illegal space uses the Phase Flesh displacement and unavoidable-damage procedure.

---

Cultivation Level 18 - Ryūjin Ascendant Form

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 7 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- Gain a Fly Speed of 60 feet and Hover.
- Gain Immunity to Lightning damage.
- Gain Resistance to Thunder damage.
- You may become Large.
- Your unarmed reach increases by 5 feet.
- Dragon's Breath becomes a 30-foot cone and deals 8d6.
- Use Storm Step once per turn for 1 Stamina instead of 3.
- Once per turn when you hit with an unarmed strike, deal an additional 3d6 Lightning or Thunder damage.

A hostile creature that starts its turn within 10 feet makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, push it 5 feet and prevent it from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn.

---

Normalized Procedure — Ryūjin Ascendant Form

- This is a temporary bodily transformation. Record the chosen size, occupied space, equipment fit, flight, reach, Resistances, and active breath profile when it begins.
- “You may become Large” is optional. If chosen, you become Large only if your current space can legally contain that size. If already Large or larger, the feature does not reduce your size. Ending the form returns you to your prior legal size under the transformation procedure.
- The 5-foot unarmed reach increase is persistent for the duration and applies to unarmed attacks and Body features using unarmed reach. It does not enlarge the range of Dragon's Breath, Dragon's Roar, or Storm Step.
- Dragon's Breath retains its Action and 2-Stamina cost. Its cone becomes 30 feet and its damage is 8d6; this is a replacement profile, not additional damage.
- Storm Step retains its Bonus Action and all destination restrictions. It costs 1 Stamina during the form and remains usable no more than once during each of your turns.
- The 3d6 rider is once per turn total and replaces no other Dragon Scales damage; both apply to a qualifying hit because the source prints both benefits.
- At the start of each hostile creature's turn, check whether it is within 10 feet. It saves once for that turn. On failure, push it 5 feet directly away along a legal route and deny Reactions. If no legal space exists, it remains in place but still loses Reactions.
- Suppressing the form makes its benefits dormant and does not extend its duration or refund its scene use.

---

tianxia.subpath.body.seven_coiled_serpen.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - Seventh Coil: Heaven-Swallowing Serpent

While open:

- Speed doubles.
- Fly Speed equal to walking Speed and Hover.
- Resistance to all damage except Psychic and Void.
- Unarmed strikes deal an additional 2d8 Force.
- Grapple creatures up to two sizes larger.
- A Grappled creature cannot teleport unless it succeeds on a Cultivation Check against your DC; failure uses Failed Spatial Movement.

Once per turn when you hit a Grappled creature, spend 2 Stamina for Heaven-Swallowing Constriction. It makes a Constitution save.

- Failed Save: 6d8 Bludgeoning or Force, no Reactions, Speed 0, and Disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saves until your next turn.
- Successful Save: Half damage and Speed halved until your next turn.

At the end of each turn with the Seventh Coil open, take 2d8 Force damage that cannot be reduced, prevented, redirected, absorbed, or used to generate resources.

Normalized Procedure — Heaven-Swallowing Serpent

- Double walking Speed after fixed additions. A movement mode explicitly equal to walking Speed uses the doubled value; fixed Speeds and teleport ranges do not.
- Gain Fly Speed equal to current walking Speed and Hover. If the Coil closes or is suppressed while unsupported, resolve falling immediately unless another support remains.
- Resistance to all damage except Psychic and Void follows ordinary ordering. The 2d8 Force added to every unarmed-strike hit is part of that hit's packet and does not have a once-per-turn limit.
- Functional size increases by two categories only for Grappling. It combines with Crushing Serpent by using the highest applicable value rather than increasing by three categories.
- A creature Grappled by you that attempts any teleportation or spatial movement must first make one Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC. On failure use Failed Spatial Movement; on success the spatial movement resolves and ordinarily ends the physical Grapple unless its rule says otherwise.
- Once per turn after hitting a creature currently Grappled by you, spend 2 Stamina to use Heaven-Swallowing Constriction. It makes one Constitution save. On failure it takes 6d8 Bludgeoning or Force, cannot take Reactions, has Speed 0, and has Disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saves until the start of your next turn. On success it takes half damage and its Speed is halved until the start of your next turn.
- Constriction damage is a separate packet created by the same activation and does not automatically create an Injury or destroy organs.
- At the end of each turn while the Seventh Coil remains open, before Coil upkeep, take 2d8 Force damage applied directly to Hit Points. It cannot be reduced, prevented, redirected, absorbed by Temporary Hit Points, delayed, shared, or converted into healing, Stamina, Charges, Beats, Momentum, or another resource.
- If that damage makes you Unconscious, all Coils close before upkeep and no Stamina is paid. Otherwise pay the printed 2-Stamina seven-Coil upkeep after the damage.

---

tianxia.subpath.body.sky_treading_tendon.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - Body Crosses Heaven

Gain a permanent Fly Speed equal to your walking Speed and Hover while conscious.

Once during each of your turns, after moving at least 30 feet before hitting with an unarmed strike, spend 2 Stamina. The attack deals an additional 4d8 Force damage, and the target makes a Strength saving throw.

- Failed Save: Push it up to 30 feet in a direction you choose and knock it Prone.
- Successful Save: Push it 10 feet.

If it collides with a solid surface, it and the surface each take additional Bludgeoning damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

---

Normalized Procedure — Body Crosses Heaven

- The permanent Fly Speed and Hover function while conscious and derive from your current walking Speed. Losing consciousness removes Hover and causes falling unless another effect supports you.
- For the once-per-turn attack, count 30 feet of actual movement before the hit during that turn. Teleportation does not add traveled distance. The 2-Stamina cost is declared after the hit and before rolling the 4d8 Force damage.
- The 4d8 is part of the triggering attack's damage packet. Then the target makes the Strength save.
- On failure, choose a legal direction and move the target up to 30 feet along a direct trajectory; on success, push it 10 feet directly away from you. Movement stops at the first surviving solid barrier.
- A collision occurs once when the forced movement is stopped early by a solid surface. The target and that discrete surface each take one Bludgeoning damage packet equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Another creature is not a “solid surface” for this clause unless its own rule expressly functions as one.
- The collision damage does not trigger this feature again, create an Injury, or grant additional forced movement.

---

tianxia.subpath.body.sky_treading_tendon.player_text:
Cultivation Level 6 - Heaven-Kicking Leg

You can use this when  You hit with an unarmed strike after moving at least 10 feet during the current turn.  
Cost: 1 Stamina  
Limit: Once per turn  
Saving Throw: Strength

On a failed save, move the target up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, horizontally, vertically, or both, and it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If unsupported afterward, it falls.

On a successful save, push it 5 feet horizontally.

A creature more than two sizes larger than you has Advantage on this saving throw.

Normalized Procedure — Heaven-Kicking Leg

- Count at least 10 feet of actual movement during the current turn before the hit. Forced movement can qualify only if you willingly accepted or directed it; teleportation does not count as traveled distance.
- Declare after the unarmed strike hits and spend Stamina before the Strength save.
- On failure, choose an unoccupied legal destination within 15 feet of the target's starting space and visible to you. The target travels along the shortest unobstructed physical trajectory, which may be horizontal, vertical, or diagonal. This is forced movement, not teleportation.
- If the full destination is blocked, move the target as far as legally possible along the selected trajectory. If unsupported, falling begins after the forced movement resolves.
- On success, push 5 feet horizontally and directly away from you. If no legal space exists, the target remains in place.
- “More than two sizes larger” means at least three size categories larger than you and grants Advantage only on this save.

player_evidence.Kicking it upward, and its fall if it en: Resolve the upward kick by hand; if the target ends unsupported, resolve its fall as well.

tianxia.subpath.body.sky_treading_tendon.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Tread the Empty Sky

Once during each of your turns while airborne, spend 1 Stamina without using an action.

Until the end of the current turn:

- Gain a Fly Speed equal to your walking Speed.
- Hover.
- Your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from creatures at least 10 feet below you.

At the end of the turn, you remain suspended until the start of your next turn. If you do not use Tread the Empty Sky again before that turn ends and remain unsupported, you fall.

Effects explicitly preventing flight, sealing the surrounding air, suppressing Body Refining features, or imposing a spatial lock prevent this movement.

Normalized Procedure — Tread the Empty Sky

- Activate once during your turn while any part of your space is unsupported or airborne. Spending Stamina requires no action.
- Until the end of that turn, gain the printed Fly Speed and Hover. The flight uses movement normally and does not create extra movement beyond your remaining movement allowance.
- Creatures at least 10 feet below every part of your space cannot make Opportunity Attacks caused by this movement. Other creatures can.
- At the end of the activation turn, remain suspended in your current legal space until the start of your next turn. During that next turn, you may reactivate the feature once. If you do not reactivate before that turn ends and remain unsupported, you fall at the end of that turn.
- Suppression or an explicit flight prohibition immediately removes flight and suspension. A spatial lock blocks only the movement authority it expressly covers; it does not automatically damage you.

player_evidence.Flight, Hover and suspension are the GM': Apply flight, Hover and suspension by hand. Tread the Empty Sky does not require an action.

tianxia.subpath.body.stone_fist.feature..player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Shattering Palm

You can use this when  You hit a creature, Construct, object, barrier, vehicle, or Formation Anchor with an unarmed strike.  
Cost: 3 Stamina  
Limit: Once per turn

Choose one form.

Break the Guard

A creature or Construct makes a Constitution saving throw.

- Failed Save: Its AC is reduced by 2 for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the reduction on a success.
- Successful Save: Its AC is reduced by 1 until the start of your next turn.

A target cannot suffer more than one AC reduction from Shattering Palm. Reapplication replaces and refreshes the existing reduction.

Fracture the Structure

The attack deals an additional 5d8 Bludgeoning or Force damage, increasing to 7d8 at Cultivation Level 17.

Against a target whose Source CL is no higher than yours, this damage ignores Resistance to Bludgeoning and Force and treats its Damage Threshold as 0. It does not ignore Immunity.

Normalized Procedure — Shattering Palm

- Choose Break the Guard or Fracture the Structure when the feature is declared. A target that is both a creature and Construct can be affected by either form, but not both from the same activation.
- Break the Guard modifies the target's current Armor Class regardless of whether it comes from armor, natural armor, Unarmored Defense, a transformation, or an Asset profile. The repeated save occurs at the end of the affected target's turns; success ends only this reduction.
- Reapplication never stacks. If the target already has the failed-save reduction, a successful-save application does not reduce its magnitude or extend it unless the new duration would last longer.
- Fracture the Structure is legal only against an object, barrier, vehicle, Formation Anchor, terrain section, or Construct. A living creature that is not a Construct is not a “structure” merely because it has armor, stone skin, or a large body.
- Treating Damage Threshold as 0 applies only to the additional 5d8 or 7d8, not automatically to the triggering attack's base damage.

player_evidence.Fracture the Structure (+ 5d8, 7d8 at CL: Fracture the Structure: once per turn, when your unarmed strike hits an object, barrier, vehicle, Formation Anchor, terrain section or Construct, you may spend 3 Stamina for an additional 5d8 Bludgeoning or Force damage, increasing to 7d8 at CL17. Against a target whose Source Cultivation Level is no higher than yours, this additional damage ignores Resistance to Bludgeoning and Force and treats Damage Threshold as 0; it does not ignore Immunity. The Damage Threshold benefit applies only to the additional damage, not the base attack. Apply Fracture the Structure by hand.

tianxia.subpath.body.ten_thousand_parasi.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - Ten-Thousand Worm Demon Body

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 7 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- Resistance to all damage except Fire, Radiant, Psychic, and Void.
- Move through creature spaces as Difficult Terrain.
- Pass through openings as narrow as 1 inch.
- Cannot be Grappled or Restrained by ordinary physical effects.
- Gain 1 Brood at the start of each turn.
- Maximum Brood +3.
- Internal Brood can heal you at 0 Hit Points.

If Internal Brood heals you at 0 Hit Points, regain the rolled amount, stand without movement, lose all remaining Brood, and end this transformation. This can happen once per activation.

Brood Tide

Action  
Area: 30-foot cone  
Cost: 3 Brood  
Saving Throw: Constitution

- Failed Save: 8d8 Poison or Necrotic, Infested, and Speed reduced by 15 feet until the end of its next turn.
- Successful Save: Half damage, not Infested, and Speed reduced by 5 feet until the start of its next turn.

A creature already Infested when it fails immediately triggers Gnawing Infestation after Brood Tide, then gains a new Infestation.

Normalized Procedure — Ten-Thousand Worm Demon Body

- This is a whole-body swarm transformation. Equipment is carried and merged or suspended under the transformation procedure; it does not fall into individual worms or create duplicates.
- Resistance excludes Fire, Radiant, Psychic, and Void. You can move through creature spaces as Difficult Terrain and through openings at least 1 inch wide, but must end in a legal space large enough for your current body unless another rule permits compression at the end.
- Ordinary physical Grapples and restraints cannot affect you. Supernatural, spatial, spiritual, conceptual, higher-Source-CL, or expressly swarm-binding effects use their normal procedures.
- Increase maximum Brood by 3 and gain 1 at the start of each turn as a direct gain.
- Internal Brood can function at 0 Hit Points once during each activation. When used, spend 1 Brood, regain the rolled amount, stand without movement if possible, lose every remaining Brood, and end the transformation. This replaces remaining at 0 but is not usable against instant death, total destruction, Erasure, or recovery prevention.
- Brood Tide: The 30-foot cone originates from you and requires line of effect. Choose Poison or Necrotic for the use. On failure deal 8d8, Infest, and reduce Speed by 15 feet until the end of the target's next turn. On success deal half, do not Infest, and reduce Speed by 5 feet until the start of its next turn.
- If a failed target was already Infested by you, resolve its existing Gnawing Infestation immediately after Brood Tide damage, end that old record, then create the new Infestation. This immediate trigger counts as Gnawing damage for Parasite Sovereignty and does not require one of the ordinary trigger events.
- A target can be affected once per use. The cone does not leave a persistent swarm, contaminate terrain, or create independent parasite creatures.

---

tianxia.subpath.body.thousand_fold_steel.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - Body Beyond the Hammer

All three Forms are active simultaneously.

- You cannot be Disarmed by an ordinary effect.
- Unarmed strikes and integrated melee weapons count as adamantine.
- Immune to ordinary effects permanently breaking, rusting, warping, corroding, or dulling your body or integrated weapons.
- When an effect would destroy or permanently deform a limb, take 4d10 Force damage instead and the limb remains functional. This damage cannot be reduced by this Subpath.

Once per turn on a melee hit, choose one:

- Perfect Edge: Additional 4d8 Slashing or Force and reduce AC by 1 until your next turn.
- Perfect Spine: Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 x Proficiency Bonus + Constitution modifier; cannot be pushed, pulled, or knocked Prone until your next turn.
- Perfect Reed: Move 20 feet without provoking and through hostile spaces as Difficult Terrain.

Each option can be selected only once per turn.

Normalized Procedure — Body Beyond the Hammer

- All three Forms are active simultaneously and no start-of-turn Form choice is required.
- Ordinary Disarm immunity and immunity to ordinary permanent breaking, rusting, warping, corrosion, or dulling protect your body and current Tempered Weapon. They do not restore an item already destroyed, protect another creature's weapon, or override artifact, divine, Secret, Foundation, Method, Immortal, or explicit equal- or higher-Source-CL authority.
- Unarmed strikes and the Tempered Weapon count as adamantine for rules that recognize that material. This does not change their damage type or grant an item property not printed here.
- When a Source Rule would destroy or permanently deform one physical limb, natural-weapon structure, or equivalent reconstructable appendage, replace only that anatomical result with 4d10 Force damage and keep the structure functional. This replacement does not apply to conceptual erasure, complete bodily destruction, Foundation destruction, or an effect that does not target anatomy.
- The replacement damage cannot be reduced by Thousand-Fold Steel Body, including Spine Form, Spine Quench, or Perfect Spine. Other independent legal defenses can interact unless the original Source Rule says otherwise. Other nonanatomical consequences of the triggering effect still resolve.
- Once per turn after one melee hit, choose one Perfect result. This use is separate from Folded Edge, Hidden Spine and can coexist on the same hit.
- Perfect Edge: Add 4d8 Slashing or Force and reduce AC by 1 until the start of your next turn. It refreshes, not stacks with, this Subpath's other AC reduction.
- Perfect Spine: Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus + Constitution modifier and become immune to physical push, pull, and Prone until the start of your next turn. It does not block teleportation or voluntary movement.
- Perfect Reed: Move up to 20 feet without provoking. You can pass through hostile spaces as Difficult Terrain but cannot end in an occupied space or pass through a solid obstruction.
- Each Perfect option can be selected at most once during the same turn even if another rule would permit another Perfect choice.

---

When an effect would destroy or permanently deform a limb, resolve the replacement by hand: take 4d10 Force damage and keep the limb functional. Thousand-Fold Steel Body cannot reduce this replacement damage. Higher-authority effects and destruction that is not anatomical follow their own rules.
player_evidence.The Tempered Weapon counting as adamanti: Your unarmed strikes and current Tempered Weapon count as adamantine against objects. Unarmed strikes ignore object Damage Thresholds. Apply the Tempered Weapon's adamantine benefit by hand when attacking an object.

tianxia.subpath.body.thousand_fold_steel.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Folded Edge, Hidden Spine

Your Body Refining melee attacks ignore ordinary Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing.

Once per turn when you hit while Edge Form is active, choose one:

- Reduce target AC by 1 until the start of your next turn.
- Prevent Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Deal an additional 2d8 Slashing or Force damage.
- Deal double damage to an unattended object, temporary barrier, vehicle, structure, or Formation Anchor.

The AC reduction does not stack with itself.

Normalized Procedure — Folded Edge, Hidden Spine

- Body Refining melee attacks ignore ordinary Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing. “Ordinary” excludes Immunity, artifact defenses, divine authority, Secret protections, Immortal defenses, and an explicit equal- or higher-Source-CL rule that cannot be bypassed.
- Once per turn after hitting while Edge Form is active, choose exactly one printed result. This is separate from Edge Form's Proficiency Bonus damage and can be applied to the same hit.
- AC reduction begins after the hit resolves and lasts until the start of your next turn. Reapplication refreshes duration and does not stack with itself.
- Reaction denial lasts until the start of the target's next turn and does not cancel a Reaction already spent.
- The 2d8 Slashing or Force is part of the triggering hit's packet and cannot critically multiply separately.
- Against an eligible unattended object, temporary barrier, vehicle, structure, or Formation Anchor, calculate the triggering hit's final damage under ordinary modifiers and then double that hit's damage once. The doubling does not apply to later damage packets or world-scale terrain that is not a legal target.
- A target cannot receive several choices from one use even if several effects would be legal.

player_evidence.Double damage to an unattended object, b: When you choose the object-damage benefit of Folded Edge, Hidden Spine, double the triggering hit's final damage to an eligible unattended object, temporary barrier, vehicle, structure or Formation Anchor by hand. This is one choice for that use, not an extra benefit added to another choice.

tianxia.subpath.body.vermilion_gate_guar.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Threshold Between Worlds

Your thresholds become 10 feet high.

When a hostile creature attempts to teleport, phase, or use spatial movement across one, it makes a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC.

- Success: The movement resolves.
- Failure: Use the Failed Spatial Movement rule.

Ranged attacks crossing a threshold grant Half Cover to a target within 5 feet of it. This does not stack with other Half Cover.

Normalized Procedure — Threshold Between Worlds

- A hostile spatial movement attempts to cross when its origin and intended destination are on opposite sides of a threshold and the shortest conceptual route would pass through its vertical plane.
- Resolve one Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC before placing the creature at the destination. On success, the movement resolves. On failure, use Failed Spatial Movement; the creature remains at the nearest legal status-quo position on the origin side unless the governing effect specifies another failure result.
- One spatial movement crossing two of your thresholds makes one check, not two. Separate activations make separate checks.
- For ranged attacks, trace the attack line from origin to target. If it crosses a threshold and the target is within 5 feet of that threshold, the target has Half Cover. Multiple thresholds and other Half Cover do not stack; use the greatest applicable cover.
- The thresholds remain intangible and do not block an effect that neither uses an attack roll nor is expressly affected by cover, unless another feature says otherwise.

tianxia.subpath.body.white_elephant_sove.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - World-Bearing Elephant King

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 7 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

Become Huge if space permits, otherwise Large with all other benefits.

For the duration:

- Resistance to all damage except Psychic and Void.
- Speed +20 feet.
- Unarmed strikes deal 2d8 before modifiers.
- Once per turn on a hit, additional 4d8 Bludgeoning or Force.
- Hostile creatures treat spaces within 10 feet as Difficult Terrain.
- Allies within 10 feet gain Half Cover against ranged attacks.
- A creature of your CL or lower cannot push, pull, knock you Prone, or move you against your will unless its feature explicitly ignores bodily anchoring.

Sovereign Trampling Advance

Once per turn after moving 20 feet in a straight line, move through hostile spaces. Each creature entered makes a Dexterity save.

- Failed Save: 4d8 Bludgeoning, Prone, moved to nearest legal space outside your path.
- Successful Save: Half damage, moved to nearest legal space, remains standing.

A creature is affected once per turn.

Normalized Procedure — World-Bearing Elephant King

- On activation, become Huge if a legal Huge space exists. Otherwise become Large and retain every other benefit. Use the transformation and equipment procedures; the form does not destroy terrain merely because space is tight.
- The duration, 7-Stamina cost, and once-per-scene limit are unchanged. If suppressed below Cultivation Level 18, the transformation becomes dormant and your size returns to the largest legal unsuppressed state.
- Resistance excludes Psychic and Void. The 2d8 unarmed die replaces the normal base die; the once-per-turn 4d8 rider is separate and applies on one hit.
- Hostile Difficult Terrain applies to every hostile space within 10 feet and does not stack with itself. Ally Half Cover is checked for each ranged attack when the line crosses or is substantially obstructed by your occupied space.
- The movement immunity compares the hostile effect's Source CL to your current effective Body Refining CL. A lower- or equal-CL creature cannot perform the listed movement unless its feature expressly ignores bodily anchoring. Higher-CL effects use their normal procedure.
- Sovereign Trampling Advance: Track 20 feet of straight-line voluntary movement during your turn. Once per turn thereafter, you may move through hostile spaces along that continuing route. Each creature whose space you enter saves once.
- Resolve entered creatures nearest to farthest. On failure deal 4d8, knock Prone, and place it in the nearest legal space outside your path; on success deal half and place it likewise standing. If no legal placement exists, your movement stops before entering that creature's space. This movement does not silently damage terrain or allow passage through solid barriers.

---

Cultivation Level 3 - Stone Skin

While benefiting from Unarmored Defense:

- Gain +1 AC.
- Gain Resistance to Cold damage.
- You can hold your breath for 1 hour.
- Gain Advantage on Constitution saving throws caused by extreme cold, high altitude, forced marches, harsh weather, environmental pressure, and mundane exposure.

Normalized Procedure — Stone Skin
- The +1 AC applies only while your chosen AC calculation is Unarmored Defense. It is an AC bonus and does not combine multiple instances of Stone Skin.
- Cold Resistance applies to Cold damage from any source unless that source expressly bypasses Resistance. Environmental cold Immunity gained later at Cultivation Level 14 supersedes but does not stack with it.
- The one-hour breath duration is a fixed replacement for ordinary breath-holding. Other features can replace it only if they provide a longer duration or expressly stack.
- The environmental-save Advantage applies to Constitution saves directly caused by the listed mundane or supernatural environmental pressures. It does not apply to an attack or technique merely flavored as weather unless the effect is adjudicated as environmental exposure.

tianxia.subpath.body.yamabushi.feature.w.player_text:
Cultivation Level 6 - Waterfall Stance

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 2 Stamina

For the duration:

- Ignore nonmagical Difficult Terrain.
- Gain Advantage on saving throws against forced movement, Prone, Frightened, and Exhaustion caused by physical exertion.
- Reduce falling damage by 5 x your CL.
- Rain, waterfalls, and heavy wind do not interfere with your vision, hearing, or movement.

The stance ends if you become Unconscious.

Normalized Procedure — Waterfall Stance
- Record activation time and Source CL. The stance ends immediately if you become Unconscious; losing contact with water or a mountain does not end it.
- “Nonmagical Difficult Terrain” includes ordinary rubble, mud, snow, undergrowth, stairs, and damaged ground. It does not ignore a cultivation Field, Formation, supernatural terrain, or a creature's occupied space unless that source is expressly nonmagical.

Cultivation Level 18 — Procession of Ten Thousand Demons

You transform the Banner’s court into a moving calamity procession.

Action  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Area: 40-foot-radius, 60-foot-high cylinder centered on the Banner  
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- The Banner’s Fly Speed becomes 40 feet and it may move through allied spaces.
- Gain 1 Dread at the start of each of your turns.
- Use Banner Bite once during each turn without spending Dread.
- Edict of the Calamity Court costs 1 Dread.
- Chosen allies in the field gain +2 AC against ranged attacks and Advantage against Frightened.
- The area is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures.
- Hostile teleportation into or out of the field requires a Charisma save against your Cultivation Save DC when the teleport’s Source CL is no higher than yours.

A hostile creature that enters for the first time during a turn or starts its turn there makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save:

- Take 6d8 Psychic or Necrotic damage.
- Become Demon-Marked until the end of your next turn.
- Become Frightened until the start of its next turn.
- Cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Successful Save:

- Take half damage.
- Become Demon-Marked until the end of your next turn.

Court Collection

Once per round when a Demon-Marked qualifying hostile creature in the field reaches 0 Hit Points:

- Choose one ally in the field.
- It regains 2d8 + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier Hit Points.
- It may move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

The same defeated creature cannot trigger Court Collection more than once, even if revived.

Procession Assets

The spectral demons, guards, beasts, musicians, scribes, and executioners in the procession are manifestations of the field, not independent creatures.

They:

- Cannot be separately targeted.
- Cannot carry items.
- Cannot flank.
- Cannot trigger resource generation independently.
- Disappear when the field ends.

Break the Procession

The Procession ends if:

- You lose Concentration.
- The Banner reaches 0 Hit Points.
- An equal- or higher-Source-CL anti-daemonic effect suppresses the Banner for a full round.
- A higher-authority exorcism succeeds on its printed contest.

When the Procession ends because the Banner was destroyed or exorcised:

- Lose all Dread.
- Gain 1 Corruption.
- Take 4d10 Psychic damage.

End of Court

At normal duration end, if you spent at least 5 Dread during the Procession, choose one:

- Gain 1 Corruption.
- The Banner becomes Hungry until purified.

This choice is made before resolving the ordinary scene-end Corruption trigger.

Reaction

- Add 1d8 associated damage.
- Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus.
- Move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Real Danger Doctrine

A willing or self-created calamity can be consumed when:

- The normal cost is paid.
- Damage and consequences are real.
- The event can defeat, injure, scar, or meaningfully set you back.
- The resulting Calamity cannot fully refund the event through a closed loop.

You can force the second furnace to pay part of an ordinary Qi cost.

- Immortal Arts.
- Permanent or indefinite transformations.
- Strategic travel or world-scale effects.
- Effects requiring expensive materials.

- Lifespan costs.
- Maximum-resource reductions.
- Corruption costs.
- Material components.
- Another creature’s expenditure.
- Costs already reduced by another feature that says they cannot be further reduced.

- Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to Proficiency Bonus.

- The original feature remains activated if you can pay its unreduced cost immediately.
- If you cannot pay, the activation fails.
- Any Qi already paid remains spent.
- You do not gain Devil Qi or Corruption from the failed Overdraw.

CL18 — Transcendent Synthesis

When you gain this feature, add one additional non-Secret Sphere to your Curriculum and record two eligible Tier 1 or Tier 2 techniques from it.

Also record one Master Expression from any Curriculum Sphere. The Master Expression must satisfy all of the following:

- You possess genuine access to a teacher, manual, inheritance, observed demonstration, or other Source Rule sufficient to study it.
- It is a Tier 3 technique or equivalent high-Realm expression.
- Its base Cultivation Point cost is 7 or less.
- You meet its non-Sphere prerequisites, including weapon, implement, Realm, and material requirements.
- It is not Secret, Legendary, permanent, resurrection, strategic-scale, an Immortal Art, or a feature that permanently grants another Sphere, Path, Subpath, Method, Foundation, or creature.

The Master Expression is recorded but not permanently learned and cannot satisfy prerequisites.

Transcendent State

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- Art Rotation may trigger once during every turn, no more than once per turn.
- When Art Rotation triggers, choose two different Rotation Benefits.
- Split-Meridian Focus upkeep becomes 0 Qi.
- A failed Concentration save ends only one of your two effects, chosen after seeing the roll.
- Nine Arts Convergence may be used once without expending its once-per-scene use and without paying its 2-Qi surcharge.

Living Curriculum

At the start of each of your turns, choose one recorded Curriculum Technique from any Curriculum Sphere.

Until the start of your next turn, you temporarily know that technique. It may be a base ability, basic expression, Tier 1 talent, or Tier 2 talent. You must meet its prerequisites. Its base Qi cost cannot exceed 5.

Master Expression

Once during Transcendent State, activate your recorded Master Expression.

- Pay its full cost and all materials.
- Use your Qi Cultivation key ability unless its Source Rule expressly requires another ability.
- You count as knowing the required Curriculum Sphere only for this activation.
- It cannot be copied by Nine Arts Convergence, Barrage, a duplicate activation, or another temporary-learning effect.
- After it resolves, you no longer know it until a later Transcendent State.

This is a genuine Tier 3 expression, not a low-tier rotation benefit.

Principle Fusion

Once per turn when you activate a qualifying Sphere technique, choose a second known or temporarily known technique from a different Sphere with a base cost of 4 or less. Spend its full base cost plus 1 Qi and apply one of the following Fusion Riders instead of resolving it as a separate activation:

- Element Rider: Add 2d8 damage of one type dealt by the second technique to one target damaged by the first.
- Movement Rider: Apply one push, pull, teleport, or voluntary movement packet of up to 15 feet that the second technique could legally produce.
- Guard Rider: Grant one legal target Temporary Hit Points equal to 3 × Proficiency Bonus or a +2 AC bonus until the start of your next turn.
- Condition Rider: Apply only the second technique’s printed successful-save or lesser condition result to one legal target that failed against the first.
- Origin Rider: Use one legal origin, implement, Domain Armament, or Formation node authorized by the second technique for the first.

A Fusion Rider cannot add an attack, create another complete activation, extend a permanent duration, multiply across a Barrage, refund more Qi than was spent, or reproduce an item’s limited-use property.

Transcendent Free Expression

Once per turn, activate one qualifying Sphere technique you know or temporarily know without spending its base Qi cost when that base cost is 4 Qi or less.

You still pay optional surcharges, material costs, weapon or item costs, hostile imposed costs, and any cost not defined as the technique’s base activation cost.

Transcendent Free Expression cannot pay for a permanent, Secret, Legendary, strategic-scale, resurrection, Master Expression, or additional-complete-activation effect.

Cultivation Level 14 — Hundred-Step Saber Procession

Action  
Cost: 6 Qi  
Movement: Up to twice your Speed  
Limit: Once per turn

Move along a legal path up to twice your Speed.

During this movement:

- You do not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- You may move through hostile creature spaces as Difficult Terrain.
- You may cross liquids, unstable surfaces, and open-air gaps no longer than 20 feet.
- You cannot pass through solid barriers, Total Cover, sealed Formations, or spaces too small for you.
- You must end in a legal unoccupied space.

Choose up to your Proficiency Bonus in different hostile creatures whose spaces you pass within your saber’s reach.

Make one saber-family weapon attack or Saber Domain Armament Attack against each chosen creature.

Resolve attacks separately.

Procession Damage

Each hit deals normal weapon or Domain Armament damage.

The first hit during the Procession deals an additional 3d8 Slashing or Force damage.

Each later hit deals an additional 2d8 damage.

Once-per-turn features apply only once across the Procession unless expressly stated otherwise.

Procession Technique Delivery

You may deliver one authorized weapon-delivered cultivation technique through the first qualifying hit.

For each additional hit through which you want to deliver the same technique:

- Spend 1 additional Qi.
- The target must be a legal target.
- Resolve its attack or save normally.
- Do not repay the technique’s base cost.
- Pay any target-specific material or permanent cost.
- A once-per-activation rider still applies once.
- A once-per-target rider may apply to each target.
- The technique cannot generate another Procession, attack sequence, or recursive copy.

This feature expressly permits one cultivation technique to be delivered through multiple attacks when its additional costs are paid.

Momentum of the Procession

After the Procession resolves:

- Gain 1 Gale Momentum for each different hostile creature hit.
- You cannot exceed your maximum.
- Choose one creature hit and push it 10 feet or knock it Prone if it is no more than one size larger than you.
