Cultivation Level 3 — Saber Conduction

You may use a saber-family weapon to deliver a targeted Qi technique.

When you activate a Qi-powered technique, you may deliver it through a saber-family weapon you are wielding when all of the following are true:

- You are proficient with the weapon.
- The technique targets one creature or one object.
- The technique has a range of Touch, 5 feet, or 15 feet or less.
- The technique has an instantaneous effect or a duration applied directly to the struck target.
- The technique does not create an area, summon a creature, establish a field, create a separate asset, or require a location rather than a target.

Additional Cost: 1 Qi

Make one attack with the saber-family weapon as part of the technique's activation.

Miss:

- The technique is not delivered.
- Its complete cost remains spent.
- No saving throw from the technique occurs.

Hit:

1. Deal the weapon's normal damage.
2. Apply the delivered technique to the struck target.
3. Resolve any saving throw required by the technique.
4. Apply all once-per-activation limits.

A thrown saber qualifies only when it has a printed thrown property or another Source Rule permits it.

The weapon may be wielded normally or float as your bound Saber Domain Armament after Cultivation Level 9.

Saber Conduction applies only to the first qualifying attack unless a later feature or another Source Rule expressly expands it.

Wind-Following Cut

Once per turn, after you gain Gale Momentum, choose one:

- Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Move your Saber Domain Armament 10 feet.
- Push the creature you hit 5 feet.
- Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
- Draw, stow, call, or release one saber-family weapon.

Spend Momentum

When you hit with a saber-family weapon or Saber Domain Armament, spend 1 Gale Momentum to choose one:

Driving Cut

Push the target 10 feet if it is no more than one size larger than you.

Hooking Cut

Pull the target 5 feet or move yourself 5 feet toward it without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Guard-Breaking Cut

The target cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Wind-Sheathed Cut

Deal additional Force or Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

A hit can receive one Spend Momentum option unless another feature says otherwise.

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 10 Qi

Your body and Soul Treasure become one distributed immortal structure.

For the duration:

- Gain Resistance to all damage except Force, Psychic, and Void.
- Your Soul Treasure cannot lose Integrity from an effect whose Source CL is lower than yours.
- Enter the Treasure and Manifest from the Treasure require no action.
- Treasure Recall costs 0 Qi and can cross ordinary planar boundaries when you know the item’s destination plane, but not sealed, artifact, Secret, or higher-authority boundaries.
- Maintain Treasure Aspect without its normal Qi cost.
- Create Soul Satellites without Concentration and move each 60 feet per turn.
- Use one Satellite as a Remote Technique Origin during each turn without surcharge.
- A floating shield Soul Treasure may protect two creatures in Guard Mode.
- A floating weapon Soul Treasure may make one additional Domain Armament Attack as part of the same Bonus Action; this additional attack does not add your ability modifier and cannot repeat once-per-turn riders.

Treasure Incarnation

Once during each of your turns, choose one state:

Wielded Incarnation

The Soul Treasure appears in your hand or worn position.

- Gain +2 AC until the start of your next turn if it is a shield or armor.
- Gain Advantage on the first attack made through it before the start of your next turn if it is a weapon or offensive implement.

Floating Incarnation

The Soul Treasure floats at one Satellite or legal point within 120 feet.

- Move it up to 60 feet.
- It can originate techniques and use its printed passive properties normally.

Inner Incarnation

Enter the Treasure.

- Gain Total Cover from effects that cannot affect the item or souls within it.
- The item remains targetable.

Reforge the Vessel

If your physical body is destroyed during Immortal Treasure Body but the Soul Treasure survives with at least 1 Integrity:

- You do not immediately die.
- You remain conscious inside the Soul Treasure at 1 Hit Point.
- Immortal Treasure Body ends.
- You cannot leave the item until you complete a reconstruction rite.

Reconstruction Rite

Time: 8 hours  
Cost: All current Qi, one permanent Hit Die, and appropriate cultivation materials

Create a replacement body adjacent to the Soul Treasure.

The replacement:

- Is recognizably yours.
- Retains your character statistics.
- May display permanent artifact traits.
- Restores you to half your Hit Point maximum.
- Does not restore spent resources or lost Integrity.

The permanent Hit Die loss can be restored only by a breakthrough, a Foundation or Method explicitly capable of restoring cultivation structure, or a higher-authority reconstruction effect.

Sever the Immortal Bond

A hostile creature may attempt to permanently sever the bond only when:

- The Soul Treasure is restrained, suppressed, or reduced to 0 Integrity.
- You are Incapacitated or inside it.
- The effect explicitly targets souls, bonds, names, or artifact ownership.

The severing source makes a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC.

On success:

- The Soul Treasure ceases to be your resurrection vessel.
- You take 10d10 Psychic and Force damage.
- You cannot bind another Soul Treasure until completing a long rest and a major repair rite.

On failure:

- The bond remains.
- The source cannot retry until it changes the circumstances, obtains new authority, or a new scene begins.

Cultivation Level 18 — Thousand-Year Lantern

You manifest a lantern containing the remembered flame-patterns of every soul you have lawfully tended.

Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Duration: The scene  
Requirement: A functioning Soul Candle

The Soul Candle becomes a Thousand-Year Lantern, a 30-foot-radius Spirit Awakening field centered on the candle. Its Asset Hit Points double for the duration.

While the Lantern persists:

- Allies of your choice in the field have Advantage on death saving throws and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.
- Allies in the field cannot be possessed or have their souls displaced by ordinary lower-Source-CL effects.
- When an ally in the field succeeds on one of those saving throws, choose one hostile creature in the field. It gains one Soul-Wick Mark or suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.
- You may use Spiritual Exorcism once during the activation without spending Resonance, provided the target is in the field.
- A creature restored by Last Flame within the field does not gain Borrowed Final Breath until the field ends.

Last Wick Extinguishes

Once during the activation, you may use the following Action:

Range: 60 feet from the Lantern  
Cost: 6 Resonance  
Requirement: A hostile creature bearing three Soul-Wick Marks that is Bloodied, has failed an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma save during the scene, has lost Concentration, or has had a supernatural defense suppressed

The target makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save: It takes 10d10 + Wisdom modifier Psychic, Fire, or Necrotic damage. Consume all its Soul-Wick Marks. Choose one sustaining expression you previously identified.

- An ordinary lower-Source-CL expression ends.
- A Restricted or equal-Source-CL expression is suppressed for the scene; the target repeats the save at the end of each turn, restoring it after two successes.
- A higher, Rare, Forbidden, Secret, divine, artifact, tribulation, Foundation, Method, or identity-defining expression is not erased automatically. One printed benefit is suppressed until the end of the target’s next turn, subject to a Cultivation Check.
- An ordinary creature whose Source CL is at least 5 lower than yours reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage can be killed outright if the campaign’s stakes permit it.

Successful Save: It takes half damage, loses one Soul-Wick Mark, and its identified sustaining expression flickers until the start of its next turn.

Last Wick Extinguishes is prepared execution authority, not universal soul erasure. Complete soul destruction, lineage extinction, permanent Method loss, and similar results require a dedicated higher-authority Source Rule or campaign-scale rite.

Cultivation Level 14 — No Fixed Compass

Your soul can continue a direction even when the body is constrained by ordinary geometry.

Direction Without Footing

Your Speed increases by 10 feet.

While completing a declared Bearing, you may move across liquid, narrow surfaces, unstable terrain, vertical surfaces, and open gaps as though they were stable ground. You fall at the end of the turn unless you reach a supporting space or another rule keeps you aloft. This is a spiritual step, not flight.

Nonmagical Difficult Terrain does not cost you extra movement while completing a Bearing.

Break the Restraining Direction

Once on each of your turns when a Grappled, Restrained, pinned, tethered, or similar effect prevents movement required by your declared Bearing, you may spend 2 Resonance and make a Cultivation Check against the effect's escape DC or Source Rule.

- Success: End one ordinary Grappled or Restrained effect on yourself, or suppress one equal-authority movement restriction until the end of the turn. You may then continue moving.
- Failure: The restriction remains. You do not spend movement that the restriction made illegal, but you cannot attempt this procedure against the same effect again during the turn.
- Higher authority: On success, suppress only the expression preventing the current movement unless the effect's own rules permit complete escape.

Bearing Without Name

Once per turn when you spend a Bearing token, you may treat it as either of the other two Bearings for one printed rider. The movement you already performed is not rewritten; only the rider changes.

Soul Splitting — Counter-Needle

While your Soul Fragment is within 60 feet of your Pole:

- you may originate Turn the Compass or Break the Four Directions from yourself or the fragment, chosen when activated;
- range, line of effect, and movement are measured from the chosen origin;
- you remain the only attacker and mover unless the feature expressly moves the fragment;
- after you spend a Bearing token, the fragment may move 10 feet without an action at the end of the activation.

Once per turn after that movement, if the fragment ends within 10 feet of your Resonance Marked Pole, impose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect on the Pole until the start of your next turn.

The fragment cannot generate Bearing tokens, complete Bearings for you, or use Break the Four Directions independently.

Compass Strike

Otherwise, it applies to the next Martial Strike that damages the Pole before the end of the turn.

- Approach — Enter the Line: Deal an additional 1d8 Psychic or Force damage. The Pole cannot take Opportunity Attacks against you until the start of your next turn.

You leave the threatened body behind and let the attacker strike the decision you already abandoned.

Failed Save: Its Speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn and it becomes Resonance Marked until the end of your next turn.

Successful Save: Its Speed is reduced by 10 feet for the rest of the turn.

Cultivation Level 18 — Hundred Echoes Kill One Moment

You manifest every combat-ready version of your position across a single decisive interval.

Bonus Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required

You enter the Hundred-Echo State.

Echo Field

At the start and end of each of your turns, record your current space as an Echo Position without counting against your normal limit. These State-created positions last until the State ends.

You can move through hostile creatures’ spaces, ignore nonmagical Difficult Terrain, and do not provoke Opportunity Attacks. You cannot end movement in an occupied space.

One Soul, Many Edges

Once on each of your turns when you use Mind Spike, make a weapon attack with a weapon you are proficient with, or activate a single-target Spirit Awakening technique, choose up to three Echo Positions within 60 feet.

After the triggering effect resolves, choose one creature legal from each selected position. Each chosen creature takes 2d8 Psychic or Force damage. A creature chosen multiple times takes damage only once, but if it is your Pursuit Mark target, it takes 4d8 instead.

This is secondary echo damage, not additional attacks and not additional technique activations.

Moment of the Final Edge

Once during the State, use an Action to choose one creature within 120 feet that you can perceive or that bears your Pursuit Mark. Select up to six Echo Positions that form a legal sequence ending adjacent to or within 30 feet of the target, depending on your chosen final attack.

Move through the sequence by spiritual step, then choose one:

- make one weapon attack with a weapon you are proficient with;
- use Mind Spike with maximum damage on its damage dice on a failed save;
- make one Cultivation Attack dealing 10d10 Psychic, Force, Slashing, or Necrotic damage on a hit.

On a hit or failed save, the target also makes a Charisma saving throw.

Failed Save: Choose two: no Reactions until the end of your next turn; Speed 0 until the start of its next turn; cannot regain Hit Points until the start of its next turn; one active lower-Source-CL movement or concealment effect ends; it is knocked Prone; it is moved 20 feet to a legal space along your echo sequence.

Successful Save: Choose one of those effects until the start of its next turn.

If the target’s Source CL is at least 5 lower than yours and it bears your Pursuit Mark, ordinary non-Secret escape, invisibility, and movement defenses cannot prevent the final approach. Equal or higher authority contests normally.

After the Last Echo

When the State ends, remove every Echo Position and Pursuit Mark you created. You cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn as your body and soul agree on which position survived.

---

Cultivation Level 14 — Pursuit Without Distance

Once your soul has learned a target’s combat rhythm, escape becomes another recorded position.

Pursuit Mark

When you damage a Resonance Marked meaningful hostile creature, you may spend 2 Resonance to convert your Resonance Mark on it into a Pursuit Mark lasting for the scene.

- A Pursuit Mark is a special Resonance Mark.
- You can maintain one Pursuit Mark at a time.
- You know the marked creature’s direction and approximate distance while it remains within 1 mile and is not behind stronger concealment.
- The target can remove the mark by spending an Action and succeeding on a Charisma saving throw, receiving Spiritual Exorcism, or crossing a higher-Source-CL boundary that severs pursuit.

Follow the Vanishing Point

Reaction  
You can use this when  The creature bearing your Pursuit Mark moves at least 15 feet, teleports, enters invisibility, changes form, crosses a portal, or leaves your current line of sight  
Cost: 4 Resonance

Choose one:

- move up to your Speed by spiritual step toward a legal space within 10 feet of its destination;
- move to an Echo Position within 60 feet and use Mind Spike against the target if it is legal from that position;
- if the target teleported or crossed a route, make a Cultivation Check against the movement’s Source Rule. On a success, arrive in a legal space within 10 feet of the destination. On a failure, move up to half your Speed toward the last legal point and learn the route’s authority category.

After arriving, record your space as an Echo Position.

Cut the Retreat

Once per round when the pursued creature leaves one of your Echo Positions or attempts to move away from you, you may consume that Echo Position. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save: Its movement ends after 5 feet and it takes 3d8 Psychic damage.

Successful Save: Its movement distance is reduced by 10 feet.

Soul Splitting — Second Stance

Your soul fragment can maintain one Echo Position of its own. You may use that position as an origin for Strike From the Echo or Three-Step Soul Execution, but doing so destroys the fragment after the technique resolves. Destruction this way does not cause the core Soul Splitting backlash damage.

You resolve three prepared killing positions as one continuous Spirit Awakening technique.

Cultivation Level 6 — Exact Counterweight

You can spend a stored Measure to reduce a matching consequence before it is finalized.

Reaction  
You can use this when  You or a willing creature bearing your Resonance Mark within 30 feet is affected by a hostile activation matching a Measure you hold  
Cost: 2 Resonance and the matching Measure

Choose the corresponding procedure.

Impact Counterweight

Reduce one instance of triggering damage by 3d8 + Wisdom modifier after Resistance and before Temporary Hit Points.

If this reduces the damage to 0, the source takes Psychic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier + Proficiency Bonus and becomes Resonance Marked until the end of your next turn, provided it is a creature within 60 feet that you can perceive or spiritually locate through your mark.

Impact Counterweight does not reduce Hit Point costs, self-inflicted sacrifice, maximum-Hit-Point reduction, Exhaustion, cultivation harm, or damage that expressly cannot be reduced unless you win the relevant authority contest.

Motion Counterweight

Choose one:

- reduce forced movement by up to 20 feet;
- prevent the target from being knocked Prone;
- grant Advantage on the triggering check or save against becoming Grappled or Restrained;
- if the effect imposed Grappled or Restrained without a check or save, make a Cultivation Check against its Source Rule. On a success, suppress that condition until the start of the protected creature's next turn.

If all forced movement is prevented or the protected creature avoids the condition, it may move 5 feet to a legal space without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the source.

Intent Counterweight

If the trigger allows an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, add 1d6 to the roll after seeing the d20 but before the outcome is finalized.

If the trigger imposed an ordinary lower-Source-CL effect without a save, make a Cultivation Check against its Source Rule. On a success, suppress one mental, emotional, spiritual, possession, command, or identity expression until the start of the protected creature's next turn.

If the added die changes a failure into a success or the suppression succeeds, impose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect on the source until the start of your next turn if it is within 60 feet and can be affected by spiritual authority.

No Borrowing from the Same Blow

A Measure gained from a hostile activation becomes available only after that activation and every linked damage packet, movement, condition, and rider have resolved. It cannot pay for Exact Counterweight against the activation that created it.

Reaction

Cost: 4 Resonance or 2 Sorrow Burdens

Choose one mode:

Divide the Pain

You take half the triggering damage, rounded up, and the ally takes the remainder. Your share cannot be reduced, redirected, or converted into healing.

Carry the Echo

The ally rerolls the triggering saving throw and must use the new result. Whether it succeeds or fails, you suffer one lesser emotional echo until the end of your next turn: Frightened, unable to take Reactions, Speed reduced by 10 feet, Disadvantage on your next attack, or another ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.

Hold the Door

Delay an ordinary possession, nightmare, charm, despair, memory-emotion wound, or identity-pressure consequence until the end of the ally’s next turn. During the delay, meaningful exorcism, healing, escape, surrender, anchor destruction, or emotional intervention can change the result. If nothing changes, the consequence occurs.

Transferring a permanent soul wound, complete memory loss, high-authority possession, curse, Secret effect, divine judgment, artifact authority, or tribulation scar requires a Cultivation Check and normally creates a persistent Burden Scar rather than simply removing the effect.

Burden Scar

A Burden Scar is a Hidden Injury of the spirit. It remains until treated through Spiritual Exorcism, a funeral rite, a proper emotional resolution, equal-authority healing, or one Burden Scar treatment procedure in the Normalized Execution Notes. It cannot be farmed for Sorrow Burdens.

Cultivation Level 3 — Taste the Radiance

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature within 60 feet gains or activates qualifying radiance, receives supernatural healing, or becomes Resonance Marked by you while carrying qualifying radiance  
Cost: 1 Resonance

Taste the spiritual structure of the triggering effect.

You learn:

- its broad purpose;
- whether it is healing, warding, cleansing, empowering, oath-bearing, shrine-backed, divine, artifact-based, or another recognizable category;
- whether its Source CL is lower than, equal to, or higher than yours;

Your bonds allow one soul to lend another the strength to remain itself.

Courage Shared

- the target may move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks;
- the target gains +1 to Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws until the start of your next turn;
- you learn one lawful recovery route for the effect you suppressed or transferred.

Cultivation Level 14 — Chain of Devotion

You manifest the living relationship between chosen souls as a battlefield network.

Action  
Cost: 6 Resonance  
Duration: The scene  
Targets: Up to your Proficiency Bonus willing creatures bearing your Vow Mark, including yourself  
Concentration: Required

While at least two linked creatures remain within 60 feet of one another, they form a Devotion Chain.

Each linked creature gains:

- +1 to Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws;
- knowledge of the direction and broad distress state of every other linked creature within 1 mile;
- the ability to communicate one brief emotional impression to the chain once per turn without an action.

Once per round when a linked creature within 60 feet takes damage, another willing linked creature may use its Reaction to take any portion of that damage, up to half, after Resistance and before Temporary Hit Points. The transferred damage retains its type and source and cannot be reduced again by the receiving creature’s Resistance unless a Source Rule expressly allows it.

Once per round when a linked creature fails an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, another linked creature within 60 feet may spend 1 Devotion and use its Reaction to grant a reroll. The target must use the new result.

Chain Anchor

You may externalize the Devotion Chain as a visible Heart-Knot Anchor in an unoccupied space within 30 feet:

- AC: your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 8 × Proficiency Bonus
- Saving Throws: uses your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throw bonuses
- Resistances: Psychic damage
- Source CL: your effective Spirit Awakening CL

While the Anchor exists, the Chain does not require Concentration. Destroying or suppressing it ends the Chain, but does not end the underlying Vow Marks.

A linked creature can leave the Chain at any time without an action. Unwilling creatures cannot be added.

Cultivation Level 6 — Heart’s Rebuke

A hostile act against one of your chosen bonds returns as spiritual pain.

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature within 60 feet damages, charms, frightens, possesses, spiritually manipulates, forcibly moves, or inflicts a Spirit Scar, Soul Wound, defining-memory injury, identity injury, grief effect, despair effect, or another effect expressly labeled a major emotional wound on a Vow-Marked creature  
Cost: 3 Resonance

The triggering creature makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save: It takes 4d8 + Wisdom modifier Psychic damage and suffers one Rebuke until the start of its next turn:

- Do Not Approach: It cannot willingly move closer to the protected creature.
- Feel What You Caused: It has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes.
- The Bond Remembers: It becomes Resonance Marked for the scene.
- Shared Alarm: The protected creature can immediately move up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the triggering creature.

Successful Save: It takes half damage. The protected creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

If you spend 1 Devotion when using Heart’s Rebuke, the protected creature also gains Advantage on the next Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw it makes against the triggering creature before the end of its next turn.

Heart’s Rebuke punishes the witnessed hostile act. It does not establish legal guilt, karmic debt, an oath breach, or permanent hostility.

Cultivation Level 18 — Unbroken Vow

A chosen bond can hold a soul in the world after ordinary fate says it should be gone.

Reaction  
You can use this when  A Vow-Marked creature within 60 feet would die, have its soul severed or removed, be permanently transformed, lose a defining memory, suffer a major identity wound, or have its complete cultivation suppressed  
Cost: 10 Resonance

Choose yourself or another willing Vow-Marked creature within 60 feet as the Vow Bearer. The triggering consequence is delayed until the end of the target’s next turn.

During the delay:

- the target remains alive and conscious at 1 Hit Point if physically possible;
- it cannot be possessed or have its soul displaced by ordinary lower-Source-CL effects;
- the Vow Bearer knows the broad category and source direction of the delayed consequence;
- the Vow Bearer may willingly take one level of Exhaustion and spend up to 3 Devotion to extend the delay by one additional round;
- healing, Spiritual Exorcism, reconstruction, reaching a legal escape destination, accepting a surrender that ends the hostile Source Rule, severing the sustaining Anchor, fulfilling a recovery condition already printed by the source, or another explicitly printed intervention can change or remove the consequence.

At the end of the delay, if the original consequence remains valid, it occurs unless you succeed on the following procedure.

The Bond Refuses

Make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s save DC or Source CL.

Success against ordinary lower-Source-CL authority: Convert death into unconsciousness at 0 Hit Points, soul removal into a Strained Soul Anchor, permanent transformation into a suppressible transformation scar, major memory loss into an inaccessible memory wound, or complete cultivation suppression into suppression of one printed system for the scene.

Success against Restricted or equal authority: Choose one of those conversions, and the target gains a persistent Vow Scar. The Scar imposes no additional numerical penalty by itself, but it is a Spiritual Affliction visible to Soul Gaze and relevant Source Rules. Remove it through the Vow Scar Recovery procedure below.

Higher, Rare, Forbidden, Secret, divine, artifact, tribulation, true-name, conceptual, reincarnation, or campaign-scale authority: On success, suppress one printed expression until the end of the scene and learn the proper reconstruction route. The complete consequence is not erased automatically.

Failure: The delay ends and the original consequence occurs. The Vow Mark remains unless the relationship or soul is destroyed.

Unbroken Bond Field

If you use Unbroken Vow while your Devotion Chain is active, every willing linked creature may contribute one of the following without an action:

- spend 1 Hit Die;
- take Psychic damage equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus, ignoring Resistance;
- spend 1 Cultivation Point from a Path it possesses;
- accept one level of Exhaustion.

For each distinct contributor, gain +1 to The Bond Refuses Cultivation Check, to a maximum of +3.

A contribution is valid only when the contributor is willing, can perceive the preservation attempt, and immediately pays the listed cost. A creature cannot be forced, dominated, contractually compelled, or have the same paid cost refunded before the Cultivation Check. Each creature contributes at most once to one use.

Unbroken Vow preserves through chosen connection. It does not compel affection, prevent a willing departure, create resurrection without a remaining soul, or supersede dedicated Secret Laws of death, karma, fate, time, or conceptual severance.

If it is still at 1 Hit Point at the end of its turn, it drops to 0 Hit Points. The game handles this delay for defeat from damage; resolve soul removal, transformation, memory or identity wounds, and cultivation suppression by hand.

You gain the Vow Mark and Devotion rules above.

When you or a Vow-Marked ally within 30 feet places a Resonance Mark on a hostile creature, you may spend 1 Devotion to grant one marked ally within 30 feet Temporary Hit Points equal to Wisdom modifier + Proficiency Bonus.

A creature can receive these Temporary Hit Points only once per round.

Cultivation Level 14 — Heart Soul Gate

You can share stability without replacing another creature’s feelings or choices.

Heart Attunement

When a willing creature within 30 feet fails a saving throw against Charmed, Frightened, possession, emotional corruption, madness, or dream intrusion, you may use your Reaction and spend 2 Resonance. The creature adds your Wisdom modifier to the saving throw. If the result becomes a success, you take Psychic damage equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus as you absorb the spiritual recoil.

You cannot use Heart Attunement on the same saving throw as another feature that adds your Wisdom modifier.

Heart Restoration

Action  
Range: Touch  
Cost: 5 Resonance

Touch one willing creature and choose one 

- Charmed.
- Frightened.
- Ordinary madness.
- Ordinary emotional corruption.
- Ordinary possession.
- A suppressed identity fracture.
- A lower-Source-CL dream intrusion.

If the effect’s Source CL is lower than yours, end it. If its Source CL is equal or higher, the target immediately repeats its saving throw with Advantage. If it has no repeat save, make a Cultivation Check against its save DC.

On a successful repeat save or Cultivation Check, choose one:

- End the effect if its Source Rule permits ordinary removal.
- Suppress it until the end of the scene.
- Reduce its severity by one stage.
- Stabilize the target so the effect cannot worsen until the next Full Cultivation Session.
- Reveal the effect’s Anchor, true name, contradiction, restitution, confession, or reconstruction requirement.

On failure, suppress one symptom until the start of your next turn and learn whether the effect is lower, equal, or higher authority.

Heart Restoration cannot erase a chosen oath, consensual bond, Soul Anchor, true Heart Demon, tribulation scar, divine judgment, Secret-Law wound, or identity change the target genuinely accepts. It must still provide a useful recovery route when full removal is impossible.

Heart Opening

Bonus Action  
Cost: 4 Resonance  
Duration: The scene

While open, allies of your choice within 10 feet have Advantage on saving throws against Charmed and Frightened. Once per round when such an ally succeeds on an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, it gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier + Proficiency Bonus.

Cultivation Level 3 — Root Soul Gate

Your soul learns the shape of its own body and refuses ordinary displacement from it.

Rooted Identity

Gain proficiency in Athletics or Acrobatics. If already proficient in both, gain proficiency in Medicine or Insight instead.

You have Advantage on saving throws and Cultivation Checks against:

- Forced possession.
- Soul displacement.
- An effect that would exchange, eject, or misidentify your soul and body.
- Forced movement caused by a spirit, psychic effect, or incorporeal creature.

Root Reclamation

Reaction  
You can use this when  You are knocked Prone, moved against your will, Grappled or Restrained by a spirit-affecting effect, or an effect attempts to separate your soul from your body.  
Cost: 1 Resonance

Choose one:

- Stand from Prone without spending movement.
- Reduce forced movement by 10 feet + 5 × floor(Proficiency Bonus ÷ 2); this is 15 feet at PB 2–3, 20 feet at PB 4–5, and 25 feet at PB 6.
- Gain Advantage on the triggering saving throw or Cultivation Check if it has not yet resolved.
- If the effect grants no roll, make a Wisdom saving throw against its save DC. If it has no save DC, use 8 + source Proficiency Bonus + source key ability modifier. On success, prevent an ordinary or lower-Source-CL separation effect. Equal or higher authority follows its printed result or becomes a recoverable soul strain rather than automatic prevention.

Root Reclamation cannot prevent physical movement caused solely by terrain collapse, a mundane vehicle, or an effect too large to be spiritually resisted unless another Source Rule makes identity relevant.

Root Opening

Bonus Action  
Cost: 1 Resonance  
Duration: The scene

While open, your Speed cannot be reduced below 10 feet by ordinary Spiritual Pressure, and standing from Prone costs only 5 feet of movement. When you end your turn in the same space in which you began it, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier + half your Proficiency Bonus.

On success, prevent an ordinary or lower-Source-Cultivation Level separation; equal or higher authority follows its own result or causes recoverable soul strain. This cannot stop movement caused solely by terrain collapse, a mundane vehicle or an effect too large to resist unless another rule makes identity relevant.

Cultivation Level 6 — Sacral Soul Gate

You admit emotional turbulence without allowing it to seize the whole self.

Fluid Affect

You have Advantage on checks made to recognize whether an emotion is your own, externally imposed, inherited from a spirit, or echoing from a memory or location.

When Soul Gaze reveals a creature’s surface emotional state, you may also learn whether that emotion is stable, suppressed, externally amplified, magically imposed, or divided against another emotion.

Sacral Reorientation

Reaction  
You can use this when  You fail a Dexterity, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw.  
Cost: 2 Resonance  
Limit: Once per round

Add your Wisdom modifier to the saving throw, potentially turning failure into success. This can be used after Soulward Response only if the saving throw is still failed, but the same modifier cannot be added twice.

If Sacral Reorientation turns failure into success:

- You become Resonance Marked by yourself until the end of your next turn.
- You may immediately use Soul Gaze on yourself without spending Resonance, learning only the source category, current severity, and likely recovery route of the triggering spiritual disturbance.
- If the triggering effect was Charmed, Frightened, emotional domination, dream intrusion, or ordinary possession, impose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect on its source if that source is within 60 feet and perceptible to you.

Sacral Opening

Bonus Action  
Cost: 2 Resonance  
Duration: The scene

While open, you can move through the space of a creature affected by one of your Resonance Marks as if it were Difficult Terrain, and you have Advantage on saving throws against effects that would force you to act from an imposed emotion. Once per turn after you succeed on such a save, move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Cultivation Level 10 — Collapse the Interval

You make two related points adjacent for one crossing.

Action or Bonus Action  
Range: 120 feet  
Cost: 5 Resonance

Choose yourself or one willing creature you touch, and choose one Near creature, object, Asset, or space within range. Move the traveler to a legal space adjacent to the Near subject by conceptual translation.

- This is not ordinary teleportation, but effects that block teleportation, Space, routes, conceptual movement, or passage can contest it.
- The traveler does not cross the intervening spaces.
- You cannot cross planes, enter an unknown sealed room, bypass a Secret prison automatically, or travel to a subject whose Near relation is being perfectly concealed.
- An unwilling creature cannot be transported.

If used as an Action, you may carry a number of willing creatures adjacent to you up to your Wisdom modifier, minimum one, by paying 2 additional Resonance per additional creature. Every traveler must arrive in a legal adjacent space.

Interval Strike

After you personally use Collapse the Interval, you may make one weapon attack with a weapon you are proficient with or use Mind Spike against one creature within legal range of your destination. This does not require an additional Action, but costs 2 Resonance.

You can use Interval Strike once per turn. It cannot be combined with another feature that grants an attack as part of the same movement unless one of them expressly allows the combination.

Nearer Than Falling

When you or a Near creature begins falling, you may use your Reaction and spend 2 Resonance. Declare the nearest legal surface within 120 feet Near for the fall and translate the falling creature to a legal space on or adjacent to it. A sealed or hostile surface can contest.

Cultivation Level 14 — Painless Martyr

Reaction  
You can use this when  An ally within 30 feet takes damage, fails an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, or would gain a Mercy Scar, Nightmare Scar, spiritual contamination, possession effect, memory wound, or identity wound  
Cost: 5 Resonance

Choose one result.

Divide the Blow

You take half the triggering damage, rounded down, and the ally takes the remainder. Damage type and bypass properties are preserved. Damage transferred to you this way cannot be reduced below your Proficiency Bonus unless the triggering damage was already lower.

Carry the Failure

The ally rerolls the triggering saving throw and must use the new result. You gain 1 Mercy Scar. If the reroll succeeds, the hostile source becomes Resonance Marked by you.

Catch the Wound

Delay one ordinary possession, contamination, memory wound, identity wound, or permanent-injury consequence until the end of your next turn. You immediately gain 1 Mercy Scar. During the delay, the ally or another creature can heal, escape, exorcise, surrender, sever an Anchor, or perform another meaningful intervention.

If the source is equal or higher authority, make a Cultivation Check. On failure, you may still delay one symptom until the start of the ally’s next turn, but not the complete consequence.

Martyr’s Limit

You cannot use Painless Martyr if doing so would force you above your Mercy Scar maximum unless you rupture a Scar first. If the feature would reduce you to 0 Hit Points, it still resolves; you fall unconscious afterward.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.miko.feature.ka.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 — Kami Descent

A willing greater kami or perfected shrine office descends into your cultivated spirit. This is negotiated hosting, not uncontrolled possession.

Bonus Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance and 1 Offering  
Duration: The scene  
Concentration: No

Choose one Descent Aspect appropriate to your shrine or covenant. You gain the universal benefits and the chosen Aspect.

Universal Benefits

- +2 AC.
- Choose one Descent Movement when the covenant is recorded: Heavenly Flight (Fly 60 feet and hover), Sacred Ascent (Climb 60 feet, including ceilings), River Passage (Swim 60 feet and breathe air and water), or Processional Step (walking Speed becomes 60 feet and you ignore nonmagical Difficult Terrain and liquid surfaces). Kami Descent grants the recorded movement.
- Advantage on saving throws against possession, curses, Frightened, Charmed, and spiritual contamination.
- Ordinary and lower-Source-CL spirits recognize the manifest kami authority and cannot disguise their broad Nature from your Spiritual Sense.
- Your Brief Purification and Minor Kami Favors can originate from you, your Soul Fragment, your Shrine Anchor, or your Manifest Messenger, but each activation still uses only one origin.

Descent of Purity

Once per turn when you spend Resonance on a Miko or Spirit Awakening feature, one willing creature affected by that feature regains Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier or repeats one save against possession, curse, poison, disease, Frightened, or spiritual contamination.

Once during the Descent, use Kami Purification as an Action without additional Resonance or Offering cost. Choose up to your Proficiency Bonus willing creatures within 60 feet. Each chosen creature selects one benefit: end one ordinary Charmed or Frightened condition; repeat one saving throw against possession, curse, dream intrusion, memory alteration, Spiritual Affliction, or Heart Demon influence with Advantage; return its displaced soul to its body if both are within 60 feet and no equal-or-higher-authority seal prevents return; or suppress one equal-or-higher-Source-CL Spiritual Affliction until the end of the scene if you succeed on a Cultivation Check against its save DC. Kami Purification grants no hostile damage, soul destruction, planar expulsion, or Anchor damage.

Descent of Protection

You and allies within 20 feet gain Resistance to Psychic and Necrotic damage. Once per round when an ally in that aura takes damage, use your Reaction and spend 1 Resonance to reduce the damage by 2d10 + Wisdom modifier.

Once during the Descent, create Sacred Ground without an Offering or Resonance cost. It lasts only until the Descent ends and uses no destructible Anchor; it is centered on you and moves with you.

Descent of Revelation

Your Spiritual Sense becomes 120 feet and can perceive through ordinary walls up to 5 feet thick for the limited purpose of detecting spirits, souls, possession, curses, dream intrusion, spiritual Assets, and sacred or profane Anchors. Total cover still prevents ordinary targeting.

Once during the Descent, ask the descending kami three questions concerning the current site, spiritual conflict, local history, or an entity the kami can perceive. The kami answers truthfully according to its knowledge and Nature.

Descent of Renewal

At the start of each of your turns, one willing creature you can perceive within 30 feet regains Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier if it has at least 1 Hit Point.

Once during the Descent, touch one creature and restore 8d8 + Wisdom modifier Hit Points, end one ordinary poison or disease, and suppress one curse, possession, Heart Demon, or spiritual contamination for the scene. Equal or higher authority requires a Cultivation Check.

Reciprocity and Taboo

When Kami Descent ends, the kami withdraws. If you upheld its Nature and Taboo, no automatic Exhaustion is gained.

If you knowingly violate the recorded Taboo during the Descent, apply the recorded Taboo Consequence immediately: one of the four consequences below must have been selected when the Shrine Covenant was created.

- Gain 1 level of Exhaustion.
- Your Soul Anchor becomes Strained until you complete the recorded Restitution.
- Lose access to one recorded Minor Kami Favor until you complete the recorded Restitution.
- Your Shrine Anchor and Manifest Messenger become unavailable until you complete the recorded Restitution.

The covenant also records one Restitution from the Procedure Addendum. The consequence cannot be changed after the breach and the GM or AI does not invent a harsher replacement during resolution.

A kami cannot use Descent to seize control of the character without a separate hostile possession procedure and saving throw. You remain the acting character.

Domain Integration

If Domain Manifestation is active when you use Kami Descent, your Domain becomes recognized sacred territory for the duration. Sacred Ground effects you create inside it use the Domain’s boundary if smaller, and willing spirits inside can communicate through spiritual impression even without a shared language.

Cultivation Level 10 — Borrowed Reflection

You can draw a temporary second self out of a reflective surface.

Bonus Action  
Range: 30 feet  
Cost: 4 Resonance  
Duration: 1 minute  
Requirement: A valid reflection within range

Create one Reflection Double in an unoccupied space adjacent to the chosen surface. You can maintain only one Reflection Double at a time.

The Reflection Double is a Medium Cultivation Asset:

- AC: your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 4 × Proficiency Bonus
- Saving Throws: uses your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throw bonuses
- Immunities: Poisoned, Disease, ordinary suffocation
- Resistances: Psychic damage
- Speed: 30 feet; it cannot move more than 60 feet from you or a valid reflection
- Source CL: your effective Spirit Awakening CL

It has no independent turn, cannot flank, hold items, make weapon attacks, provide Help, maintain Concentration, or use your Subpath features independently.

On your turn, it can move up to its Speed when you move or as part of a Bonus Action you use to direct it.

While it exists:

- You may originate Mind Spike, Soul Gaze, a Resonance Mark, or another single-target Spirit Awakening technique from your space or the Double’s space.

- You still pay all costs and use your own action economy.

Exchange With the Image

Once on each of your turns, when you use a Spirit Awakening technique from the Double’s space, you may spend 1 Resonance to exchange spaces with it immediately before or after the technique resolves. This movement is teleportation and fails across an effect that blocks teleportation or reflected passage.

Break the Double

When the Double is reduced to 0 Hit Points, every creature within 5 feet of it makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save: The creature takes 2d8 Psychic damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Successful Save: It takes half damage.

You may dismiss the Double without this burst.

Cultivation Level 18 — World Behind the Glass

You unfold the spiritual territory that every reflection implies.

Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Duration: The scene  
Requirement: At least one valid reflection within 60 feet

Create a 30-foot-radius Mirror Domain centered on you, your Reflection Double, or a reflective surface within 60 feet. The center remains fixed unless it is your Double; if centered on the Double, the field moves with it.

The Domain is visibly transformed by silver water, reversed shadows, glass pathways, doubled voices, and reflections that move before their subjects.

While it persists:

- Every creature and object in the Domain has a valid reflection for your features.
- You may originate Spirit Awakening techniques from any unbroken reflective surface in the Domain.
- Once per round when a traced hostile creature attacks you or an ally in the Domain, you may impose Disadvantage without spending your Reaction. Resolve this before the roll.
- A traced enemy cannot become Hidden from you through ordinary darkness, invisibility, smoke, disguise, or mundane cover that leaves any reflection exposed.
- When a traced creature fails an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw against you, you may move it up to 10 feet to an unoccupied reflected space it could physically occupy. This is forced spiritual displacement, not teleportation.

The Domain requires Concentration. If every reflective surface in it is destroyed, completely obscured, or suppressed, the Domain ends.

Reflection Cell

Once during the activation, when a traced creature in the Domain fails a Wisdom or Charisma saving throw against one of your Spirit Awakening features, you may spend 6 Resonance to draw it into a Reflection Cell.

The target disappears into a mirrored copy of the Domain until the end of its next turn. While inside:

- it is Incapacitated and has total cover from creatures outside the Cell;
- it can perceive distorted reflections of the real Domain;
- at the end of its turn, it repeats the Charisma saving throw;
- on a success, it returns to its former space or the nearest unoccupied space;
- on a failure, it remains until the end of its following turn, then returns automatically unless a stronger Source Rule extends the imprisonment.

An ordinary creature whose Source CL is at least 5 lower than yours can remain imprisoned for the scene after two failed saves if the Mirror Domain’s center becomes a destructible Mirror Gate Anchor:

- AC: your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 8 × Proficiency Bonus
- Resistances: Psychic damage
- Source CL: your effective Spirit Awakening CL

Destroying or suppressing the Anchor immediately releases every imprisoned creature.

Equal- or higher-Source-CL targets, major enemies, Secret Law practitioners, divine beings, artifact-bound creatures, and creatures protected by explicit anti-banishment authority cannot be imprisoned for the scene through this feature alone. They use the repeated-save procedure.

World Behind the Glass does not create a permanent plane, duplicate souls, or replace true mirror, space, imprisonment, or conceptual authority from another Source Rule.

Cultivation Level 10 — Raise Specter

You construct a temporary manifestation from corpse memory or a Soul Fragment. It is a Spirit Cultivation Asset, not the creature restored and not a full companion.

Action  
Cost: 5 Resonance and 1 Soul Fragment  
Duration: The scene, or 1 hour outside conflict  
Range: Create the specter in an unoccupied space within 30 feet

Choose Warden Specter or Predatory Specter when created.

Specter Profile

- Size: Medium
- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 6 × Proficiency Bonus
- Speed: Fly 40 feet; hover
- Saving Throws: Uses your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throw bonuses
- Resistances: Psychic and Necrotic
- Immunities: Poison, Disease, Poisoned, Prone, Grappled, Restrained, and ordinary bodily effects
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
- Action economy: No independent turn. At the end of each of your turns, it moves up to its Speed. As a Bonus Action, direct one Specter Expression.

Warden Specter Expressions

- Guard the Threshold: One ally within 10 feet of the specter gains Half Cover and Advantage on its next saving throw against possession or soul displacement before the start of your next turn.
- Seize Intruder: One spirit, incorporeal undead, possessed creature, or Resonance Marked creature within 10 feet makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, its Speed becomes 0 and it cannot possess another creature until the start of your next turn.
- Testify: The specter reproduces one memory, route, image, or statement contained in the spent fragment. Protected information remains limited to what the fragment held.

Predatory Specter Expressions

- Spectral Strike: Make a Cultivation Attack against a creature within 5 feet. On a hit, deal 2d10 + Wisdom modifier Necrotic or Psychic damage.
- Harrier of the Living: One creature within 10 feet cannot take Reactions and has Disadvantage on the next death saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn. This cannot target an ally unless the ally willingly accepts the risk.
- Drink Fear: One Frightened or Resonance Marked creature within 10 feet makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it takes 2d8 Psychic damage and you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

Destruction

If the specter is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it disperses. If created from a Coerced fragment, you take Psychic damage equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus as the custody breaks.

The source’s complete soul is not harmed merely because the specter is destroyed. A manifestation cannot use the source creature’s attacks, spell list, Legendary actions, equipment, full statistics, or identity-defining features.

Soul Splitting Expression — Twin Custody

While Soul Splitting is active, the Soul Fragment may serve as the origin of a Specter Expression. The specter still receives only one expression per Bonus Action and gains no independent action.

Cultivation Level 18 — Concept of the Missing Footstep

You unfold a domain in which movement and witness no longer possess a reliable relationship.

Bonus Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Area: 40-foot-radius aura centered on you  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required

The area becomes an Unwritten Procession.

Unrecorded Movement

When you move at least 5 feet, choose any number of hostile creatures in the aura. Each chosen creature makes a Wisdom saving throw once per turn.

Failed Save: Until you next deal damage, touch it, or end your turn without cover or concealment, you are unnoticed by that creature. Your movement does not provoke from it, and it cannot communicate your current route.

Successful Save: It can perceive you, but cannot take Opportunity Attacks against you during that movement.

Cut Action From Witness

Once on each of your turns after you damage a creature, use Mind Spike, interact with an object, or cross a ward inside the aura, choose one Witness that failed a save against the Domain this round. Choose one:

- it remembers the result but not your identity as the source;
- it remembers your involvement but not the route or method;
- it cannot communicate the event until the start of your next turn;
- it gains an Unwritten Trace and cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.

This cannot erase the event, undo damage, manufacture an innocent culprit, defeat an explicit true-name oath, or alter a permanent record already created by higher authority.

Empty Space Assassination

Once during the activation, choose one creature in the aura that currently does not notice you. Move up to your Speed by spiritual step and make one of the following against it:

- one weapon attack with a weapon you are proficient with;
- Mind Spike with maximum damage on its damage dice if it fails the save;
- one single-target Spirit Awakening technique of Cultivation Level 10 or lower that normally costs no more than 5 Resonance, paying its normal cost.

If the attack hits or the target fails its save, add 6d8 Psychic damage and it loses Reactions until the end of your next turn. If it succeeds, it takes half the bonus damage and immediately notices you.

This is one technique resolution and cannot recursively trigger another execution, assassination, or extra-action feature.

The World Notices the Wound

At the end of the activation, every creature affected by Cut Action From Witness receives a final Wisdom saving throw. On a success, it reconstructs the missing attribution from context. On a failure, the specific gaps remain for 24 hours, though evidence, testimony, Spiritual Exorcism, Echo Scribe records, mirror confession, perfect witness authority, or investigation can restore the truth.

This capstone does not remove you from history, records, names, karmic consequences, or the memories of creatures outside the Domain.

You temporarily sever the link between a target’s perception and its ability to identify you as the subject of that perception.

Choose one creature that can perceive you or bears your Unwritten Trace. It makes a Wisdom saving throw.

While you are Unwritten to it:

- it cannot voluntarily target you with attacks or single-target techniques;
- it cannot take Opportunity Attacks against you;
- it cannot accurately communicate your current location;
- it treats spaces you occupy as apparently empty until physical contact, collision, or an effect requiring an occupied space reveals the obstruction;

A creature immune to Charmed is not automatically immune; this is perception-attribution authority. A creature without a mind or sense of subjecthood may be unaffected, while a hive mind, ward network, or spirit collective may use its controlling Source Rule to contest.

An ally can use an Action to point you out through touch, a shared sense, a linked spirit, a formation signal, or direct guidance. The target then repeats the save with Advantage. Cultivation Level 10 — Hourglass Mark

You place a target inside the delay between intention and result.

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 5 Resonance  
Duration: Up to 1 minute

Choose one creature you can perceive. It makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save: The creature gains your Hourglass Mark. This is a special Resonance Mark. At the end of each of its turns, it repeats the save, ending the mark on a success.

Successful Save: It suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect until the start of your next turn.

You can maintain only one Hourglass Mark. Because it is one of your Resonance Marks, applying it replaces another Resonance Mark you placed on that creature, and applying an ordinary Resonance Mark to that creature replaces the Hourglass Mark unless this feature expressly says otherwise. Creating a new Hourglass Mark ends the previous one.

While the mark lasts, once per round when the marked creature begins one of the following activities, you may spend 1 Resonance and gain 1 Time Debt to apply the corresponding delay.

Delayed Movement

When it begins voluntary movement, reduce the distance available to that movement by 15 feet, minimum 0. If this prevents it from reaching a required destination, an action requiring that arrival must be redirected to another legal target or fails under its normal rules.

Delayed Strike

When it makes an attack roll, subtract 1d6 from the roll. Decide after seeing the d20 but before the outcome is finalized.

Delayed Technique

When it forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw against a technique, choose one target. That target adds 1d6 to its saving throw. This cannot modify an environmental or passive save whose source is no longer the marked creature.

Delayed Reaction

When it attempts a Reaction, the Reaction occurs only after the triggering action, movement, or technique fully resolves. If the trigger is no longer valid at that time, the Reaction does not occur and any resource committed specifically to that Reaction is not spent.

You cannot apply more than one Hourglass delay to the same roll, movement, technique, or Reaction.

Break the Glass

The marked creature or a creature adjacent to it can use an Action to strike, shatter, dispel, exorcise, or spiritually realign the mark.

The acting creature makes one of the following checks against your Cultivation Save DC:

- Intelligence (Arcana);
- Wisdom (Insight);
- Dexterity (Sleight of Hand);
- a Cultivation Check using an appropriate Source Rule.

On a success, the Hourglass Mark ends. Time, Fate, Spirit, Clock, Sound, anti-curse, and suitable conceptual severance effects can qualify.

Your soul recognizes the pressure of a moment immediately before the body understands it.

Before the Bell

Echo of the Chosen Step

Bonus Action

Action

Kitsune True Form

Bonus Action

EARTH_BASE_SPENDING_A_BURDEN_MARK.player_text:
Spending a Burden Mark

Once per round, when a marked creature or object you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Burden Mark without using an Action. Choose one Earth Response appropriate to the trigger.
Anchor Step
Trigger: The marked target begins movement while touching a surface, including walking, climbing, burrowing, jumping, forced movement, or standing from Prone.
Reduce one of the target’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn. At CL 11 (Cultivation Level), this reduction becomes 20 feet.
This cannot reduce a Speed below 0.
If the movement is forced movement, reduce the forced movement distance by the same amount.
Drag Down
Trigger: The marked target willingly moves at least 5 feet, jumps, climbs, flies upward while within 10 feet of a solid surface, or attempts to stand from Prone.
The target makes a Strength saving throw.
Failed Save: The target falls Prone, or if already Prone, its Speed becomes 0 until the end of the current turn.
Successful Save: Reduce the target’s Speed by 5 feet until the end of the current turn.
A creature flying high in open air is affected only if it is within 10 feet of a solid surface, unless a talent says otherwise.
Bear the Blow
Trigger: The marked target deals damage to you, an ally, an object, or a Foundation Space while the damaged target is touching one of your Foundation Spaces or is within 5 feet of you.
Reduce the damage by:
1d8 + your Earth key ability modifier
At CL 5, this becomes 2d8 + modifier; at CL 11, 3d8 + modifier; at CL 17, 4d8 + modifier.
Shift the Load
Trigger: The marked target hits a creature with an attack roll while both are touching the ground or a legal Earth surface.
Before damage is rolled, choose one willing creature within 10 feet of the damaged creature, including yourself.
The chosen creature gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Earth key ability modifier, minimum 1.
If the chosen creature is touching one of your Foundation Spaces, double the Temporary HP.
Raise the Ridge
Trigger: The marked target makes a ranged attack roll, casts a spell, uses a sphere talent, or creates a harmful line or area effect while touching a surface within 60 feet of you.
Raise a low ridge, berm, stone lip, packed-earth mound, or similar obstruction in one unoccupied 5-foot space touching the marked target or the triggering line of effect.
The ridge lasts until the start of your next turn. It grants Half Cover against one attack or effect that crosses through its space, then crumbles.
Raise the Ridge does not block movement unless a talent says otherwise.
Settle the Impact
Trigger: The marked target would push, pull, knock Prone, shove, move, teleport, or otherwise displace another creature or object.
Reduce the displacement by 10 feet. At CL 11, reduce it by 20 feet.
If this reduces the displacement to 0, the displaced creature or object may immediately move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the marked target.
Settle the Impact does not prevent planar travel or teleportation unless the distance is reduced to 0 and the effect is not a Domain, Secret Inheritance, artifact, or story-scale effect.

Refraction Responses
You spend a Faultline Mark to react to an event involving something marked.
A Faultline Mark is the mark you spend for a Refraction Response. When a marked creature, object, attack line, or Glass Surface is involved in an event below, you may spend the mark to use a response you know.

Turn the Angle
Use this when a marked creature hits you or an ally within 5 feet of one of your tempered Glass Surfaces.
Reduce the triggering damage by 1d8 + your Proficiency Bonus.
At CL 5 (Cultivation Level), reduce it by 2d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 11, reduce it by 3d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 17, reduce it by 4d8 + your Proficiency Bonus.
If this reduces the damage to 0, the attacker cannot make Opportunity Attacks until the start of its next turn.
Visible Crack
Use this when a marked creature attempts to Hide, become Invisible, benefit from Cover, or conceal the origin of an attack or technique.
Until the start of your next turn, you and allies who can see one of your Glass Surfaces know the marked creature’s space, even if the creature is Invisible or hidden.
This does not reveal a creature through Total Cover unless the Glass Surface also has line of sight to the creature.
Bitter Edge
Use this when a marked creature willingly moves 5 feet or more.
The creature takes Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of the current turn.
At CL 11+, you may also make the first square of movement through your adjacent space or your Glass Surface count as difficult terrain.
Shatter Warning
Use this when a marked creature makes an attack roll through or against one of your Glass Surfaces.
Impose a -2 penalty on the triggering attack roll.
If the attack misses, the marked creature takes Piercing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Refracted Step
Use this when you spend a Faultline Mark on a creature within 5 feet of you or your tempered Glass Surface.
Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the marked creature.
At CL 5, move 10 feet. At CL 11, move 15 feet. At CL 17, move 20 feet.
Break the Line
Use this when a marked object, barrier, weapon, shield, door, or Glass Surface takes damage.
Add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage dealt to that object or surface.
If the object is reduced to 0 HP, choose one creature within 5 feet of it. That creature takes Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

Cultivation Level 3 — Speak with the Dead

You can awaken corpse memory or lingering residue without importing a spell’s fixed assumptions.

Ritual: 1 minute  
Range: Touch  
Cost: 1 Resonance

Choose a corpse with an intact head, chest, or other body part that retains a memory-bearing organ or a funerary object linked to the deceased, funerary object, grave marker, severed body part containing meaningful residue, or location where a creature died within the last year.

Ask up to 1 + half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down, questions. The response comes through voice, gesture, corpse movement, remembered sensation, nearby shadows, written condensation, or another appropriate medium.

What the Dead Know

The residue can answer only from information the creature knew, perceived, believed, or experienced before death. It may be confused, biased, incomplete, or emotionally distorted. It does not know what occurred after death unless the lingering spirit remained present.

Resistance and Protection

The corpse or residue can resist if:

- The creature was hostile to you.
- Its funeral rites prohibit questioning.
- Its soul or memory is sealed.
- Another authority claims custody.
- It died under Secret, divine, artifact, or higher-Source-CL concealment.

Make a Cultivation Check against the protecting effect or the creature’s Charisma save bonus converted into a DC of 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Charisma modifier. On failure, you learn whether the resistance is unwillingness, ignorance, damage, concealment, or higher custody.

Repeat Questioning

Once you use Speak with the Dead on a given residue, you cannot question the same residue again until you learn materially new information, repair it, obtain consent, or a new scene begins. Repetition cannot force a different answer through dice fishing.

Funerary Reading

Gain proficiency in Medicine or Religion. If already proficient in both, gain proficiency in Investigation or Insight instead.

tianxia.subpath.body.bone_monarch.featur.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Bone Guard Manifestation

Action  
Range: An unoccupied space within 30 feet  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 5 Stamina

Manifest one Bone Guard. You may maintain only one at a time.

Bone Guard Statistics

- Size: Medium
- AC: 14 + Proficiency Bonus
- Hit Points: 5 x your CL
- Speed: 30 feet
- Saving Throws: Uses your saving-throw modifiers
- Immunities: Poison damage, Poisoned
- Cultivation Level: Your CL

Bone Strike

Melee Cultivation Attack: Uses your Cultivation Attack Modifier; reach 5 feet; hit 2d8 + Constitution modifier Piercing or Bludgeoning damage.

Guard the Sovereign

Reaction: When you or an ally within 5 feet of the Bone Guard is targeted by an attack, impose Disadvantage on that attack roll.

The Bone Guard acts immediately after your turn. As a Bonus Action, command it to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Move, or Guard one creature or doorway. Without a command, it takes Dodge and remains within 30 feet of you if possible.

It disappears at 0 Hit Points, when the duration ends, or when you create another.

Normalized Procedure — Bone Guard Manifestation
- The Bone Guard is a manifested Body Asset, not a Complete Soul, Companion, independent character, corpse, or harvestable supply of permanent bone. Creating another causes the existing Guard to disappear.
- It occupies a Medium space. It has no ability scores or proficiencies beyond what its printed statistics require. “Uses your saving-throw modifiers” means use the numerical modifier shown on your character record for the called save; it gains no separate save proficiency.
- The Guard can move normally during its turn. When you command Attack, it may move and make one Bone Strike. Dash, Disengage, Dodge, and Help use the corresponding action and allow ordinary movement. Move lets it move up to its Speed and take no action. Guard lets it move and prepare Guard the Sovereign.
- Issuing the command costs your Bonus Action. The source prints no command distance, so no additional distance limit is imposed while you and the Guard are on the same plane and no effect blocks your direct cultivation control.
- Without a command, it takes Dodge and, if possible, uses movement to remain within 30 feet of you. It does not independently choose attacks or tactics.
- Guard the Sovereign is the Bone Guard's Reaction, usable once per round. Declare after a legal protected creature is targeted but before the attack roll. The Guard must be within 5 feet of that creature at that moment.
- Bone Strike is a cultivation attack made by the Guard using your Cultivation Attack Modifier. The Guard is the attack's origin, but you remain the controlling Source Rule for Source CL and feature attribution. It cannot deliver your personal hit riders unless a feature expressly permits it.
- Ordinary creature healing does not restore the Guard unless the healing rule can target a Body Asset. At 0 Hit Points it disappears with no transferable remains, materials, or injury to you.

tianxia.path.spirit_awakening.feature.so.player_text:
Soul Anchors

Every Spirit Awakener has a Soul Anchor under the universal Soul Anchor rules. It describes what keeps the awakened self coherent: a true name, vow, ancestor, grief, dream, mask, mirror, companion spirit, shrine, debt, lost home, forbidden memory, heart demon, unfinished death, or another defining spiritual root.

At Cultivation Level 1, record:

- the Anchor’s name or description;
- whether it is primarily internal, relational, locational, embodied, object-linked, or vow-linked;
- one way the cultivator normally communes with it during a Full Cultivation Session;
- any separate physical vessel, relationship, or location that represents it.

These entries describe the Anchor. They do not create a destructible object, Companion, Cultivation Asset, immunity, weakness, or additional ability unless another Source Rule says so.

Path interactions:

- Your Soul Anchor is a legal focus for Spirit Awakening techniques when a Source Rule permits a spiritual focus.
- A Soul Anchor is not automatically a physical object and cannot be attacked unless a Source Rule gives it an external manifestation or Anchor profile.
- A Strained Soul Anchor does not erase your Path features, but it can prevent an expressly printed Anchor Invocation and can affect techniques that explicitly depend on it.
- Ordinary damage cannot destroy a Soul Anchor.
- Severing, rewriting, consuming, or permanently replacing a Soul Anchor requires an explicit high-authority Source Rule and an explicit recovery or reconstruction procedure.
- Realm Suppression does not remove the existence of a Soul Anchor, though it can suppress higher-CL expressions that depend on it.

A Spirit Companion, ancestor, shrine, object, relationship, or vow used as a Soul Anchor is not automatically a full Companion, Cultivation Asset, or destructible Spiritual Anchor. Those statuses require separate rules.

---

Spirit Awakening Subpaths

At Cultivation Level 3, choose one Spirit Awakening Subpath for which you have legal access. You gain its features at Cultivation Level 3, Cultivation Level 6, Cultivation Level 10, Cultivation Level 14, and Cultivation Level 18.

| Classification | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Open Tradition | Teachable through a recognized school, shrine, profession, community, military office, or public scripture. Open access does not imply low power or common practitioners. |
| Restricted Lineage or Scripture | Requires a hidden teacher, guarded manual, shrine, sect, spirit pact, haunted location, initiation, profession, or controlled institution. |
| Rare Inheritance | Comes from bloodline, reincarnated memory, spirit ancestry, relic fusion, mutation, possession survived and integrated, divine scar, or singular transmission. |
| Forbidden Method or Variant | Uses condemned, coercive, predatory, destabilizing, politically prohibited, or spiritually hazardous practices. Forbidden is not automatically Daemonic. |
| Secret Law | Direct law-level authority requiring explicit discovery and its printed initiation price. |
| Daemonic | A mechanical tag only when a Source Rule interacts with Corruption, daemonic energy, purification, or anti-daemonic rules. Social accusation does not create this tag. |

A character normally has one Subpath progression. A future parent or Variant lineage uses its printed replacement procedure rather than granting a second simultaneous progression.

A Subpath does not grant general access to a thematically similar Sphere. A Dreamweaver does not automatically learn Dreams; a Mirror Speaker does not automatically learn Illusion or Space; an Ancestral Channeler does not automatically learn Spirit Companions or Death. Only an explicit Source Rule grants a Sphere or talent.

tianxia.path.spirit_awakening.feature.do.player_text:
CL15 — Domain Manifestation

Use a bonus action.
Cost: 6 Resonance 
Area: 30-foot aura centered on you 
Duration: The scene 
Concentration: No 
Domain Type: Personal Domain

Manifest the spiritual truth seeded by your Soul Anchor and refined through your Subpath. Record its sensory expression when you gain this feature. That description grants no additional effect.

The Domain moves with you and ends when you are Incapacitated, willingly end it, leave the scene, become unable to manifest Path features, or a Source Rule suppresses or breaks it.

A creature is affected while inside the aura. Entering the aura does not itself trigger a saving throw unless a Source Rule says so.

Anchored Allies

Allies of your choice in the Domain have Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against:

- Charmed and Frightened;
- possession and coercive Hosting;
- dream intrusion;
- memory alteration;
- emotional domination;
- soul displacement.

You may revise which willing creatures count as allies at the start of your turn without an action. You cannot designate an unwilling hostile creature as an ally merely to bypass its protection or Bond terms.

Unfading Marks

Your Resonance Marks on creatures in the Domain do not expire from duration. A mark ends normally when the creature leaves the Domain, the Domain ends, or another effect removes it.

Domain Pressure

Once on each of your turns, when a creature in the Domain fails a saving throw against one of your Spirit Awakening Path or Subpath features, impose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect on it without additional cost.

This can occur only once during the turn, regardless of the number of failed saves, targets, echoes, or origins created by the activation.

Revealed Spirits

Within the Domain, Spiritual Sense detects ordinary invisible spirits, possession links, Hosted entities, projected souls, Soul Fragments, and lower-Source-CL spiritual disguises without a check. Equal- or higher-authority concealment remains contested.

Subpath Domain Expression

A Subpath may grant an additional Domain expression. That expression modifies this one Domain; it does not create a second Domain, second aura, second turn, or additional Concentration slot unless it explicitly says otherwise.

Domain Collision

Compatible Domains coexist. When two Domain expressions impose contradictory laws upon the same target, space, Bond, route, or effect, compare Source CL. Equal Source CL uses a Cultivation Check contest. Losing suppresses only the contradictory expression, not the entire Domain, unless a Source Rule expressly says the whole Domain collapses.

A Domain is not automatically a Spiritual Anchor, prison, anti-teleport field, sanctuary, spirit court, Companion command zone, or law over every soul inside it.

At CL20, the Domain’s radius becomes 60 feet and its activation cost becomes 4 Resonance.

---
